questions.explain: Key: C. First write the source code (II), then compile it into object code (I), then execute it to test (III). You cannot compile code that has not been written.

questions.stem: Machine language is categorized as a
questions.explain: Key: A. Machine language (binary) is the first generation. Assembly is second, high-level languages such as Pascal are third, and languages such as SQL are fourth.

questions.stem:
Program testing can be described as
I. checking that all documentation is included in the program
II. executing the program manually with input values to see the results
III. running the program using sample data to identify errors in the program
questions.explain: Key: C. Testing means running the program, either by hand (a dry run, II) or on the computer with test data (III), to find errors. Checking the documentation (I) is not testing the program.

questions.stem: Extracting information from a database can be achieved through the use of
questions.explain: Key: C. Queries extract the records that match criteria. Reports present data that has already been selected, and files and objects are general terms.

questions.stem: A single row of data in a database is called a
questions.explain: Key: A. A row is a record (all the data about one item). A field is a column, and a table or file holds many records.

questions.stem: $A$3 is an example of what type of addressing mechanism?
questions.explain: Key: D. The dollar signs fix both the column and the row, so $A$3 is an absolute address that does not change when copied. A3 without dollar signs would be relative. ("Red addressing" is printed as it appears in the paper.)

questions.stem:
Item 49 refers to the following spreadsheet.
ABCDEFG
1
217
335
445
539
6
7
To add the values 17, 35, 45 and 39 in the spreadsheet table above, which function should be placed in cell B6?
questions.explain: Key: A. =SUM(B2:B5) adds the four values. B includes B6 itself (a circular reference), ADD is not a function, and COUNT counts cells instead of adding.

questions.stem: Which of the following actions is required for creating a chart in a spreadsheet?
questions.explain: Key: C. You must select the data the chart will show. Printing, paper size and orientation are page-setup tasks.

questions.stem: The default alignment for numbers in spreadsheet is
questions.explain: Key: B. Numbers are right-aligned by default; text is left-aligned.

questions.stem:
Item 52 refers to the following spreadsheet.
BCDE
1
2First NameSurnameMark 1Bonus Points
3KingsleyClarke69No
4JohnHenry69Yes
5ZaraSmith71Yes
6SeanSmith91No
The spreadsheet has been sorted by a primary field and then a secondary field. What are the primary and secondary fields respectively?
questions.explain: Key: A. Surnames are in A–Z order (Clarke, Henry, Smith, Smith), and the two Smiths are then ordered by Mark 1 (71, 91). First names (B) and bonus points (D) are not in order. Note that C also happens to fit this data (Mark 1 ascending, then No before Yes for the two 69s), so the item is ambiguous; A is the intended answer.

questions.stem:
Item 53 refers to the following spreadsheet.
ABCD
1
2VAT15%
3
4ItemsCost PriceVATTotal
5Washer4300
6Dryer1500
7Stove2750
What formula should be inserted into C5 to calculate the VAT for the washer?
questions.explain: Key: B. B5 is the cost price and $B$2 is the VAT rate, fixed with $ signs so the formula can be copied down for the dryer and stove. 5B is not a valid cell address, and D divides by 100 even though 15% is already stored as 0.15 (and B2 would shift when copied).

questions.stem: Which of the following features allows the user to insert individual names in a primary document?
questions.explain: Key: C. Mail merge inserts each person's details from a data source into the primary document. Headers and footers repeat the same text on every page.

questions.stem: A website consists of a set of web pages that are linked together with
questions.explain: Key: A. Hyperlinks connect the pages of a website. HTML is the language pages are written in, HTTP is the transfer protocol, and Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology.

questions.stem: In order to perform a block operation in a word processing application; the required text must first be
questions.explain: Key: D. Text must be selected (highlighted) before any block operation such as cut, copy, move or format can be applied to it.

questions.stem: I need to search a 50-page document for the acronym IT and insert the words 'Information Technology' in its place. Which of the following is the MOST efficient method for accomplishing this task?
options: Insert key found on the keyboard
Scan the document and quickly make the necessary changes
Cut each occurrence of IT and then type in Information Technology
questions.explain: Key: A. Find and replace changes every "IT" in one step. Scanning 50 pages or cutting each one by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and the Insert key only switches between insert and overtype mode.

questions.stem:
Which of the following must be considered when creating a website?
I. The intended audience
II. The artistic design of the whole website
III. The layout of the pages in the website
questions.explain: Key: D. Good web design plans for the audience, the overall look (design) and the layout of each page, so all three must be considered.

questions.stem: Which of the following is normally used for website-to-website connections?
questions.explain: Key: D. A hyperlink takes you from one site to another. Hypertext is the text containing links, a modem connects to the Internet, and a monitor is a display.

questions.stem: Which of the following PowerPoint Presentation icons represents the slide sorter?
options: <svg viewBox="0 0 48 40" style="width:100%;max-width:48px;height:auto;display:block" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" role="img" aria-label="icon: a projector screen on a stand"><line x1="6" y1="6" x2="42" y2="6" stroke-width="2.4"/><rect x="10" y="6" width="28" height="18"/><line x1="24" y1="24" x2="24" y2="34"/><line x1="16" y1="34" x2="32" y2="34"/></svg>

<svg viewBox="0 0 48 40" style="width:100%;max-width:48px;height:auto;display:block" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" role="img" aria-label="icon: four small squares in a grid"><rect x="8" y="6" width="13" height="11"/><rect x="27" y="6" width="13" height="11"/><rect x="8" y="23" width="13" height="11"/><rect x="27" y="23" width="13" height="11"/></svg>

<svg viewBox="0 0 48 40" style="width:100%;max-width:48px;height:auto;display:block" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" role="img" aria-label="icon: a square split into a narrow left pane and two right panes"><rect x="10" y="4" width="28" height="32"/><line x1="20" y1="4" x2="20" y2="36"/><line x1="20" y1="22" x2="38" y2="22"/></svg>

<svg viewBox="0 0 48 40" style="width:100%;max-width:48px;height:auto;display:block" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" role="img" aria-label="icon: a page with a folded corner and small dotted plus signs"><polyline points="8,4 34,4 40,10 40,36 8,36 8,4"/><line x1="24" y1="9" x2="24" y2="17"/><line x1="20" y1="13" x2="28" y2="13"/><line x1="16" y1="21" x2="16" y2="29"/><line x1="12" y1="25" x2="20" y2="25"/><line x1="30" y1="21" x2="30" y2="29"/><line x1="26" y1="25" x2="34" y2="25"/><line x1="10" y1="32" x2="38" y2="32" stroke-dasharray="2 2"/></svg>
questions.explain: Key: B. The four small squares show slides laid out as thumbnails, which is Slide Sorter view. The projector screen (A) starts the slide show, the split window (C) is Normal view, and D is another view button. (Old-syllabus item: presentation software is not in the current CSEC IT syllabus, CXC 30/G/SYLL 17.)

questions.stem: Which of the following items are considered computer hardware?
questions.explain: Key: C. Hardware is physical equipment, such as output devices. Data is raw facts, and programs and operating systems are software.

questions.stem: Data that has been processed and has meaning is termed
questions.explain: Key: A. Information is data that has been processed so that it has meaning. A database is an organised store of data, and storage and output are stages of the IPOS cycle.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be termed 'application software'?
questions.explain: Key: D. Internet Explorer is a web browser, an application program. DOS, Linux and Mac OS are operating systems (system software).

questions.stem: Which of the following activities would NOT be considered as cloud storage?
options: Data stored and accessible on a LAN
Data back-up and storage devices on the Internet
Data managed by storage providers or hosting companies
questions.explain: Key: B. Data kept on a local area network stays inside the organisation, so it is local storage, not the cloud. Cloud storage is on remote servers over the Internet, run by providers.

questions.stem: Which of the following could NOT be classified as a cloud-based application?
questions.explain: Key: D. Windows is an operating system installed on your own computer. Gmail, Dropbox and Google Drive run on remote servers and are reached over the Internet.

questions.stem: The lights in a room turn on as soon as a person enters. Which input device MOST likely controls the lighting in the room?
questions.explain: Key: A. A motion sensor detects the person automatically and switches on the lights. A remote or keyboard needs someone to press it, and a scanner captures images of documents.

questions.stem: For which of the following interface types is the user required to remember specific instructions and syntax?
questions.explain: Key: D. A command-driven interface needs typed commands with exact syntax. Menus and GUIs show you the choices, and "computer screen" is not an interface type.

questions.stem:
Item 9 refers to the following model of a globe.
[Picture: a solid three-dimensional model of the Earth (a globe).]
The MOST suitable printer for creating the model of the globe is
questions.explain: Key: A. A 3-D printer builds solid objects layer by layer, so it can make a model globe. Laser, inkjet and thermal printers only print flat images on paper.

questions.stem: The RP Secondary School wants the administrative staff to have access to all student and teacher data. Which of the following networks would be MOST suitable to enable such access?
questions.explain: Key: D. The staff are all in one school building, so a local area network (LAN) is the best fit. A WAN or MAN covers a much larger area such as a country or city, and a WLAN is just a wireless LAN; the key given for this paper is LAN.

questions.stem:
Item 11 refers to the following symbol.
The symbol represents
questions.explain: Key: B. The dot with curved bars spreading out is the standard Wi-Fi symbol. Bluetooth has its own angular “B” rune symbol, and LAN and hotspot are not shown this way.

questions.stem: Unauthorized, real-time interception of a private communication on a computer network is referred to as
questions.explain: Key: D. Secretly intercepting (listening in on) communications as they happen is electronic eavesdropping. Identity theft is pretending to be someone, industrial espionage is stealing company secrets, and propaganda is biased information.

questions.stem: Double entry data verification involves
options: the data being copied to another device
different data entered once by two different persons
the same data entered once then re-entered by another person
questions.explain: Key: D. In double entry the same data is typed twice (for example by two people) and the computer compares the two copies. Copying data or entering different data does not check for typing errors.

questions.stem: Part of a private network using Internet technology and public telecommunications that can be accessed by business suppliers, vendors, customers and partners is called an
questions.explain: Key: C. An extranet lets selected outsiders such as suppliers and customers into part of a private network. An intranet is for employees only, the Internet is public, and Ethernet is a LAN technology.

questions.stem: Which of the following shows an increase in computer memory capacity?
questions.explain: Key: D. MB < GB < TB, so D increases at every step. A decreases, and B and C are out of order.

questions.stem: Which of the following functions is performed by a modem?
questions.explain: Key: A. A modem converts between digital and analog signals (modulation and demodulation). Uploading and downloading are what you do over the connection.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of technologies is commonly used by banks to read data on cheques?
questions.explain: Key: D. MICR reads the magnetic-ink characters on cheques. OCR reads ordinary print, OMR reads shaded marks, and POS is a checkout system.

questions.stem: Which of the following operations is considered a feature of a biometric system?
questions.explain: Key: A. Biometric systems identify people from body features such as fingerprints. The other options are medical ideas.

questions.stem: In order to use a program stored on a flash drive, the program must be transferred into
questions.explain: Key: B. Programs are loaded into RAM before the CPU can run them. ROM, PROM and EPROM are read-only in normal use.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a hardware component of a computer system?
questions.explain: Key: A. A data file is stored information (software/data), not a physical part. Main memory, peripherals and the CPU are hardware.

questions.stem: The process of scrambling messages at the sending end and unscrambling them at the receiving end is called
questions.explain: Key: B. Encryption scrambles and decryption unscrambles messages. Espionage and eavesdropping are spying.

questions.stem:
There are many software restrictions used by computers to protect data and maintain data integrity. Which of the following entities are software restriction media?
I. Viruses
II. Passwords
III. Encryptions
questions.explain: Key: C. Passwords and encryption are software measures that restrict access to data. Viruses are threats, not protections, so any option with I is wrong.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices can be used for both input and output?
questions.explain: Key: A. A touchscreen shows output and takes input when you touch it. Barcode readers, scanners and document readers are input only.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of accessing files sequentially?
options: Starts with the largest data field
Starts with the smallest data field
questions.explain: Key: B. Sequential access starts at the first record and reads the records in order. "Any order" describes direct access, and field size has nothing to do with it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a hardware user interface?
questions.explain: Key: D. A touchscreen is a physical device that the user interacts with directly, so it is a hardware user interface. A GUI and icons are software, and a sensor collects data automatically rather than providing an interface for the user.

questions.stem: An official of Company X sells confidential information about his company to Company Y. What is the term used for this type of information misuse?
questions.explain: Key: C. Passing a company's secrets to a competitor is industrial espionage. Identity theft involves pretending to be a person, and eavesdropping is intercepting communications.

questions.stem: Which of the following are NOT categorized as system software?
questions.explain: Key: A. Productivity tools such as word processors and spreadsheets are application software. Operating systems, translators (compilers, interpreters) and utilities are system software.

questions.stem:
Before purchasing a computer, James was given a sheet with the following hardware specifications.
Intel Pentium IV64 bit
3.6 GHz2 GB533 MHz
50 RAM160 GBSATA
HDD7200 rpm
The word use of the computer is
questions.explain: Key: B. Word size is the number of bits the CPU handles at once, here 64 bits. 2 GB is the RAM, 7200 rpm is the hard disk speed, and 533 MHz is the bus/memory speed.

questions.stem: Which type of interface allows the user to communicate with the computer system by keying in instructions?
questions.explain: Key: D. Typing (keying in) commands is a command-driven interface. Menus, GUIs and touch interfaces let you choose rather than type commands.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a correctly formatted e-mail address?
questions.explain: Key: C. An e-mail address has a user name, one @ sign and a full domain name (happy.net). A has no proper domain, B has no user name, and D has two @ signs.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of software should be used for applications that involve repetitive numerical calculations?
questions.explain: Key: C. Spreadsheets are designed for repeated calculations with copyable formulas.

questions.stem:
The following formula is located in position B6 of a spreadsheet.

= B3 + B4 + $B$5

What would be the resulting formula if the initial formula was copied to the position located immediately on the left?
questions.explain: Key: C. Copying one column to the left (to A6) changes the relative references B3 and B4 to A3 and A4, but the absolute reference $B$5 stays the same. C-column answers move the wrong way, and B wrongly changes $B$5.

questions.stem:
In creating a query, a student entered the following criteria for the date field.

> = 05/11/2017 and < = 05/14/2017

The output will show days
questions.explain: Key: B. In month/day/year format the criteria select 11 May to 14 May 2017 inclusive. C is the opposite range, and D misreads the format.

questions.stem: Spreadsheet formulae use
questions.explain: Key: C. Formulae calculate with values, cell addresses and ranges (as in =SUM(B2:B5)*2). Labels are text and are not used in calculations, so any option with labels is wrong.

questions.stem: Which of the following buttons can be used to fully justify text?
options: <svg viewBox="0 0 60 44" style="width:100%;max-width:60px;height:auto;display:block" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" role="img" aria-label="left alignment button"><line x1="8" y1="6" x2="52" y2="6" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="12" x2="38" y2="12" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="18" x2="52" y2="18" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="24" x2="32" y2="24" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="30" x2="52" y2="30" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="36" x2="40" y2="36" stroke-width="2.6"/></svg>

<svg viewBox="0 0 60 44" style="width:100%;max-width:60px;height:auto;display:block" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" role="img" aria-label="right alignment button"><line x1="8" y1="6" x2="52" y2="6" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="22" y1="12" x2="52" y2="12" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="18" x2="52" y2="18" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="28" y1="24" x2="52" y2="24" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="30" x2="52" y2="30" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="20" y1="36" x2="52" y2="36" stroke-width="2.6"/></svg>

<svg viewBox="0 0 60 44" style="width:100%;max-width:60px;height:auto;display:block" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" role="img" aria-label="centre alignment button"><line x1="8" y1="6" x2="52" y2="6" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="15" y1="12" x2="45" y2="12" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="18" x2="52" y2="18" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="18" y1="24" x2="42" y2="24" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="30" x2="52" y2="30" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="14" y1="36" x2="46" y2="36" stroke-width="2.6"/></svg>

<svg viewBox="0 0 60 44" style="width:100%;max-width:60px;height:auto;display:block" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" role="img" aria-label="justify alignment button"><line x1="8" y1="6" x2="52" y2="6" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="12" x2="52" y2="12" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="18" x2="52" y2="18" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="24" x2="52" y2="24" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="30" x2="52" y2="30" stroke-width="2.6"/><line x1="8" y1="36" x2="52" y2="36" stroke-width="2.6"/></svg>
questions.explain: Key: D. The justify button has all lines the same length, touching both margins. A is align left (ragged right edge), B is align right, and C is centre.

questions.stem:
Item 43 refers to the following table containing data on three countries, A, B and C, for 2018 and 2019.
Country20182019
A300600
B500800
C500600
Which of the following types of charts is NOT suitable for representing the data above?
questions.explain: Key: A. A pie chart can only show the parts of one whole, so it cannot compare two years. Bar, line and column charts can show both years.

questions.stem: The field that uniquely identifies a record in a database is called the
questions.explain: Key: B. The primary key is unique for every record. A foreign key links to another table, an alternate key is a candidate key not chosen as primary, and a secondary key is used for sorting or searching.

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences of steps is correct for deleting a field in a database table?
options:
Choose the delete row option.
Select row to be deleted and right click.
Open table in design view.
Choose yes to confirm deletion.

Open table in design view.
Select row to be deleted and right click.
Choose the delete row option.
Choose yes to confirm deletion.

Select row to be deleted and right click.
Open table in design view.
Choose the delete row option.
Choose yes to confirm deletion.

Select row to be deleted and right click.
Choose the delete row option.
Open table in design view.
Choose yes to confirm deletion.
questions.explain: Key: B. Open Design View first (each field is a row there), right-click the field, choose Delete Rows and confirm. The other sequences try to select or delete before opening Design View.

questions.stem:
Item 46 refers to the following database table.
Item No.Item Desc.Quantity
H050Hammer20
H040Hammer40
FK030Fork35
FK020Fork40
FK015Fork45
The database table above shows records sorted by
questions.explain: Key: D. Item No. runs H050, H040, FK030, FK020, FK015, which is Z–A (descending) order. Quantity goes 20, 40, 35, 40, 45, so it is not sorted either way.

questions.stem:
Which of the following clearly identifies a hyperlink on an HTML document?
I. A link to an email address
II. A link to another webpage
III. A link to another location within the webpage
questions.explain: Key: D. A hyperlink can point to an e-mail address (mailto:), another web page, or a bookmark on the same page, so all three are hyperlinks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used for executing HTML code?
questions.explain: Key: B. A web browser reads the HTML and displays the page. An assembler translates assembly language, and although a browser contains a parser, the program you use to run (display) HTML is the browser.

questions.stem: Which security feature offers the LEAST protection to a Word document?
options: Saving as compatible with the appropriate software version
questions.explain: Key: D. Saving in a compatible format does nothing to protect the content. Restricting editing, adding a digital signature and encrypting with a password all protect the document.

questions.stem:
Item 50 refers to the following spreadsheet.
ABCD
1
2
3
4
5
6
7
8=sum(B2::B6)(shaded)
9
If the formula in Cell B8 is copied to the shaded cell, C8, then the formula in Cell C8 would be
questions.explain: Key: C. Copying one column to the right changes the relative column letter from B to C while the rows stay the same, giving =sum(C2:C6). A keeps the old column, and B and D wrongly shift the rows.

questions.stem:
Item 51 refers to the following algorithm.
Read (A, B)
If A < B Then
Print(A);
Which of the following tasks does the following algorithm perform?
options: Reads two numbers and prints the first number
Reads two numbers and prints the smaller number
Reads two numbers and prints the first number if it is larger than the second number
Reads two numbers and prints the first number if it is smaller than the second number
questions.explain: Key: D. A is printed only when A < B. It does not always print A, it prints nothing when B is smaller, and C reverses the condition.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a conditional construct?
questions.explain: Key: A. IF-THEN-ELSE chooses a path based on a condition (selection). FOR, WHILE and REPEAT are loops (iteration); "FOR … ENDWHILE" is also a mismatched pair.

questions.stem: When implementing a program, which of the following steps comes after executing?
questions.explain: Key: C. The order is write source code, compile (or interpret), link, execute, then maintain. Linking and compiling come before executing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a high-level programming language?
questions.explain: Key: D. Assembly language is low-level (second generation). C, Java and Pascal are high-level languages.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms is an invalid variable name?
questions.explain: Key: B. Variable names must start with a letter, so 2count is invalid. Sum, Vat15 and Count all start with a letter.

questions.stem: The decision box of a program flow chart shows the
questions.explain: Key: B. The diamond (decision) holds a test or condition with Yes/No exits. Connectors link pages, rectangles hold calculations, and parallelograms show input/output.

questions.stem:
Item 58 refers to the following algorithm.
I. Ask users for length and width
II. length, width
III. area ← length * width
IV. "Area of rectangle is", area

Which of the following options, in the correct order, can be used to replace I, II and III in the algorithm?
questions.explain: Key: C. The algorithm must first prompt the user, then read the values, and finally write (output) the result. The item's labels are a little confusing as printed, but the logical order prompt → read → write only fits option C.

questions.stem:
Item 60 refers to the following algorithm.
Write ("Enter price: ")    (1)
Read (price)               (2)
Vat: = price * 15%         (3)
Write vat                  (4)
Which line contains a processing statement?
questions.explain: Key: C. Line 3 calculates the VAT, which is processing. Lines 1 and 4 are output and line 2 is input.

questions.stem: Shanice uses her phone to pay her VirginTel bill, a laptop to type her SBA and the school Wi-Fi to upload it to Google Classroom. Which term BEST describes the combined use of computers, software and telecommunications to capture, process, store and send information?
questions.explain: Key: B. Information Technology is the use of computers, software AND telecommunications to handle information, which is everything Shanice does. A is the study of computation and programming, not the everyday use described. D is only one part (turning data into information). C covers sending data over distance but not the computers and software.

questions.stem: A weather office in Barbados must run hurricane-track models that need trillions of calculations per second. Which type of computer is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: A. Supercomputers are built for raw calculation speed, which complex weather models need. C is designed to handle huge numbers of transactions and users at once (banks, airlines), not maximum calculation speed. B is far too slow. D runs one dedicated job inside a device.

questions.stem: Zion is playing a football game on his laptop. Each time he scores, the game checks "IF score > 50" to unlock a new stadium. Which part of the CPU carries out this comparison?
questions.explain: Key: B. The ALU performs arithmetic and logical comparisons such as greater than. D fetches and decodes instructions and directs the other parts, but it does not do the comparison itself. A is fast memory holding frequently used data. C stores start-up instructions.

questions.stem: At the Zanderij Airport check-in desk an agent scans a passport, the system looks up the booking, prints a boarding pass and saves the check-in record. Which stage of the IPOS cycle is the saving of the record?
questions.explain: Key: C. Keeping the check-in record for later use is storage. Scanning the passport is A; looking up the booking is B; printing the boarding pass is D.

questions.stem: Island Bloom Florists in Cap-Haïtien wants staff in two shops to open the same price list from anywhere. They have a reliable Internet connection and a small budget for hardware. Which storage option BEST suits them?
options: An external hard drive kept in the main shop
DVD-R discs posted between the shops
A USB flash drive carried by the manager
questions.explain: Key: C. Cloud storage lets both shops reach one up-to-date file from anywhere with the Internet, and needs no new hardware. A can only be used in one place. B is slow and cannot be updated once burned. D is easily lost and only one person can use it at a time.

questions.stem: A supermarket on Hope Road wants cashiers to enter product details quickly and accurately at the till. Which input device is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Key: D. A barcode scanner reads the product code directly, which is fast and accurate. B is for drawing. C reads pencil marks on forms such as multiple-choice answer sheets. A selects points on a screen and is rarely used today.

questions.stem: The IT technician at Palmetto Point Secondary is listing the software on the lab computers for an audit. Which of the following should she list as SYSTEM software?
options: A school timetable app written for Sandbox Tree College
questions.explain: Key: C. A defragmenter is a utility, and utilities are system software because they look after the computer itself. B and D are general-purpose application software. A is custom (bespoke) application software.

questions.stem: Mr. Castillo, a network technician, types commands such as ipconfig and ping to test the school network quickly. Which type of user interface is he using?
questions.explain: Key: D. Typing text commands at a prompt is a command line interface, which experts like for speed and control. A uses windows, icons and pointers. B offers a list of choices. C relies on taps and swipes.

questions.stem: Kayla needs a laptop for video editing her Carnival TikToks. Which specification would make the BIGGEST difference to how smoothly the editing software runs?
options: A 1 TB hard disk instead of a 512 GB hard disk
Two USB ports instead of one
questions.explain: Key: C. Video editing holds large amounts of data in memory; more RAM stops the system swapping to storage and slowing down. A bigger disk in A stores more but does not make editing faster. Extra ports in D and a bigger battery in B do not affect processing speed.

questions.stem: Jaden's printer shows "Paper jam". He has removed the jammed sheet but the message is still on. What should he do NEXT?
options: Turn the printer off and on again, then send the document again
questions.explain: Key: A. After clearing a jam, restarting the printer resets the sensor and clears the queue, the simplest fix first. Reinstalling the operating system in D is drastic and unrelated. Ink in C has nothing to do with a jam. A cable in B would cause a connection error, not a jam message.

questions.stem: Ms. Brooks enters her Form 4 IT test results into a spreadsheet. Which of the following is DATA rather than information?
options: The class average for the IT test is 63%
Three students scored below the pass mark
The highest mark in the test was 91, scored by Tariq
questions.explain: Key: B. Raw numbers with no context or meaning are data. A, C and D have all been processed and given context, so they are information.

questions.stem: Daniel finds a website claiming a new hurricane will hit the Turks and Caicos Islands next week. The page was updated today, but it names no author and its owner sells hurricane shutters. Which TWO criteria for reliable information does the page FAIL?
questions.explain: Key: B. No named author means no authority, and a seller of shutters gains from spreading fear, so objectivity fails. Currency, in A and C, is fine because the page was updated today. Coverage, in A and D, is about how complete the information is, which is not the problem described. Usability, in C, is a website design criterion, not a test of reliability.

questions.stem: A clerk types a student's date of birth into the school database, then a second clerk types it again and the computer compares the two entries. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: C. Entering the data twice and comparing the copies is double entry, a verification method that checks the data was copied correctly. D and B are validation checks performed by the computer against rules, not second entries. A means visually reading the data against the source.

questions.stem: The Oranjestad Courier's subscription form must reject a phone number unless it has exactly seven digits. Which validation check is this?
questions.explain: Key: D. Checking the number of characters is a length check. A checks a value lies between limits (e.g. age 13 to 19). B checks a field is not empty. C compares two fields against each other.

questions.stem: Oduba Power & Water prints meter readings for all 40,000 customers in one run every month, processing every record in customer-number order. Which file access method is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: A. When every record is processed in key order in one batch run, sequential access is efficient. D access suits finding single records instantly. C supports both and adds an index overhead not needed here. B files are stored in the order records arrived, not in customer-number order.

questions.stem: The computers in one Breadfruit Valley Secondary lab are connected to each other and to a printer in the same room. This network is a
questions.explain: Key: A. A local area network covers a small area such as a room or building. C spans countries. B spans a town or city. D links one person's devices (phone, earbuds, watch) within a few metres.

questions.stem: Seaside Credit Union has a website for its staff only, reached with a staff login, where staff read policies and book leave. This is
questions.explain: Key: B. An intranet is a private network using web technology for an organisation's own staff. A also lets selected outsiders (suppliers, partners) in. C is the public global network. D describes how computers share resources, not a private staff website.

questions.stem: Coralstone College is replacing its peer-to-peer lab with a CLIENT–SERVER network. Which statement about the new network is TRUE?
options: Every computer has equal status and shares its own files.
It cannot be used in a school.
It does not need any network cables or wireless signals.
A central server manages files, security and backups for the client computers.
questions.explain: Key: D. In client-server networks a powerful server provides services centrally. A describes peer-to-peer. B is false: most schools use client-server. C is false: every network needs a transmission medium.

questions.stem: Sea-Almond Secondary School's lab LAN must be connected to AlliouaganaTel's network so students can reach the Internet. Which device connects the LAN to the Internet and decides the best path for data packets?
questions.explain: Key: B. A router joins different networks (the LAN and the ISP's network) and routes packets between them. A forwards data only to the right device within a LAN. D broadcasts to every device in a LAN. C connects one computer to a network.

questions.stem: A new data link between Las Américas Airport and the cruise pier must carry very high bandwidth and must not be affected by electrical interference. Which medium is BEST?
questions.explain: Key: D. Fibre carries light, giving very high bandwidth and immunity to electrical interference. A and C carry electrical signals that suffer interference and lower speeds over distance. B works only over a few metres in line of sight.

questions.stem: A walkie-talkie lets only ONE person speak at a time, but each person can both talk and listen. This mode of transmission is
questions.explain: Key: B. Data flows in both directions but only one direction at a time. A is one direction only (like a radio broadcast). C is both directions at the same time (like a phone call). D is about capacity, not direction.

questions.stem: Which mobile technology lets Aaliyah tap her phone on a card reader at a Kaya Grandi shop to pay?
questions.explain: Key: B. NFC works over a few centimetres and is used for contactless payment. A finds location. D needs line of sight and is used in TV remotes. C is used for long-distance links.

questions.stem: The school posts the new timetable at https://www.mahoegrove.sr/students/timetable.html (an address). In this URL, what does .sr represent?
options: The country-code top-level domain for Suriname
The file type of the page
The protocol used to transfer the page
The name of the folder holding the page
questions.explain: Key: A. .sr is Suriname’s country-code top-level domain. The protocol is https, which C describes. /students/ is the folder in D. .html is the file type in B.

questions.stem: Dante types www.carnivalsxm.org into his browser and the Carnival page appears a moment later. What role did DNS play?
options: It encrypts the page so it cannot be read.
It stores a copy of every website.
It translates the domain name into the server's IP address.
questions.explain: Key: D. The Domain Name System looks up the IP address for a name, like a phone book. Encryption in B is done by HTTPS. C and A are not DNS functions.

questions.stem: Two Form 4 students argue about whether "the Internet" and "the Web" are the same. Which statement settles the argument CORRECTLY?
options: The Internet is a service that runs on the Web.
The Internet and the Web are exactly the same thing.
The Web is a service that runs on the Internet.
E-mail is part of the World Wide Web.
questions.explain: Key: C. The Internet is the global network; the Web is the collection of linked pages accessed over it using HTTP. B and A confuse the two. E-mail, in D, is a separate Internet service, not part of the Web.

questions.stem: An attacker floods the Santo Domingo cruise port booking website with so many fake requests that real cruise passengers cannot reach it. This attack is
questions.explain: Key: A. DoS attacks overload a server to make it unavailable, which attacks availability. C tricks users into giving details. B redirects users to a fake site. D is illegal copying of software.

questions.stem: Keisha receives a text: "Your bank card is blocked. Click bit.ly/unblock to fix it." This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: D. Smishing is phishing by SMS text message. A uses voice calls. C secretly redirects a real web address to a fake site. B is self-replicating malware.

questions.stem: Malware that encrypts the files on The Port-au-Prince Courier's computers and demands payment to unlock them is
questions.explain: Key: B. Ransomware holds data hostage until a ransom is paid. A shows unwanted adverts. D secretly collects information. C disguises itself as useful software; it may deliver ransomware but is not defined by demanding payment.

questions.stem: Hackers steal the customer records of a Caribbean hotel chain and publish them online. Which is the MOST serious impact on the ORGANISATION?
options: Loss of reputation and customer trust, plus possible legal penalties
Customers must change their e-mail passwords
questions.explain: Key: A. Organisations lose trust, bookings and may face fines under data protection laws. D is an impact on individuals. C is not an impact on the organisation. B is unrelated to a data leak.

questions.stem: Which countermeasure BEST protects data on a laptop that might be stolen from a car?
options: Installing a firewall on the router at home
questions.explain: Key: C. Encryption makes the data unreadable without the key, even if the laptop is stolen. A is irrelevant. D protects against power spikes. A firewall at home in B does not protect a stolen device.

questions.stem: A school wants to protect its server room against power cuts during storms so the server can shut down safely. What should it install?
questions.explain: Key: B. A UPS gives battery power for long enough to shut down safely. D and C protect against software threats. A deters intruders.

questions.stem: Which is the STRONGEST password for Kevin's school e-mail?
questions.explain: Key: B. A long passphrase with upper and lower case, numbers and symbols is hard to guess or crack. D uses his name and birth year. A and C are among the most common passwords.

questions.stem: Since the bank introduced online banking and ATMs, it needs fewer tellers but has hired cybersecurity staff. This shows that automation
options: causes some job loss but also creates new jobs requiring new skills
questions.explain: Key: A. Automation replaces routine jobs but creates skilled roles, so retraining matters. B, D and C are one-sided or false.

questions.stem: Which IT professional is responsible for designing the structure of a database, managing access rights and making sure the data is backed up?
questions.explain: Key: D. The DBA designs, secures and maintains databases. C designs websites. B studies the current system and designs new systems. A repairs and maintains hardware.

questions.stem: Doctors at a hospital in St. Kitts use a video link to examine a patient on Nevis. This use of ICT is called
questions.explain: Key: C. Telemedicine delivers health care at a distance. B is working from home. D is buying and selling online. A is designing using computers.

questions.stem: Tamara copies a paragraph from a web page into her Word report but wants it to match the font of her report, not the website. Which paste option should she use?
questions.explain: Key: D. Keep Text Only strips the web formatting so the text takes on the document's style. C keeps the website's fonts. A makes uneditable text. B links to the source instead of copying it.

questions.stem: To write the chemical formula H<sub>2</sub>O correctly in a word processor, the 2 should be formatted as
questions.explain: Key: B. Subscript lowers small text below the line, as in H₂O. D raises it (as in 10²). A and C do not change the position.

questions.stem: Jerome inserted a table of contents in his SBA report, then added a new heading. The new heading does NOT appear in the TOC. What should he do?
options: Apply a Heading style to it and then update the table of contents
Insert a page break before the heading
Type the heading into the TOC by hand
Make the heading bold and larger
questions.explain: Key: A. A TOC is built from heading styles and must be updated after changes. Typing by hand (C) breaks the automatic links and page numbers. Bold and size (D) are not a heading style. A page break (B) does not add an entry.

questions.stem: Before building a website for the Simpson Bay Lagoon clean-up, a team draws boxes showing every page and how the pages link together. This diagram is a
questions.explain: Key: A. A site map shows all the pages of a site and the links between them. C (wireframe) shows the layout of a single page. D and B are not planning tools for a site.

questions.stem: On a long FAQ page, the link "Back to top" jumps to the start of the SAME page. This hyperlink goes to
options: a bookmark (anchor) on the same page
questions.explain: Key: C. Links to a place on the same page use a bookmark or anchor such as href="#top". B, A and D are the other hyperlink types.

questions.stem: In a spreadsheet, the value 450 is in the cell where column D meets row 7. The cell address is
questions.explain: Key: C. A cell address is the column letter followed by the row number. B reverses them. A is a range format. D is not valid.

questions.stem: Cells B2:B31 hold the marks of 30 students. Which formula counts how many students scored 50 or more?
questions.explain: Key: A. COUNTIF counts cells in a range that meet a condition. COUNT in B counts numbers and ignores the criterion. C does not count: SUM ignores the TRUE/FALSE results (older versions show #VALUE!). IF in D tests one value, not a count.

questions.stem: Cell D2 contains =B2*$F$1. If D2 is copied to D5, what formula is in D5?
questions.explain: Key: D. The relative reference B2 moves down 3 rows to B5; the absolute reference $F$1 does not change. A changes the absolute reference. B changes nothing. C moves the column, but the copy was straight down.

questions.stem: A teacher wants marks below 50 to turn red automatically. Which feature should she use?
questions.explain: Key: C. Conditional formatting changes a cell's appearance when a condition is met. D joins cells. A keeps headings visible. B shows long text on several lines.

questions.stem: Mrs. Duzant wants to show what PERCENTAGE of the year's Carnival budget went to each of five categories. Which chart is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Key: A. A pie chart shows parts of one whole. B shows trends over time. D shows the relationship between two numeric variables. C compares values over time, not shares of a total.

questions.stem: Which is an advantage of a database over a set of separate spreadsheets for a school's records?
options: It cannot be accessed by more than one user
Data is stored once and linked, reducing duplication and inconsistency
It does not need a computer
questions.explain: Key: B. Related tables avoid repeating data, so it stays consistent. C is false. A is false and would be a disadvantage. D is false.

questions.stem: In a table of students, which field is the MOST suitable primary key?
questions.explain: Key: C. A primary key must be unique for every record; IDs are assigned to be unique. Surnames (A), birth dates (B) and forms (D) can repeat.

questions.stem: A field PhoneNumber holds numbers such as 5421234 that are never used in calculations. The BEST data type is
questions.explain: Key: A. Phone numbers are identifiers, not quantities; Text keeps leading zeros and allows symbols like + or -. C could drop a leading zero and suggests arithmetic. D is for money. B stores only two values.

questions.stem: Which query criterion in the Surname field finds all surnames beginning with "Ri" (Richardson, Rijk, Richards)?
questions.explain: Key: D. The * wildcard matches any characters after Ri. A matches only the exact word Ri. C finds names ENDING in ri. B is an invalid range.

questions.stem: A report lists all sponsors of the Carnival parade grouped by Category, with the total donation for each category. Which report features are used?
questions.explain: Key: C. Grouping collects records by Category; Sum gives the total per group. B relates to forms and queries. D and A are table-design features.

questions.stem: The St. Kitts and Nevis Youth Cricket League wants a program to calculate batting averages. Which should be the FIRST step?
questions.explain: Key: D. You must understand exactly what is required before designing a solution. B, C and A come later.

questions.stem: A program reads the prices of items bought and outputs the total. In an IPO chart, "total" belongs under
questions.explain: Key: A. The total is the result displayed. Prices are B. Adding them is processing (C), and nothing here needs to be kept for later (D).

questions.stem: Kemar writes the steps for a robot that sorts bags at CJIA. Which of the following is NOT a property his algorithm should have?
options: It has a finite number of steps.
Each step is precise and unambiguous.
The steps are in a logical order.
It may run forever if the data is unusual.
questions.explain: Key: D. An algorithm must terminate. A, B and C are required properties.

questions.stem:
Your teacher writes this pseudocode on the board for a warm-up. What is printed?
count ← 0
FOR i ← 1 TO 4 DO
count ← count + i
ENDFOR
PRINT count
questions.explain: Key: D. count accumulates 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10. B counts iterations instead of summing. C is the final value plus one. A ignores the loop.

questions.stem: A program accepts exam marks from 0 to 100. Which value is BOUNDARY test data?
questions.explain: Key: A. Boundary data sits at the edge of the valid range (0 or 100). B is normal data. D and C are erroneous data.

questions.stem: A programmer at a Barbados engineering firm writes code for a tiny sensor chip using instructions like MOV A, 5 and ADD A, B. Which statement BEST describes the language she is using?
options: A high-level language that uses English-like words such as PRINT
A low-level language that uses mnemonics such as ADD and MOV
Binary code made only of 0s and 1s
questions.explain: Key: B. Assembly (2GL) uses short mnemonics that map to machine instructions. A describes a 3GL such as Python. D is machine code (1GL). C describes 4GLs such as SQL.

questions.stem: Akeem's program stops with an error when a user types "ten" instead of 10 at an int(input()) prompt. This is a
questions.explain: Key: B. The code is valid but crashes while running because of bad input. C or A would be found before running. D gives wrong answers without crashing.

questions.stem: A Form 5 program for the school nurse asks each student for their age, which must be stored as a whole number. Which Python statement does this correctly?
questions.explain: Key: C. input() returns text, and int() converts it to an integer. B applies int() to the prompt text. D is Java-style. A is not valid syntax.

questions.stem:
Jaylen tests this Python code in the Code Lab. What is the output?
total = 0
for i in range(1, 5):
total = total + i
print(total)
questions.explain: Key: C. range(1, 5) gives 1, 2, 3, 4 (it stops BEFORE 5), so the total is 10. D wrongly includes 5. A and B count instead of adding.

questions.stem: Your teacher asks her class to document the bus-fare program they wrote for their SBA. Which of these is INTERNAL documentation?
options: The technical specification of the server
A comment such as # calculate the discount
questions.explain: Key: D. Internal documentation is inside the program code: comments, meaningful names, indentation. A, B and C are external documentation.

questions.stem: Sunny Isle Tours, a small tour company in Grenville, has moved all its bookings onto computers. Which of the following is a LIMITATION of relying on IT?
options: It depends on a steady electricity supply and working networks.
It allows customers to pay online.
It stores records in a small physical space.
It processes large amounts of data quickly.
questions.explain: Key: A. When power or networks fail (for example after a hurricane) IT systems stop, a real limitation. D, C and B are all advantages of IT.

questions.stem: A smart fridge in a Layou hotel kitchen sends an alert when its temperature rises. The computer inside the fridge is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: D. An embedded computer is built into another device to perform one dedicated task. B and A are large, powerful systems. C is a general-purpose personal computer.

questions.stem: Shaquille's Carnival parade video is 3 GB. His school limits uploads in megabytes. About how many megabytes is the video?
questions.explain: Key: C. 1 GB = 1,024 MB, so 3 x 1,024 = 3,072 MB. A confuses MB with KB. D divides instead of multiplying. B multiplies by 8, confusing bytes with bits.

questions.stem: Which of the following storage media is the MOST durable to carry daily in a school bag because it has no moving parts?
questions.explain: Key: A. An SSD uses flash memory with no moving parts, so it survives knocks. B has spinning platters and a moving head that can be damaged by a drop. C scratches easily. D is used for backups in data centres, not carried daily.

questions.stem: In an ATM transaction at a bank on Fort Street, which step is OUTPUT?
options: The machine dispenses cash and prints a receipt.
The new balance is saved in the bank's database.
questions.explain: Key: A. Cash and a receipt are produced for the user, so that is output. Typing the PIN in C is input; checking the balance in B is processing; saving the balance in D is storage.

questions.stem: Coral Reef Dive Shop in New Amsterdam plans to keep ALL its files ONLY in the cloud. Which is a DISADVANTAGE of this plan?
options: Files can be shared with staff in other locations.
Files cannot be reached when the Internet connection is down.
The business does not have to buy and maintain servers.
The provider usually keeps backup copies.
questions.explain: Key: B. Cloud storage depends on Internet access, a real problem during outages after storms. A, C and D are advantages.

questions.stem: Mrs. Richardson, a teacher with limited use of her hands, wants to type lesson notes. Which input method is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: D. Speech recognition lets her dictate without using her hands. A, C and B all need fine hand movement.

questions.stem: A pharmacy in Brades prints small labels for medicine bottles and receipts at the counter. The printer must be quiet, fast and need no ink. Which printer is BEST?
questions.explain: Key: D. Thermal printers use heat-sensitive paper, need no ink and are quick and quiet, ideal for labels and receipts. B is noisy. A needs cartridges. C draws large technical drawings.

questions.stem: LibreOffice can be downloaded free, and anyone may view and change its program code. It is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: B. Open-source software makes the source code available for anyone to study and modify. D is a free trial of commercial software. C keeps its code secret and is licensed by the owner. A is written for one particular organisation.

questions.stem: Grandpa Arrindell, who has never used a computer, wants to buy tickets at a ferry kiosk in Marigot. Which interface would be EASIEST for him?
options: A graphical interface needing right-click menus
A touch interface with large labelled buttons
questions.explain: Key: D. Large touch buttons are intuitive and need no prior skills. A and B need memorised commands. Right-click menus in C assume mouse experience.

questions.stem: A Wallblake Road electronics store advertises a laptop with four specifications. Which one tells you about the PROCESSOR?
questions.explain: Key: C. The processor is described by its make/model, clock speed (GHz) and number of cores. D is RAM. A is storage. B is the screen.

questions.stem: A computer in the Bayleaf Hill lab shuts itself down after about 20 minutes and the case feels very hot. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The fan or air vents are blocked with dust, so the computer is overheating.
The printer is out of paper.
questions.explain: Key: A. Automatic shutdown with a hot case points to overheating, usually from dust or a failed fan. A loose monitor cable in C gives no picture but does not shut down the PC. B and D would not cause shutdowns.

questions.stem: A customer fills in a paper form to open an account at Seabreeze Credit Union; the form is then keyed into the computer. The paper form is a
questions.explain: Key: D. The original document from which data is first captured is a source document. B is output by a computer, filled in by a person and fed back in (like a utility bill stub). C can be read directly by a machine. A is output, not input.

questions.stem: A clerk types Rhea's age as 15 although she is 16. The system accepts it because it lies between 11 and 19. Why can a VALID entry like this still be WRONG?
options: Validation only checks that data is sensible and follows rules, not that it is the true value.
Validation is only done after data has been printed.
Validation checks that data was copied exactly from the source document.
Valid data is always checked by a second person.
questions.explain: Key: A. An age of 15 passes a range check of 11 to 19 even if the student is really 16. C describes verification. D describes double checking, not validation. B is false: validation happens on entry.

questions.stem: An online form for the Carnival Development Committee checks that the Date Returned is not earlier than the Date Borrowed for costume rentals. This is a
questions.explain: Key: A. Comparing two related fields to make sure they agree is a consistency (inconsistency) check. C compares one value to fixed limits. B checks the kind of data (number, text). D validates a code using a calculated extra digit.

questions.stem: Jamal links his phone to his wireless earbuds and smartwatch using Bluetooth. This forms a
questions.explain: Key: B. A personal area network connects one person's devices within a few metres. D covers a building. C covers a city. A covers countries.

questions.stem: A government wants to connect offices in Bridgetown, Holetown and Speightstown so they share one system across the island. The MOST appropriate network type is a
questions.explain: Key: A. A metropolitan area network spans a town or island-sized area. D is a few metres. B or C covers one building, not several towns.

questions.stem: A distributor lets its supermarket customers log in to its private network to check stock and place orders. This private network shared with outside partners is an
questions.explain: Key: C. An extranet extends a private network to selected outside users. B is for staff only. D is public. A links one person's devices.

questions.stem: The school buys ten new desktop computers for its lab network. Which device is REQUIRED in EACH computer so that it can connect to the network?
questions.explain: Key: B. Every networked device needs a NIC (wired or wireless) to send and receive data. D joins networks; A converts signals for the ISP line; C boosts a weak signal. None of these goes inside each computer.

questions.stem: A school's Wi-Fi signal is weak in classrooms far from the office. What should the technician add?
options: A wireless access point (or extender) nearer the classrooms
questions.explain: Key: C. An extra access point broadcasts Wi-Fi where coverage is poor. A does not improve Wi-Fi coverage. B is unrelated. D connects wired devices in one place.

questions.stem: IereTel advertises a home Internet package with "100 Mbps bandwidth". Bandwidth is BEST defined as
options: the number of computers on a network
the amount of data that can be transmitted in a given time
the length of a network cable
questions.explain: Key: C. Bandwidth is the capacity of a channel, measured in bits per second (e.g. Mbps). D, B and A are unrelated.

questions.stem: After a hurricane, GSM masts are down but a relief team still needs to send data from a remote beach. Which technology is MOST likely to work?
questions.explain: Key: A. Satellite links do not depend on local masts or cables. B and C have very short range. 4G in D needs working cell masts.

questions.stem: A Roseau mobile provider is upgrading its masts from 4G to 5G. Which is the MAIN advantage customers will notice?
options: It is only for voice calls
Much faster data speeds and lower latency
It works without any cell towers
questions.explain: Key: B. 5G offers higher speeds and very low delay. D is false: it still needs masts (more of them). C is false: it uses radio waves. A is false: it is mainly for data.

questions.stem: Why should Imani check for HTTPS before typing her card number on a website?
options: HTTPS makes the page load faster.
HTTPS encrypts data between her browser and the server.
HTTPS proves that the shop's products are good quality.
questions.explain: Key: C. HTTPS uses encryption so intercepted data cannot be read. B, D and A are not what HTTPS does; a padlock does not even prove a business is honest.

questions.stem: Which Internet service lets a family in The Bahamas make a cheap video call to relatives in Guyana over the Internet?
questions.explain: Key: C. Voice over IP carries voice and video calls over the Internet. A transfers files. D translates domain names. B is a collaboratively edited website.

questions.stem: Which of the CIA principles is broken when a student changes his grades in the school database without permission?
questions.explain: Key: D. Integrity means data is accurate and only changed by authorised people. A is about who can SEE the data. B is about data being reachable when needed. C is a security process, not one of the CIA three.

questions.stem: An IT audit at a Georgetown school finds that the office computers have not had operating system updates for two years. This weakness is called a
questions.explain: Key: C. A vulnerability is a weakness that could be exploited. A is something that might exploit it. B reduces the risk. D is the actual attempt.

questions.stem: Tyrone downloads a "free" game which secretly lets a hacker control his computer. The program is a
questions.explain: Key: B. A Trojan pretends to be useful software while hiding a malicious function. A spreads by itself across networks without needing a disguise. D protects a network. C is a small file a website stores in the browser.

questions.stem: A student copies paragraphs from a website into her SBA report without acknowledging the source. This is
questions.explain: Key: A. Presenting someone else's work as your own is plagiarism. B is copying software illegally. D is unauthorised access. C is stealing a company's secrets.

questions.stem: Mean comments about a Form 4 student spread in a WhatsApp group and on Instagram. Which is an impact of this cyberbullying on the INDIVIDUAL student?
options: Anxiety, low self-esteem and avoiding school
A fall in the company's share price
questions.explain: Key: B. Cyberbullying harms victims' mental health and attendance. C and A are impacts on governments. D is an impact on organisations.

questions.stem: Two-factor authentication (2FA) on Nadia's Instagram means she must
options: change her password every two days
enter her password AND a code sent to her phone
questions.explain: Key: D. 2FA combines something you know (password) with something you have (phone code). B is still one factor. C and A are not authentication factors.

questions.stem: The St. John’s Courier installs a firewall between its office network and the Internet. A firewall protects the network by
options: filtering incoming and outgoing traffic according to rules
questions.explain: Key: C. Firewalls allow or block traffic based on rules. Removing viruses in B is antivirus software. A is a UPS. D is a backup.

questions.stem: Which backup plan BEST protects a Cockburn Town accounting firm's data from a hurricane that floods its office?
options: Daily backups stored off-site or in the cloud
Saving files twice in the same folder
Backups on a second hard drive in the same office
questions.explain: Key: A. Off-site or cloud copies survive damage to the building. D and C keep copies in the same place. Paper in B would also be flooded and is hard to restore.

questions.stem: Ms. Hodge now works from home three days a week, connecting to her office over the Internet. This is
questions.explain: Key: D. Telecommuting is working away from the office using ICT. C involves short-term freelance jobs. B is contracting work to another firm. A is learning online.

questions.stem: A bank in Antigua is closing two branches and moving customers to online and mobile banking. Which is a DRAWBACK of this for its customers?
options: Customers can bank 24 hours a day.
Older customers without Internet skills may be left out.
questions.explain: Key: B. The digital divide can exclude people without skills or access. A, C and D are benefits.

questions.stem: Mr. Lake's newsletter spells "Phillipsburg" wrongly 23 times. The FASTEST way to correct every one is
options: Find and Replace with Replace All
questions.explain: Key: B. Replace All changes every occurrence at once. C suggests synonyms. A copies formatting. D reverses the last action.

questions.stem: Three teachers are editing the same sports-day programme, and the head of department wants to see every change and accept or reject each one. Which feature should they turn on?
questions.explain: Key: D. Track Changes records each insertion and deletion so it can be accepted or rejected. B stops people editing. A creates personalised copies. C counts words.

questions.stem: In a mail merge to send invitations to 120 parents, which item is the DATA SOURCE?
options: The list of parents' names and addresses
questions.explain: Key: A. The data source holds the records (names, addresses) that fill the fields. C is the primary (main) document. B and D are the merged output.

questions.stem: Jada is coding the home page for her school's Earth Day website and must include the logo with alternative text for screen readers. Which HTML code is correct?
options: <img src="logo.png" alt="Seagrape Bay Secondary School logo">
questions.explain: Key: D. The img tag needs src for the file and alt for the description. B has no src, so no picture shows. C creates a hyperlink to the image file. A is not a real HTML tag.

questions.stem: A business website looks fine on a desktop but on a phone the menu runs off the edge of the screen. Which evaluation criterion does it FAIL?
questions.explain: Key: A. A site should adapt to different screen sizes. C, D and B are about the content, not how it displays.

questions.stem: Mama's Johnny Cakes, a food stall in Falmouth, wants to plan its monthly budget. Which is the BEST reason to use a spreadsheet?
options: It can store photographs of every product.
Totals recalculate automatically when a value changes, so 'what-if' questions can be tested.
It prevents all errors in data entry.
It replaces the need for an accountant entirely.
questions.explain: Key: B. Automatic recalculation makes what-if analysis fast. A is not the purpose. C is false: wrong inputs give wrong outputs. D overstates what a spreadsheet does.

questions.stem: Cell A1 = 10, A2 = 4, A3 = 2. What is the result of =A1-A2*A3?
questions.explain: Key: B. Multiplication comes before subtraction (BODMAS): 4*2 = 8, then 10-8 = 2. D works left to right: (10-4)*2 = 12. C and A are miscalculations.

questions.stem: A scorekeeper's sheet has 300 rows of cricket scores. She wants the column headings in row 1 to stay visible as she scrolls down. Which feature should she use?
questions.explain: Key: C. Freezing panes locks the top row in place. D would hide the headings. B reorders data. A joins cells.

questions.stem: The tourism office has 2,000 rows of visitor data with the columns Month, Country and Visitors. The manager wants a quick summary table showing total visitors for each country, which can be rearranged by month without writing formulas. Which feature should be used?
questions.explain: Key: D. A pivot table groups and summarises large data sets (e.g. Sum of Visitors by Country) and can be rearranged by dragging fields. C only keeps headings visible. A displays data but does not summarise it into a table. B changes the look of cells that meet a condition.

questions.stem: In a workbook, cell B4 on the sheet named Summary must show the value in cell C10 of the sheet named January. Which formula is correct?
questions.explain: Key: C. A reference to another sheet uses SheetName!Cell. D reverses the parts. B uses a range colon wrongly. A is not valid without a range.

questions.stem: The Customers table of Island Water Sports holds the ID, name, phone and e-mail of each customer. In database terminology, all the details stored about ONE customer form a
questions.explain: Key: D. A record (row) holds all the fields for one entity. A is one item such as Surname. C holds many records. B asks a question of the data.

questions.stem: Table Orders contains a field CustomerID which is the primary key of table Customers. In table Orders, CustomerID is a
questions.explain: Key: D. A foreign key is a field in one table that is the primary key of another, creating the link. It is not the primary key (A) of Orders. C is made of two or more fields. B is any field that could be the primary key of its own table.

questions.stem: In a table of library books, each book has ONE publisher, but a publisher can publish MANY books. What is the relationship between Publishers and Books?
questions.explain: Key: C. One publisher relates to many books. A would mean each publisher has one book. B would need a linking table. D is incorrect.

questions.stem: A query must show members aged 13 to 17 inclusive. Which criterion in the Age field is correct?
questions.explain: Key: B. Between includes both end values. D excludes 13 and 17. C finds only those exact ages. A finds everyone outside the range.

questions.stem: The guidance counsellor needs an alphabetical list of the names of all students in Form 4B from the Students table. Which SQL statement produces it?
options: SELECT Name FROM Students WHERE Form = "4B" ORDER BY Name;
SELECT Students FROM Name WHERE Form = "4B";
SELECT Name FROM Students ORDER BY Form;
questions.explain: Key: A. SELECT field FROM table WHERE condition ORDER BY field is the right structure. B swaps table and field. D has no WHERE. C tests the wrong field.

questions.stem: Breaking the problem "organise the sports day" into smaller tasks such as "register athletes", "record results" and "award points" is called
questions.explain: Key: B. Top-down design divides a big problem into smaller, manageable sub-problems. C removes errors. D translates code. A tests an algorithm by hand.

questions.stem: A program stores the value of GCT as 0.15, and this value never changes while the program runs. GCT should be declared as a
questions.explain: Key: B. A constant holds a value that does not change during execution. C can change. D and A are data types, and 0.15 is real, not string or Boolean.

questions.stem: Kiara is drawing a flowchart for a voter-registration check. Which symbol should she use for the DECISION "Is age >= 18?"
questions.explain: Key: A. Decisions are diamonds with Yes/No exits. B is a process. C is input/output. D is start/stop.

questions.stem:
A savings game doubles a player's coins each round. How many times does the body of this loop execute?
n ← 1
WHILE n < 20 DO
n ← n * 2
ENDWHILE
questions.explain: Key: B. n takes the values 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 at the start of each pass (5 passes), becoming 32, which ends the loop. A forgets the pass that starts with n = 16. C and D assume n goes up by one or two.

questions.stem: Before typing her loop into the Code Lab, Precious completes a trace table for it. A trace table is used to
options: record the values of variables step by step to check an algorithm's logic
draw the symbols of a flowchart
questions.explain: Key: C. A trace table records variable values during a dry run. D, A and B are not its purpose.

questions.stem: Which translator converts the WHOLE high-level program into machine code BEFORE it runs, producing an executable file?
questions.explain: Key: C. A compiler translates the whole program at once into an executable. B translates and runs line by line. D translates assembly language. A joins compiled modules.

questions.stem: Put these steps in program implementation in the correct order: (1) execute, (2) create source code, (3) maintain, (4) translate/compile, (5) link.
questions.explain: Key: D. Write the source code, translate it, link it, run it, then maintain it. A compiles before writing. B links before compiling. C executes first.

questions.stem: Andre's Python program for a cricket scoreboard will not run. Which line contains a SYNTAX error?
questions.explain: Key: C. A comma is missing between the arguments, breaking the language rules. B, A and D are valid Python.

questions.stem:
A program stores the scores from four rounds of a dominoes tournament. What is printed?
scores = [12, 45, 7, 30]
big = scores[0]
for s in scores:
if s > big:
big = s
print(big)
questions.explain: Key: D. The loop keeps the largest value seen: 12, then 45; 7 and 30 are smaller. B is only the starting value. C is the last element. A is the smallest.

questions.stem: Which Python loop is MOST suitable for reading prices until the cashier types 0?
questions.explain: Key: A. A while loop repeats an unknown number of times until the sentinel 0. A for loop with range (D) repeats a fixed number of times. C chooses once. B only outputs.

questions.stem: The Caymanian tourism office uses computers and the Internet to collect visitor numbers and publish monthly reports. Which statement BEST describes the relationship between IT and information shown here?
options: IT provides the tools that turn data into useful information and communicate it.
IT and information mean the same thing.
Information can only exist on a computer.
IT is used only to store information, not to process it.
questions.explain: Key: A. IT is the set of tools (hardware, software, networks) used to capture, process, store and share information. B confuses tool and product. C is false: information exists on paper too. D ignores processing and communication.

questions.stem: A delivery rider for a Willemstad pharmacy compares devices he could carry on his scooter. Which list puts them in order from MOST portable to LEAST portable?
questions.explain: Key: C. A smartwatch is worn on the wrist, then a phone in the pocket, then a laptop in a bag, and a desktop stays on a desk. A and D mix the order; B is the reverse.

questions.stem: Leah was typing her SBA when the power went off and her laptop shut down; the unsaved work was lost. Which type of memory lost its contents?
questions.explain: Key: C. RAM is volatile; it needs power to keep its contents. D is permanent. Flash memory in B and A is non-volatile, so data survives without power.

questions.stem: A Barbados film club stores finished films on Blu-ray discs for its archive. A Blu-ray disc is an example of which type of secondary storage?
questions.explain: Key: A. Blu-ray, DVD and CD are read and written with a laser, so they are optical. C storage uses magnetised surfaces (hard disks, tape). D storage uses flash chips. B storage is RAM/ROM, not a disc.

questions.stem: A temperature sensor in a school's server room sends readings to a computer, which switches on an air conditioner if the room is above 24 °C. Switching on the air conditioner is
questions.explain: Key: C. The signal sent to the actuator that turns on the air conditioner is the result produced by the system, so it is output. The sensor reading is B; comparing with 24 °C is D; logging readings would be A.

questions.stem: Which factor is the MOST important reason a school might keep its exam results on a LOCAL server rather than in the cloud?
options: It wants to avoid buying any hardware.
It wants full physical control over who can reach the sensitive data.
It wants the provider to handle all backups automatically.
It wants staff to reach the results from any country.
questions.explain: Key: B. Local storage keeps sensitive data on premises under the school's own control. D, A and C are reasons to choose cloud storage instead.

questions.stem: The Government of Haiti wants to read the marks on 3,000 multiple-choice census forms where people shaded boxes in pencil. Which device should it use?
questions.explain: Key: B. OMR detects the position of shaded marks on a pre-printed form. C converts printed or written letters into editable text. D reads the magnetic numbers on cheques. A reads printed barcodes.

questions.stem: A blind student at Sea-Almond Secondary School needs to read the text of a website. Which output device would help MOST?
questions.explain: Key: A. A braille display raises pins to show the text as braille cells that can be read by touch. C, D and B all produce visual output.

questions.stem: A guesthouse in Sabana Basora pays a programmer to write a booking system just for its six rooms. This software is
questions.explain: Key: C. Software written for the specific needs of one organisation is custom (bespoke). B software is bought ready-made by many users. D describes how the code is licensed, not who it was written for. A maintains the computer.

questions.stem: A hotel in Grace Bay is thinking of letting guests control room lights with voice commands such as "Turn off the lamp". Which is the MAIN disadvantage of a voice interface?
options: It cannot be used by people who cannot see.
It needs a mouse and keyboard.
It needs the user to memorise many commands.
It may misunderstand accents and does not work well in noisy places.
questions.explain: Key: D. Voice interfaces struggle with background noise (a fete, a classroom) and some Caribbean accents. C describes a command line. A is wrong: voice suits visually impaired users. B is wrong: voice needs neither.

questions.stem: The school office must choose between two PCs for typing letters and keeping student records. PC1: Core i3, 8 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD, $650. PC2: Core i9, 64 GB RAM, 4 TB SSD, $3,200. Which choice is BEST justified?
options: PC1, because it meets the needs of office software at a much lower cost
PC1, because a Core i3 is faster than a Core i9
PC2, because records need 4 TB of storage
PC2, because the most powerful computer is always the best choice
questions.explain: Key: A. Evaluating a system means matching the specification to the purpose and budget; letters and records need little power. D ignores cost and purpose. C grossly overestimates the storage needed. B is false: a Core i9 is faster.

questions.stem: After Hurricane season repairs, a classroom PC shows "No Internet" but other PCs are online. What should the technician check FIRST?
options: Whether the ISP has shut down the island's Internet
Whether the printer driver is installed
Whether the network cable is plugged in or the Wi-Fi is connected on that PC
Whether the PC needs more RAM
questions.explain: Key: C. Troubleshooting starts with the simplest, local cause; if only one PC is offline, its own connection is most likely at fault. A is unlikely because other PCs work. D and B do not cause a lost connection.

questions.stem: Which source is MOST likely to give ACCURATE, CURRENT information on an approaching storm?
options: A forwarded WhatsApp voice note with no sender details
A video posted by an account that sells generators
A blog post written three years ago
The official meteorological service website, updated today
questions.explain: Key: D. An official, named authority with a current date scores best on authority and currency. A has no authority. C is out of date. B is not objective because the seller benefits from fear.

questions.stem: A Caribbean bank account number ends in an extra digit calculated from the other digits, so that a single mistyped digit is detected. This extra digit is a
questions.explain: Key: C. A check digit is calculated from the other digits and recalculated on entry; a mismatch shows an error. B checks limits. D checks the field is not empty. A adds up values in a batch of forms.

questions.stem: The Coralstone College library system must find any one student's borrowing record instantly, but also print a full list in student ID order at the end of term. Which file organisation is BEST?
questions.explain: Key: A. Index-sequential stores records in key order (for the full list) and keeps an index for fast direct access to one record. A serial file (C) is unordered. A sequential-only file (B) needs every earlier record read first to find one. Tape in D supports only sequential access.

questions.stem: A small family-run guesthouse links its three computers so each can share files and the one printer, without buying a server. In this PEER-TO-PEER network,
options: one central server controls every computer
computers must be in different countries
