each computer can share its own resources and there is no dedicated server
questions.explain: Key: D. Peer-to-peer computers have equal status and share directly. A describes client-server. B and C are false.

questions.stem: A regional bank is reviewing its networks. Which of the following is the BEST example of a WAN?
options: Five computers in a Lelydorp office
The network that connects a bank's branches in St. Kitts, Antigua and Barbados
questions.explain: Key: D. A WAN spans large distances, such as several countries. C and A are LANs/WLANs. B is a PAN.

questions.stem: The Hummingbird Ridge computer lab uses a STAR topology with all PCs cabled to one central switch. What happens if one workstation's cable is cut?
options: Data travels the other way round the ring.
Only that workstation loses its connection.
Every computer loses Internet but not files.
questions.explain: Key: B. Each device has its own link to the central switch, so one cable failure affects only that device. D describes a bus backbone failure. C is false. A describes a ring topology.

questions.stem: Which device converts digital signals from a computer into a form that can travel over a telephone or cable line, and back again?
questions.explain: Key: D. A modem modulates and demodulates signals. A and B connect devices inside a LAN. C connects a device to the LAN.

questions.stem: A TV remote that only sends signals to the TV uses which mode of transmission?
questions.explain: Key: C. Data travels in one direction only. A allows both ways, one at a time. D allows both ways at once. B combines several signals on one channel.

questions.stem: A technician is wiring a new Form 5 classroom so each PC connects to a switch on the wall. Which transmission medium is MOST likely to be used?
questions.explain: Key: B. Twisted pair is cheap and standard for short LAN links. Undersea fibre (C), satellite (A) and microwave (D) are for long-distance links.

questions.stem: During a power cut, Malik turns on the hotspot on his phone so his sister can finish her homework on her laptop. A hotspot allows the phone to
options: share its mobile data connection with other devices over Wi-Fi
questions.explain: Key: D. A hotspot turns the phone into a wireless access point. C, B and A are not hotspot functions.

questions.stem: Which is a DISADVANTAGE of relying on mobile data for an online exam at home in a hilly area of St. Kitts?
options: Mobile phones cannot use the Internet.
Mobile data cannot carry web pages.
Coverage and signal strength may be poor or unreliable.
questions.explain: Key: D. Hills and distance from masts weaken signals, a real problem on small islands. B and A are false. C is false and would not be a disadvantage.

questions.stem: After the Carnival J'ouvert jump-up, Tia saves her phone video to her cloud drive to free space. Which term describes sending the video FROM her phone TO the cloud server?
questions.explain: Key: B. Sending data from your device to a remote server is uploading. A is the reverse. D is viewing pages. C is playing media while it downloads.

questions.stem: A group of Form 5 students all edit the same online page of revision notes, and the page keeps a history of changes. This is a
questions.explain: Key: B. A wiki is a site many users can edit collaboratively, with version history. C is mainly written by one author in dated posts. A finds pages. D displays pages.

questions.stem: A fake website looks exactly like the bank's real site, and users are sent there even when they type the correct address because the DNS has been tampered with. This is
questions.explain: Key: A. Pharming redirects a correct address to a fake site by poisoning DNS or a hosts file. B relies on a link in a message. C uses phone calls. D is unsolicited bulk e-mail.

questions.stem: Someone secretly records data passing over an unsecured café Wi-Fi network. This misuse is
questions.explain: Key: A. Intercepting communications without permission is electronic eavesdropping. D overloads a service. B is illegal copying. C spreads biased information.

questions.stem: A stall in a Caribbean market sells burned copies of a popular football video game for $5 each. Selling these copies is
questions.explain: Key: C. Unauthorised copying and selling of software breaks copyright. D is passing off work as your own in writing. B tricks people into giving information. A uses someone else's personal details.

questions.stem: False stories spread on social media before an election claim that a candidate has left the island. Which impact on GOVERNMENT is MOST likely?
options: The candidate's phone battery runs down
Loss of public trust and interference with fair elections
questions.explain: Key: D. Fake news can mislead voters and damage trust in democratic processes. C, A and B are unrelated.

questions.stem: Malliouhana Power & Water is reviewing the security of its server room. Which of these is a PHYSICAL security measure?
options: A biometric fingerprint lock on the door
questions.explain: Key: B. A lock controls physical entry. A, C and D are software or logical measures.

questions.stem: The school gives teachers permission to EDIT grades but students may only VIEW their own. This countermeasure is
questions.explain: Key: A. Access privileges set what each user may read or change. B records who did what. D filters network traffic. C copies data.

questions.stem: A viral post claims the Anguilla ferry has sunk, and Josh's friends are sharing it. Which practice is part of good digital citizenship?
options: Clicking every link to see where it goes
Sharing your password with your best friend
Thinking before sharing and checking a story is true
questions.explain: Key: C. Responsible users check facts before sharing. B, D and A put people at risk.

questions.stem: Which group is MOST at risk of job loss when a supermarket installs self-checkout machines?
questions.explain: Key: B. Routine, repetitive tasks such as scanning items are the easiest to automate. C, A and D are roles that automation creates or needs more of.

questions.stem: The person who studies a business's current manual system, gathers requirements and designs a new computer system is a
questions.explain: Key: A. The systems analyst investigates problems and designs solutions. B writes the code from the design. C manages the network. D creates images and visuals.

questions.stem: A fisherman in Grenada uses an app to check wave heights and fish prices at different markets before he sets out. This BEST shows ICT in
questions.explain: Key: D. Weather and market-price apps support fishing decisions. B, A and C are different fields.

questions.stem: Shania wants page 1 of her report in portrait and page 2, a wide table, in landscape. What must she insert between the pages?
questions.explain: Key: A. Orientation is set per section, so a section break lets each part have its own layout. D affects columns only. B starts a new line. C adds a note at the bottom of the page.

questions.stem: The guidance office sends out a form letter and wants to stop anyone changing it, but still allow it to be opened and read. Which option is BEST?
options: Restrict Editing so the document is read-only
questions.explain: Key: D. Restricting editing (or marking as read-only with a password) prevents changes while allowing reading. B records changes but allows them. C and A do not protect the document.

questions.stem: On a fillable registration form for the Carnival Village food tent, applicants must choose ONE of: Johnny cakes, Guavaberry drinks, Johnny cakes and drinks. Which form control is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. A drop-down list limits the entry to set choices, preventing typing errors. C allows anything. D is for dates. A is for images.

questions.stem: A Form 5 group is designing a six-page website for a hurricane-preparedness campaign. Which design feature BEST helps users move between its pages?
options: A different background colour on each page
A consistent navigation bar on every page
Very large images on the home page
questions.explain: Key: C. Consistent navigation in the same place lets users find any page. B confuses users. D slows loading. A makes reading harder.

questions.stem: A web page contains: <a href="mailto:info@carnivalsxm.org">Contact us</a>. What happens when a visitor clicks "Contact us"?
options: The browser opens the Carnival website home page
A file downloads to the computer
A new e-mail message opens addressed to info@carnivalsxm.org
The visitor jumps to the top of the page
questions.explain: Key: C. The mailto: link type opens the user's e-mail program. D needs a #bookmark. B needs a link to a file. A needs a web address.

questions.stem: In a sports-day sheet, C2 holds a student's house points. Which formula displays "Qualify" if the points are 20 or more, otherwise "Try again"?
questions.explain: Key: B. IF(test, value if true, value if false) with >= includes exactly 20. C excludes 20. D swaps the results. A returns a count (0 or 1), not the words.

questions.stem: A price list is in A2:B50 (code in column A, price in column B). Which formula finds the price of the item code typed in E2?
questions.explain: Key: A. VLOOKUP(lookup value, table, column number, FALSE for exact match) returns column 2, the price. C has the arguments in the wrong order. B returns column 1, the code itself. D is incorrect syntax.

questions.stem: A cell shows #DIV/0!. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The formula divides by an empty cell or a cell containing zero
questions.explain: Key: A. #DIV/0! means division by zero (empty cells count as 0). A misspelled function in B gives #NAME?. A narrow column in C shows ####. A deleted cell in D gives #REF!.

questions.stem: A sheet of costume orders must be sorted by Band (A to Z) and, within each band, by Cost (highest first). Which is correct?
options: Primary key Band descending; secondary key Cost ascending
Sort Band only, then type the costs in order
Primary key Band ascending; secondary key Cost descending
Primary key Cost descending; secondary key Band ascending
questions.explain: Key: C. The main grouping is the primary key; the order within each group is the secondary key. D swaps the keys. A reverses both directions. B is manual and error-prone.

questions.stem: A school has one worksheet per term and a Year sheet with =SUM(Term1:Term3!D5). What does this formula do?
options: Adds cell D5 on every sheet from Term1 to Term3
Counts the sheets in the workbook
Links to an external file named Term3
Adds cells D1 to D5 on the Term1 sheet only
questions.explain: Key: A. This is a 3-D reference: the same cell across a range of sheets. D, B and C misread the reference.

questions.stem: A small clinic in Puerto Plata plans to replace its paper patient cards with a computerised database. Which is a DISADVANTAGE?
options: Several staff can see the same up-to-date record
Staff need training, and setup costs money
questions.explain: Key: C. Costs and training are genuine drawbacks. B, A and D are advantages.

questions.stem: A linking table StudentClub records which students belong to which clubs. Its primary key is made from BOTH StudentID and ClubID. This is a
questions.explain: Key: B. A primary key made of two or more fields is composite. Each part is ALSO a foreign key, but together they form the key, so D is incomplete. C is used for sorting or searching. A is a single field.

questions.stem: In the school sports federation's Athletes table, the Gender field must only accept M or F. Which table property enforces this?
questions.explain: Key: D. A validation rule such as "M" Or "F" rejects anything else. A fills a value in automatically. C changes the label. B allows 50 characters.

questions.stem: In a query for a Road Town hardware store, a new column is typed as LineTotal: [Quantity]*[UnitPrice]. This is a
questions.explain: Key: C. A calculated field creates a new value from other fields. A prompts for a value. D and B are keys in tables.

questions.stem: A data-entry screen shows one customer at the top and a list of that customer's orders underneath. This design is a
questions.explain: Key: B. A subform shows the related 'many' records for the record in the main form. A is for printing. C asks for a value. D shows rows of one table.

questions.stem: After designing an algorithm to calculate bus fares, Ravi tests it with several fares to make sure it gives the right answers. Which problem-solving step is this?
questions.explain: Key: B. Checking that the algorithm gives correct results is testing and validation. A, D and C are earlier steps.

questions.stem: Which data type is MOST suitable for a variable that records whether a student has paid the Carnival trip fee?
questions.explain: Key: A. Paid or not paid has only two values: TRUE/FALSE. D and B are numbers. C holds one symbol.

questions.stem: A cashier at a Carnival food booth enters the price of each item sold and types -1 when the day is over. Which control structure should the algorithm use?
options: A loop controlled by a sentinel value
questions.explain: Key: D. -1 is a sentinel (rogue) value that ends a loop such as WHILE or REPEAT-UNTIL. A runs once in order. C chooses once. B declares data.

questions.stem:
What is printed when this pseudocode runs with score = 75?
IF score >= 80 THEN
PRINT "Distinction"
ELSE IF score >= 60 THEN
PRINT "Credit"
ELSE
PRINT "Pass"
ENDIF
questions.explain: Key: B. 75 is not >= 80, but it is >= 60, so Credit is printed and the rest is skipped. D needs 80 or more. A is only for scores below 60. C wrongly runs two branches.

questions.stem: A trace of an algorithm shows the variable total ends at 30, but the correct total is 40. The program ran without crashing. What type of error does the algorithm contain?
questions.explain: Key: B. The algorithm runs but gives a wrong result, a logic error. A stops translation. D crashes the program while it runs. C is unrelated.

questions.stem: Testing a program on the computer with prepared test data (normal, boundary and erroneous) is DIFFERENT from a dry run because
options: test data is never used in computer testing
a dry run uses a compiler
a dry run happens after the program is sold
the program is actually executed by the computer rather than traced by hand
questions.explain: Key: D. A dry run is a manual trace; computer testing runs the code. B, A and C are false.

questions.stem: A Trinidad doubles vendor's Pascal program stores the price of a meal, such as 12.50. Which declaration creates this variable?
questions.explain: Key: D. A price with decimals needs the real data type. C holds whole numbers only. B holds true/false. A holds one character.

questions.stem:
What is the output of this Python code when temp = 31?
if temp > 32:
print("Hot")
elif temp > 28:
print("Warm")
else:
print("Cool")
questions.explain: Key: C. 31 is not greater than 32, but it is greater than 28, so Warm prints. A needs more than 32. D needs 28 or below. B wrongly runs two branches.

questions.stem: Which Python code performs a LINEAR SEARCH for the name "Zion" in the list names?
options:
found = False
for n in names:
    if n == "Zion":
        found = True
questions.explain: Key: D. A linear search checks each element in turn and sets a flag if found. A sorts. C prints the first element. B overwrites the list.

questions.stem: Kyle's bus-fare program uses the variable name x for the total fare. His teacher asks him to rename it total_fare. Why?
options: Meaningful identifiers make the code easier to read and maintain.
Python does not allow single-letter names.
It makes the program use less memory.
Short names make the program run faster.
questions.explain: Key: A. Meaningful names are part of good internal documentation. D and C are false: names do not affect speed or memory noticeably. B is false: single-letter names are allowed.

questions.stem: A student explains to her Form 4 class that a supermarket in Montego Bay uses computers and telecommunications to capture, store, process and transmit sales data. Which term BEST describes this use of technology?
questions.explain: Key: C. IT is the use of computers (and telecommunications) to store, retrieve, transmit and manipulate data. B is hardware design; C controls physical processes; D is automatic sensor recording.

questions.stem: At King Street Phone Hub, the rule 'Back up the sales file every evening' is part of the ICT system. Which level of the ICT Components Hierarchy does this rule belong to?
questions.explain: Key: C. A rule people follow is a procedure. A is physical equipment; C is programs; D is communication links.

questions.stem: A regional weather service needs to model the path of a hurricane approaching the Leeward Islands using trillions of calculations. Which type of computer is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. Supercomputers are built for massive calculation speed. A suits many transactions; B and D lack the power.

questions.stem: A bank with branches on six islands must process millions of card transactions each day, reliably, for thousands of users at once. Which type of computer should it use?
questions.explain: Key: A. Mainframes handle huge numbers of simultaneous transactions reliably. A is for scientific calculation; B and C are personal devices.

questions.stem: A Liamuiga Power & Water clerk types a meter reading of 95,000 instead of 950, and the customer receives a huge bill. The computer calculated correctly. This situation illustrates:
questions.explain: Key: B. Garbage In, Garbage Out: wrong input gives wrong output. Nothing suggests malware (B), failure (C) or a processing mode (D).

questions.stem: A juice factory in Trinidad keeps its pasteuriser at exactly 72 °C with no operator. Which feature is ESSENTIAL for this process control application?
questions.explain: Key: A. Process control needs sensor input, real-time processing and output to control devices. A, C and D are not essential.

questions.stem: Tiana is typing her SBA when a power cut switches off her desktop. Work she had not saved is lost. In which type of memory was the unsaved work held?
questions.explain: Key: B. RAM is volatile. ROM and EPROM are non-volatile (A, D); the hard disk holds only saved work (B).

questions.stem: While a grade-book program runs, one part of the CPU decides whether each student's mark is greater than or equal to 50. Which part performs this comparison?
questions.explain: Key: B. The ALU performs arithmetic and logical comparisons. A coordinates; C stores frequently used data; B is secondary storage.

questions.stem: Each promotional photo for a New Amsterdam hotel is 4 MB. How many photos fit on a 2 GB memory card? (Use 1 GB = 1,024 MB.)
questions.explain: Key: B. 2 × 1,024 = 2,048 MB; 2,048 ÷ 4 = 512. B uses 1,000; C forgets to divide; D is a wrong operation.

questions.stem: A technician says a chip in an old machine can be wiped by exposing it to ultraviolet light and then reprogrammed. Which type of memory is this?
questions.explain: Key: D. EPROM is erased with ultraviolet light. A can be written only once; C and D are volatile RAM types.

questions.stem: A regional bank keeps a copy of all its records for ten years in a vault in another country, and rarely needs to read individual records. Which medium is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. Tape has huge capacity, low cost and long shelf life for archives. A and B have small capacity; D is volatile.

questions.stem: A small business stores all its files only in cloud storage. After a storm, power returns in Gros Islet but there is no Internet for three days. What is the MAIN problem?
options: The files are encrypted by the storm
questions.explain: Key: B. Cloud storage depends on an Internet connection. The files still exist (A); C and B are not caused by an outage.

questions.stem: Your CXC Paper 01 answer sheet is marked by a machine that detects which bubbles have been shaded. Which input method is used?
questions.explain: Key: C. OMR detects marks in set positions. C reads characters; B reads magnetic ink; D reads bars.

questions.stem: Island Auto Repairs in San Fernando must print job cards on three-part carbon forms in a dusty workshop. Which printer should it buy?
questions.explain: Key: C. Only an impact printer presses through carbon copies. A, D and C are non-impact.

questions.stem: Aaliyah, a Form 4 student, is blind. Which pair of devices would BEST allow her to use a computer for her coursework?
options: Screen reader with headphones and a refreshable braille display
questions.explain: Key: D. Sound and touch replace sight. A, B and D all depend on seeing the screen or output.

questions.stem: A hotel pool system uses a sensor to measure the water level and a motorised valve to let in more water when the level is low. What is the motorised valve?
questions.explain: Key: C. An actuator turns a signal into physical action. The sensor (B) is the input device (A); the valve does not store data (B).

questions.stem: Kyle edits a document while another document prints and music plays. Which operating system feature allows one user to do several tasks at the same time?
questions.explain: Key: D. Multitasking lets one user run and switch between several tasks. B processes saved-up jobs; C serves many users; D is a utility.

questions.stem: GRENLEC collects meter readings over a month and then produces every customer's bill in a single run. Which processing mode is this?
questions.explain: Key: A. Data accumulated over a period and processed together is batch processing. A and C process immediately; D is not one of the three modes.

questions.stem: Shanice downloads a free 'Carnival filter' app that secretly sends her passwords to criminals. Which type of malware is this?
questions.explain: Key: D. A Trojan horse is disguised as something useful or fun. A spreads by itself; B and D are not malware.

questions.stem: A student's Pascal program for the SBA is translated as a whole into machine code, producing a file that can run on its own. Which translator was used?
questions.explain: Key: D. A compiler translates the whole program at once. A translates line by line; B translates assembly language; C is a utility.

questions.stem: A two-person tour company in English Harbour needs invoicing software within a week and has a budget of US$300. Which type of software is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Key: B. Off-the-shelf software is cheap and available immediately. B is costly and slow; C and D do not provide invoicing.

questions.stem: Tourists collecting hire cars at a NMIA self-service kiosk need to find their booking, sign and collect a key. Which user interface is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: D. Simple guided choices suit first-time users. A needs expert knowledge; C is for developers; D is unreliable in a noisy airport.

questions.stem: Tamika, a Form 5 student who travels by bus, compares laptops. One has a 10-hour battery and weighs 1.4 kg; the other has a 3.5-hour battery and weighs 2.9 kg. Which specifications matter MOST for her?
questions.explain: Key: A. Portability depends on battery life and weight. B, A and D do not address her daily travel.

questions.stem: In the Sandbox Tree College lab, a monitor's power light is on and the computer is running, but the screen is black. What should a student check NEXT?
options: The video cable and the monitor's input source
questions.explain: Key: B. Both devices have power, so the signal path is next. A is already proven; C and B are unrelated to the display.

questions.stem: A Form 5 class records 45, 78, 62, 90 and 51 as test marks. The teacher then states, 'The class average is 65.2.' Which statement is correct?
options: The marks are information; the average is data
The marks are data; the average is information
questions.explain: Key: C. Raw marks are data; the processed average is meaningful information.

questions.stem: A cable company prints each bill with a payment slip showing the customer's account number. The customer returns the slip with payment and it is scanned back into the same system. The slip is a:
questions.explain: Key: D. It is output by the system, completed and returned as input. A is incomplete; C and D are not documents of this kind.

questions.stem: Kemar is researching coral reefs around Jamaica. He finds a dive shop's page that says 'Our reefs are perfect, book your dive now!' Which criterion is MOST in question?
questions.explain: Key: B. A business selling dives has a reason to be biased. A, B and D are not the main concern here.

questions.stem: A website asks a new user to type her password twice so that the two entries can be compared. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Key: D. Entering data twice and comparing is double-entry verification. A, C and B are validation checks.

questions.stem: At the tuck shop, prices range from US$0.50 to US$6.00. A patty was rung up as US$250 instead of US$2.50. Which validation check would BEST prevent this?
questions.explain: Key: C. 250 is outside 0.50–6.00. B only checks for blanks; C compares two fields; D is verification, not validation.

questions.stem: A supermarket till must find a product's price the instant its barcode is scanned, from a file of 20,000 products. Which file organisation is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: A. Random organisation calculates the record's address for instant access. A and C require reading from the start; D causes errors.

questions.stem: A hotel group links the reservation systems of its hotels in Jamaica, Antigua and Barbados so all front desks share one booking database. What type of network is this?
questions.explain: Key: A. The hotels are on different islands, so the network covers a wide area. A LAN covers one site, a MAN one city, and a PAN the space around one person.

questions.stem: Jada's smartwatch sends her step count to her phone, which plays music through her Bluetooth earbuds while she jogs along the Roseau boardwalk. These devices form a
questions.explain: Key: B. Devices around one person, linked by Bluetooth within a few metres, form a Personal Area Network. The other options cover much larger areas.

questions.stem: At a secondary school, students can log in at any of the 90 computers and find their own saved documents, and the technician backs up all work every night from one machine. Which network model is in use?
questions.explain: Key: D. Roaming log-ins and central backup depend on a central server. Peer-to-peer has no server; PAN and extranet describe area and access, not this model.

questions.stem: A resort in English Harbour lets approved travel agents in the USA log in to its booking system to reserve rooms for their clients. The agents are using the resort's
questions.explain: Key: A. Selected outsiders with controlled log-ins use an extranet. An intranet is for the resort's own staff only; the public Internet requires no special access; a LAN is defined by area.

questions.stem: In a computer lab arranged in a star topology, the central switch suddenly fails. What is the MOST likely result?
options: Only one computer loses its connection
Data is rerouted through the backbone cable
All computers in the lab lose network access
The printer becomes the new switch
questions.explain: Key: C. Every device in a star connects through the central switch, so its failure stops the whole network. One computer failing would affect only that computer; rerouting is a mesh feature; a printer cannot act as a switch.

questions.stem: A school replaces cables in its library with Wi-Fi so students can use laptops anywhere. Which is a disadvantage of this WLAN compared with the old cabled LAN?
options: New devices are easier to add
No cables need to be laid
Signals can be intercepted, so strong encryption is needed
Students can move around the library
questions.explain: Key: C. Radio signals travel through the air and can be intercepted, so WPA2/WPA3 encryption is needed. The other three options are advantages of a WLAN.

questions.stem: An emergency operations centre wants its network links to keep working even if one connection is cut by a falling tree during a hurricane. Which topology BEST meets this need?
questions.explain: Key: A. Mesh provides several routes, so data can avoid a broken link. A bus fails if the backbone breaks, a star if the centre fails, and a single ring if one link breaks.

questions.stem: A three-person tour desk at the cruise pier shares one printer and a few files between laptops. They have no IT budget and little technical skill. Which is the MAIN advantage of a peer-to-peer network for them?
options: Cheap and simple to set up without a dedicated server
Scales easily to hundreds of users
questions.explain: Key: A. Peer-to-peer uses existing computers and needs no server or specialist. Central security, central backup and scalability are client–server advantages.

questions.stem: Ms Hodge is on a call while a bus carries her from San Fernando to Port of Spain. Her phone moves from one cell tower's area to the next without the call dropping. This process is called
questions.explain: Key: C. Passing a call between cells is a handover. Roaming means using another operator's network; tethering shares data; pairing links Bluetooth devices.

questions.stem: A lab of 30 PCs connected through an old hub slows down whenever students save work at the same time. The technician replaces the hub with a switch. Why does this help?
options: A switch sends data only to the port of the intended device
A switch boosts the Wi-Fi signal
A switch connects the lab directly to the Internet
A switch converts digital signals to analogue
questions.explain: Key: A. A switch uses MAC addresses to deliver data only where it is needed, reducing collisions. Converting signals is a modem's job, connecting to the Internet is a router's, and boosting is a repeater's.

questions.stem: Which device connects the LAN in a Frederick Street jewellery store to its ISP's network and forwards data packets between the two networks?
questions.explain: Key: D. Routers connect different networks using IP addresses. Switches and hubs connect devices within one LAN; a NIC connects one device.

questions.stem: A family in a rural area still connects over a telephone line. Which device converts the computer's digital signals into analogue signals for the line, and back again?
questions.explain: Key: A. Modem stands for modulator–demodulator. A router links networks, a switch links LAN devices and a WAP lets wireless devices join a LAN.

questions.stem: A school wants students' tablets in every classroom to connect to its existing cabled network. Which device should be installed in each block?
questions.explain: Key: B. A wireless access point connects wireless devices to a wired LAN. A modem converts signals for an ISP line, a bridge joins LAN segments, and a hub is a wired connector.

questions.stem: Kittitian Water & Light company needs a high-bandwidth link to a power station 2 km away, past high-voltage equipment and in an area with frequent lightning. Which medium is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. Fibre carries light, so it is immune to electrical interference and lightning, and it handles long distances at high bandwidth. UTP is limited to about 100 m and affected by interference; infrared and Bluetooth have tiny ranges.

questions.stem: A cruise ship sailing between Haiti and Barbados wants to offer Internet access to passengers while far from land. Which transmission medium makes this possible?
questions.explain: Key: D. Only satellite covers ships in the open ocean. Cables cannot reach a moving ship, and infrared works only over a few metres.

questions.stem: Andre downloads a 500 MB video for his SBA on a 25 Mbps connection. Ignoring overheads, how long will the download take?
questions.explain: Key: B. 500 MB × 8 = 4,000 Mb; 4,000 ÷ 25 = 160 s. 20 s comes from forgetting to multiply by 8; the other values come from arithmetic slips.

questions.stem: Security officers at Carnival Village use two-way radios. Only one person can speak at a time and each says 'Over' when finished. Which transmission mode is this?
questions.explain: Key: C. Both directions, but one at a time, is half-duplex. Simplex is one-way only; full-duplex allows both at once, as in a phone call.

questions.stem: Rohan's TV remote stops working whenever his little brother sits between the remote and the TV. Which medium does the remote MOST likely use?
questions.explain: Key: B. Infrared needs a clear line of sight and is blocked by people and objects. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi radio pass around and through obstacles; satellites are not used by remotes.

questions.stem: An engineer in Paramaribo wants to control a port crane remotely in real time, with almost no delay between her command and the crane's movement. Which feature of 5G is MOST important here?
questions.explain: Key: A. Low latency is what allows real-time remote control. SMS arrived with 2G; infrared and 2G batteries are irrelevant.

questions.stem: At a store on Market Street, Tamara holds her phone about 2 cm from the card terminal and the payment is approved after she scans her fingerprint. Which technology sent the payment details?
questions.explain: Key: B. Tap-to-pay over a few centimetres with no pairing is Near Field Communication. GPS gives location, Bluetooth needs pairing over about 10 m, and infrared is used by remotes.

questions.stem: Kemar is hiking where there is no mobile signal, yet his phone still shows his exact position on a map he downloaded earlier. Why is this possible?
options: NFC tags along the trail send his position
The phone guesses from his last Wi-Fi network
The GPS receiver uses satellite signals and does not need mobile data
The phone uses Bluetooth from nearby hikers
questions.explain: Key: C. GPS is receive-only from satellites; the downloaded map provides the background. Bluetooth and NFC do not provide location in this way, and guessing would not be exact.

questions.stem: Dante's laptop has no Internet connection, but his phone has a strong 4G signal. He turns on a setting so the laptop can use the phone's data over Wi-Fi. This is called
questions.explain: Key: A. Sharing a phone's mobile data with other devices is tethering via a personal hotspot. Roaming uses another operator's network; pairing is Bluetooth; handover is moving between cells.

questions.stem: At Douglas–Charles Airport, Rhea sees two networks: the airport's official one and 'Free_Airport_WiFi2' with no password. What is the MAIN risk of logging in to her bank on the second network?
options: Bank apps cannot work on any Wi-Fi
It may be a fake (evil twin) hotspot used to capture her data
It will use up her mobile data bundle
questions.explain: Key: C. An open hotspot imitating the real network can be used to intercept log-ins. Battery and data use are not the main risk, and bank apps do work on Wi-Fi.

questions.stem: Mr Lake, who lives in Dutch Quarter, sends his daily blood-pressure readings from a home monitor through his phone to a heart specialist overseas and has monthly video consultations. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: A. Health care delivered at a distance using telecommunications is telemedicine. The other options are unrelated uses.

questions.stem: Kayla says that a WhatsApp video call to her cousin in Antigua and reading the CXC website are both uses of the World Wide Web. Which statement is correct?
options: Only the video call uses the Internet
Both are part of the World Wide Web
Both use the Internet, but only the website is part of the World Wide Web
questions.explain: Key: D. The Web is linked pages accessed with HTTP; the call is a VoIP service that uses the Internet but not the Web. The other options misunderstand the Internet–Web relationship.

questions.stem: Keisha is booking a snorkelling trip on the site https://www.tobagotours.co.tt/trips/reef.html and wants to know which country's domain it uses. Which part of the URL is the top-level domain?
questions.explain: Key: B. The TLD is the last part of the domain name: .tt (Trinidad and Tobago). https is the protocol, /trips/ the path and reef.html the file name.

questions.stem: Ashley types www.coralreefcafe.gd into her browser. Before the page can load, which system converts that name into the web server's IP address?
questions.explain: Key: A. The Domain Name System translates domain names into IP addresses. HTML writes pages, FTP transfers files and VoIP carries calls.

questions.stem: Ms Hodge is about to pay school fees online. The address starts with https:// and shows a padlock. What does the HTTPS protocol guarantee?
options: Data sent between her browser and the server is encrypted
The organisation running the site is honest
questions.explain: Key: C. HTTPS encrypts data in transit. It does not prove a site is honest (scammers can use HTTPS), error-free or faster.

questions.stem: A web designer finishes a website for a soursop shop on her laptop. To make it available to the world, she logs in to the hosting server and transfers the files. What is she doing, and with which protocol?
questions.explain: Key: D. Sending files from her laptop to the server is uploading, and FTP/SFTP is the file transfer protocol. DNS translates names, VoIP carries calls, and downloading is the opposite direction.

questions.stem: A small business in Holetown stores all its records in cloud storage. During a two-day Internet outage after a storm, what problem is it MOST likely to face?
options: Staff cannot access the records until the connection returns
The cloud provider loses all data on the island
questions.explain: Key: B. Cloud data is safe off-site but needs an Internet connection to reach it. An outage does not delete cloud data, stop computers starting or affect data held overseas.

questions.stem: A hacker breaks into a Barbados school's system and changes several students' final marks. The system stays online and nothing is copied. Which security goal has been broken?
questions.explain: Key: C. The marks are now inaccurate (integrity). Nothing was disclosed (A) and the system stayed online (C); portability is not a security goal.

questions.stem: An audit of a Willemstad law office finds every PC still uses the factory password 'admin'. This password is BEST described as a
questions.explain: Key: D. It is a weakness. A threat is something that could exploit it, an attack is the actual attempt, a countermeasure reduces risk.

questions.stem: Within an hour of one infected laptop joining a hotel network in Ocho Rios, every unpatched PC is infected, though no one opened a file. The malware is MOST likely a
questions.explain: Key: C. Self-spreading without user action is a worm. A virus needs a host file to be opened; a trojan relies on disguise; adware shows adverts.

questions.stem: Shania downloads a free movie app that works normally but secretly records her passwords. The app is BEST described as a
questions.explain: Key: A. It is disguised as useful (trojan) and spies (spyware). It did not self-replicate (A). C is a protection; D floods servers.

questions.stem: Customers of a Trinidad bank type the bank's correct web address but arrive at a convincing fake site. This attack is
questions.explain: Key: D. Correct address, wrong site = pharming (e.g. poisoned DNS). Phishing needs a fake link; vishing is by phone; plagiarism is unrelated.

questions.stem: A resident of Nevis receives a text saying she has won a cruise and must reply with her card number. This is
questions.explain: Key: B. Phishing by SMS = smishing. Vishing is by voice call; C uses e-mail; pharming redirects web traffic.

questions.stem: A ferry company's booking website in Anguilla goes offline for six hours because thousands of infected devices flood it with requests. This is a
questions.explain: Key: D. Many devices flooding a server = distributed denial of service. The others do not involve flooding.

questions.stem: Kerry copies an 1850 poem, which is out of copyright, and enters it in a school competition as her own. This is
questions.explain: Key: A. No copyright exists, so it is not infringement, but she claimed the work as hers: plagiarism.

questions.stem: A Grenada business buys one licence for accounting software and installs it on six office PCs. This breaks the
options: acceptable use policy of the bank
End User Licence Agreement, so it is software piracy
questions.explain: Key: C. Installing beyond the licence terms in the EULA is piracy. The other options are unrelated documents or principles.

questions.stem: Over three weeks, a Form 4 student in Road Town is mocked daily in group chats, stops sleeping well and misses classes. The MAIN impact on him is
questions.explain: Key: A. Anxiety and sleep loss are psychological, with knock-on effects on school. There is no evidence of A, C or D.

questions.stem: Ransomware shuts down the computer systems of a company that unloads containers at the Belize City tender port for a week. The MOST likely knock-on impact is that
options: supermarkets and hardware stores run short of stock
questions.explain: Key: D. Imports cannot be processed, so businesses run short. B, C and D are not linked to the port's systems.

questions.stem: A small Antigua hotel refused to pay a ransom and restored its data from backups but still lost money. Its LARGEST hidden cost was MOST likely
options: lost bookings while systems were down
questions.explain: Key: D. Downtime and lost revenue are usually the biggest hidden cost. The ransom was not paid; C and D are trivial.

questions.stem: Why is the leak of citizens' fingerprints from a national ID database MORE serious in the long term than the theft of their bank cards?
questions.explain: Key: D. Biometric data is permanent; cards can be cancelled. C and D are false; B misses the point.

questions.stem: Hackers try to disrupt the computers that control water pumping for an entire Caribbean island. This is especially serious for the government because
options: it is a form of plagiarism
water companies do not use computers
water supply is critical national infrastructure
questions.explain: Key: D. Critical infrastructure attacks threaten public health and safety. B and C are irrelevant; D is false.

questions.stem: The Kingston power supply often cuts out for a few minutes. An office wants staff to be able to save their work and shut down safely. It should install
questions.explain: Key: D. A UPS provides short-term battery power. A surge protector handles spikes; C and D are network protections.

questions.stem: A San Pedro shop kept its only backup drive in the same desk as its PC, and a flood destroyed both. The BEST improvement is to
options: keep an automatic backup in the cloud or another location
back up more carefully on Fridays
questions.explain: Key: A. Off-site/cloud copies survive local disasters. A and D keep the same location problem; C does not stop floods.

questions.stem: The IT technician at a St. Lucia credit union is choosing a login method for staff who approve loans. Which combination is a TRUE example of two-factor authentication?
options: Password and a code from an authenticator app
questions.explain: Key: C. Something you know plus something you have. A and C are both 'know'; D is single-factor.

questions.stem: A laptop holding a St. Kitts clinic's patient records is stolen from a car. Which countermeasure would mean the thief CANNOT read the records?
questions.explain: Key: A. Encrypted data is unreadable without the key. The others do not protect stored data.

questions.stem: At a Jamaican hospital, porters can view full patient histories. Which countermeasure BEST fixes this?
options: Access privileges based on least privilege
questions.explain: Key: D. Give each role only the access it needs. B and C are irrelevant; D weakens security.

questions.stem: A teacher's grade was changed overnight in a school system. Which countermeasure shows WHO made the change and WHEN?
questions.explain: Key: B. An audit trail logs actions with user and time. The others do not record activity.

questions.stem: Mr. Hodge receives an e-mail from support@rnicrosoft.com asking him to reset his password. Which habit would reveal the trick MOST directly?
options: Replying to ask if it is genuine
Inspecting the address for substituted characters
questions.explain: Key: D. 'rn' replaces 'm'. Replying, clicking or forwarding all engage with the attacker or spread the risk.

questions.stem: A café in Grand Anse that lets customers use its Wi-Fi still protects the network with WEP encryption, and the owner worries about eavesdropping. The technician should advise
options: keeping WEP because it is strongest
upgrading to WPA2 or WPA3 with a strong passphrase
questions.explain: Key: C. WEP is easily cracked. C makes it open; D is only a speed bump.

questions.stem: A Trinidad supermarket replaces 8 of 12 cashier tills with self-checkouts. Which plan BEST balances automation's benefits with its impact on staff?
options: Introduce them gradually and retrain cashiers for new roles
questions.explain: Key: B. Benefits are kept and workers are redeployed. A ignores human cost; B gives up the benefits; D damages trust.

questions.stem: Ms. Greenaway, an insurance clerk, works from home in San Pedro using a laptop, video calls and cloud storage. Which is a DISADVANTAGE for her?
questions.explain: Key: B. Isolation is a key disadvantage; A, B and D are advantages.

questions.stem: Who in a Guyanese bank would back up the customer database, set which staff can access it and tune slow queries?
questions.explain: Key: D. These are core DBA duties. B designs websites, C teaches users, D designs hardware.

questions.stem: A Jamaican hospital hires someone to interview staff, evaluate the current paper process and specify a new computerised system for programmers. This person is a
questions.explain: Key: A. Defining problems and specifying solutions is the analyst's role. The programmer then codes it.

questions.stem: A small hospital in Dominica sends a CT scan at night to a radiologist in Jamaica, who returns a report within an hour. A drawback of this approach is that
options: it is always slower than a local radiologist
the remote radiologist cannot examine the patient and it fails if the Internet is down
CT scans cannot be sent electronically
it requires the patient to fly to Jamaica
questions.explain: Key: B. Teleradiology depends on connectivity and limits follow-up. B, C and D are false.

questions.stem: A Georgetown supermarket's tills scan barcodes and automatically reduce the stock count for each item sold. This is a function of
questions.explain: Key: D. Electronic point of sale records sales and updates stock. The others belong to medicine, design and security.

questions.stem: Tourists point their phones at Fort Zeelandia and see historical images and labels appear over the live camera view. This technology is
questions.explain: Key: C. AR adds digital content to the real world. VR replaces the view entirely; C and D are unrelated.

questions.stem: After a hurricane, the Belizean government wants close-up images of roof damage across several districts quickly and safely. The MOST suitable technology is
questions.explain: Key: B. Drones survey damage quickly without risking people. The others do not capture images.

questions.stem: Tamara is typing a report on Liberta Marina and needs to show the area of a berth as 45 m². Which feature formats the 2 correctly?
questions.explain: Key: B. The 2 in m² is raised above the line: superscript. Subscript (A) lowers text, as in H₂O. Strikethrough (B) crosses text out, and small caps (D) changes letter shapes, not position.

questions.stem: A 12-page SBA report on the San Nicolaas Community Garden needs one wide table printed sideways on page 8 while all other pages stay upright. What must the student insert before and after the table?
questions.explain: Key: B. Orientation belongs to a section, so page 8 needs its own section. Page breaks (A) start a new page without a new section; column breaks (B) are for newsletter columns; text wrapping breaks (C) affect text around objects.

questions.stem: The secretary of the Regent Street Traders Association wants the association's name to appear at the top of every page of a 20-page report automatically. Which feature should she use?
questions.explain: Key: C. A header repeats in the top margin of every page. A footnote (A) sits at the bottom of one page; a heading (C) is a section title, not repeated text; a title page (D) appears once.

questions.stem: Andre formatted ten headings in a 15-page report by hand. His teacher asks him to change all headings to green. Which feature would have let him change all ten in one step?
questions.explain: Key: D. Modifying a style updates every heading using it. Format Painter (C) copies formatting but painted copies do not update later; Find and Replace (B) works on text; word count (D) only counts.

questions.stem: Keisha copies a paragraph from a utility company's web page into her newsletter, but it arrives in a large blue font with a grey background. Which paste option makes it match the newsletter's own formatting?
questions.explain: Key: D. Keep Text Only drops the web page's formatting. Keep Source Formatting (A) keeps the problem; Picture (C) makes it uneditable; Paste link (D) keeps a link to a source file and does not fix formatting.

questions.stem: In the bibliography of an SBA report on Caribbean fisheries, the first line of each reference starts at the margin and the remaining lines are indented. This is a
questions.explain: Key: A. Everything except the first line indented is a hanging indent. A first-line indent (A) indents only line 1; a right indent (C) moves the right edge; justification (B) is alignment, not indentation.

questions.stem: The menu of the Guavaberry Grove Café lists prices such as $4.50, $12.75 and $105.00. Which tab stop lines up the prices on their decimal points?
questions.explain: Key: B. A decimal tab aligns numbers on the point. Left (A) aligns starts, centre (B) centres text, and right (D) aligns the ends, which only works if every price has the same number of decimal places and is a weaker answer.

questions.stem: Kevin replaces every “Manager” with “Supervisor” in a 30-page pharmacy handbook using Replace All with no options set. Afterwards “Management” reads “Supervisorment”. Which option would have prevented this?
questions.explain: Key: D. Whole words only stops matches inside longer words. Match case (B) checks capitals, which does not help here; wildcards (C) and Sounds like (D) widen the search rather than narrowing it.

questions.stem: Jordan's letter says “Please reply buy Friday” and the spelling checker found no errors. Why?
options: “buy” is a real word, so the dictionary check accepts it
The letter is too short to check
questions.explain: Key: B. Spell checkers compare words with a dictionary, so real words used wrongly (buy/by) pass. That is why proofreading is needed. The other options are not how checkers work.

questions.stem: Three teachers at the Sea-Almond Secondary School must suggest edits to the hurricane plan so the principal can accept or reject each one. Which feature should they use?
questions.explain: Key: C. Track Changes records edits for accept/reject. Comments (A) suggest without editing; Mark as Final (C) discourages editing; Format Painter (D) copies formatting.

questions.stem: The office manager of the Otrobanda Hotel wants to make sure front-desk staff cannot OPEN a document listing staff salaries. Which feature is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: C. Only encryption with a password stops the file being opened. Mark as Final (C) and read-only (B) still let anyone read it; Restrict Editing (D) limits changes, not reading.

questions.stem: A permission slip from the Frangipani Hill Academy PTA must let parents tick boxes and type names but not change any wording. Which setting achieves this?
questions.explain: Key: B. Filling in forms allows input only in form controls. Mark as Final (B) blocks normal editing including filling in; Track Changes (A) records but allows any change; encryption (D) controls opening, not editing.

questions.stem: A power cut hits while Dario is typing his SBA. When he restarts Word, it offers a recovered version of his document. Which safety feature saved his work?
questions.explain: Key: D. AutoRecover saves recovery information at intervals (10 minutes by default). AutoCorrect (A) fixes typing errors; the others are unrelated.

questions.stem: Simone wants Word to generate a table of contents for her report on the Antiguan Fisheries Cooperative. What must she do FIRST?
options: Put the headings in a table
Apply heading styles to the headings
questions.explain: Key: C. Word builds a TOC from heading styles. Bold (A) changes appearance only; typed page numbers (C) are unreliable; a table (D) is irrelevant.

questions.stem: After generating a TOC, Marlon adds a new section called “Interviews with Fishers”. Which option should he choose when updating the TOC?
questions.explain: Key: C. New or renamed headings need an entire-table update. Page numbers only (A) misses the new heading; retyping (C) is unnecessary; the TOC does not update itself (B).

questions.stem: In a mail merge of 640 Sports Day letters for Coralstone PTA, the Excel file containing parents' names, addresses and children's forms is called the
questions.explain: Key: C. The list of variable details is the data source (data file). The primary document (B) holds the standard letter; a merge field (C) is a placeholder; the merged document (B) is the output.

questions.stem: Island Water Sports filters its recipient list with: District Equal to Sandy Ground AND Balance Greater than 0. Which customer receives a letter?
questions.explain: Key: A. With AND, both conditions must be true: Sandy Ground and a balance above 0. Options (D) and (C) fail the district condition; option (B) fails the balance condition.

questions.stem: Kezia has set up the first label of a sheet of mailing labels with an Address Block. The other labels show only «Next Record». What should she click next?
questions.explain: Key: B. Update Labels copies the first label's layout to every label. Preview (A) would show mostly blank labels; Greeting Line (C) is for letters; finishing now (B) would print empty labels.

questions.stem: A registration form for the Trinidadian Youth Sports Camp asks for T-shirt size: S, M, L or XL. Which form control is BEST?
questions.explain: Key: B. A drop-down limits answers to valid choices. Plain text (A) allows misspellings; date picker (B) is for dates; picture (D) is for images.

questions.stem: Tanya draws a diagram showing that the home page of the Barbadian Steel Pan Orchestra site links to About, Concerts, Join and Contact. This planning tool is a
questions.explain: Key: D. A site map shows pages and links. A wireframe (B) shows one page's layout; a style sheet (C) holds formatting; a web host (D) provides server space.

questions.stem: Bridgetown Public Library is planning a website for adults over 60. Which design decision BEST suits this intended audience?
options: Large, clear, high-contrast text and simple layouts
Small decorative fonts to fit more on the page
Navigation hidden behind icons with no labels
questions.explain: Key: A. Older readers benefit from large, clear text and simple layouts. The other options reduce readability and usability for this audience.

questions.stem: On the Hellshire Beach Eco Club site, which HTML correctly displays a photo with a suitable text alternative?
options: <img src="cleanup.jpg" alt="Students collecting plastic on Hellshire beach">
questions.explain: Key: C. img needs src (the file) and alt (a meaningful description). Option (A) has no source; option (B) uses the anchor tag wrongly; option (D) uses invalid tag and attribute names.

questions.stem: A student's page shows the words “Cruise ships at Port Zante” instead of the photo after uploading. On her laptop the photo appeared. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The image file was not uploaded or its name/path does not match exactly on the server
The alt text is too long
JPEG images are not allowed on the Web
questions.explain: Key: A. Alt text appears when the browser cannot load the image, usually a missing upload or a case/path mismatch. Alt length (A) never hides images; JPEG (B) is standard; the title (D) affects only the tab.

questions.stem: A student in Charlestown is researching local news for a Nevis heritage project and finds the page http://www.nevispages.com/news.htm. In this URL, what is the domain name?
questions.explain: Key: A. The domain name is nevispages.com; www is not part of it. Option (B) includes the protocol and server name; option (C) is the page file; option (D) is the extension.

questions.stem: Keon finishes the Montserrat Volcano Tours site on his laptop and copies the files to his hosting company's server. Which protocol is normally used for this upload?
questions.explain: Key: D. FTP (File Transfer Protocol) transfers files to the web server. HTTP (A) is used to download pages into a browser; SMTP (C) sends e-mail; DNS (B) translates domain names to IP addresses.

questions.stem: Barbados Reef Divers wants a link that opens a new e-mail to bookings@reefdivers.example.bb. Which href is correct?
questions.explain: Key: D. E-mail links need mailto:. Option (B) is treated as a file path; option (A) jumps to a bookmark; option (C) tries to open a web page.

questions.stem: A long FAQ page for the St. Lucia Jazz Festival has a heading with id="tickets". A link at the top uses href="#Tickets" and does nothing. Why?
options: The bookmark name must match exactly, including capital letters
questions.explain: Key: D. Fragment identifiers are case-sensitive: #Tickets does not match tickets. Bookmarks work on the Web (B); mailto (C) is for e-mail; headings are common bookmark targets (D).

questions.stem: Grenada Spice Co-op website links to a PDF price list that the co-op created. Which type of hyperlink is this?
options: A link to an e-mail address
A link to another web page
A link to a user-created file
questions.explain: Key: D. A PDF the organisation made is a user-created file. The other types go to pages, positions on a page or e-mail.

questions.stem: While evaluating Trinidad Carnival Visitor Guide, a student finds that the fete calendar still shows last year's dates. Which evaluation criterion is MOST affected?
questions.explain: Key: C. Out-of-date information is an accuracy (currency) problem. It does not affect loading speed (B), layout on devices (C) or access for people with disabilities (D).

questions.stem: The home page of the DOM Island Ferry Express site has a 9 MB photo and takes 25 seconds to load on a phone. Which action BEST improves the page?
options: Add alt text to the photo
Resize and compress the photo before uploading
questions.explain: Key: D. Smaller files load faster. Alt text (A) improves accessibility, not speed; the domain (C) and underlining (B) do not affect load time.

questions.stem: Mr. Hodge, treasurer of a St. John’s Carnival troupe, wants totals to update automatically whenever a costume price changes. Which feature of a spreadsheet makes this possible?
questions.explain: Key: A. Formulas recalculate when their input cells change. A and C are word-processing features; D only previews printing.

questions.stem: A Form 4 student opens a worksheet and sees the Name Box showing K12. What does K12 identify?
questions.explain: Key: A. A cell address is the column letter followed by the row number. A reverses them; B and D misread the address.

questions.stem: A teacher at Hummingbird Ridge High School selects the range C3:F10 to format test marks. How many cells are selected?
questions.explain: Key: B. C–F is 4 columns and rows 3–10 is 8 rows: 4 × 8 = 32. A and B miscount the rows; C adds an extra row and column.

questions.stem: In a tuck-shop sheet, cell D4 displays 37.50 but the formula bar shows =B4*C4. Which statement is correct?
options: D4 contains a formula and displays its result
D4 contains a value typed by the user
questions.explain: Key: C. The formula bar shows the true contents; the cell shows the result. C and B ignore the formula; D is not a real fault.

questions.stem: A school stores student ID numbers such as 00427 in a spreadsheet, but they display as 427. How should the IDs be entered so the zeros remain?
options: Type an apostrophe before each ID or format the cells as Text
questions.explain: Key: B. An apostrophe or Text format stores the ID as a label. A, B and D do not stop leading zeros being dropped.

questions.stem: A Grenada farmer's spreadsheet has B2 = 12, C2 = 4 and D2 = 2. What does =B2+C2*D2 display?
questions.explain: Key: D. Multiplication first: 4 × 2 = 8, then 12 + 8 = 20. B adds first; C and D are arithmetic slips.

questions.stem: A student's three test marks are in B5, C5 and D5. Which formula correctly calculates her average?
questions.explain: Key: A. Brackets make the addition happen before division. A divides only D5; C multiplies; B omits C5.

questions.stem: A ferry office lists passenger NAMES in A2:A41. Which formula counts how many passengers are listed?
questions.explain: Key: C. COUNTA counts non-empty cells including text. COUNT counts only numbers (0 here); SUM adds numbers; the COUNTIF criterion tests numbers.

questions.stem: A grade book has averages in F2:F30. Which formula counts the students with an average of 50 or more?
questions.explain: Key: B. COUNTIF needs the range, then the criterion in quotation marks. B lacks quotes; C and D are not valid ways to count.

questions.stem: A credit union pays a $25 bonus to members whose savings in C4 are at least $1,000; otherwise nothing. Which formula is correct?
questions.explain: Key: D. 'At least' means >=. A excludes exactly $1,000; C returns text instead of numbers; B reverses the test.

questions.stem: A Little Bay hardware store's order form uses =VLOOKUP(E2,$A$2:$C$50,3,FALSE). A cashier types a code that is not in the price list. What appears?
questions.explain: Key: C. With FALSE (exact match), a missing code returns #N/A. D would happen only with TRUE; A and C are not VLOOKUP's response.

questions.stem: Swim times are in B2:B9; the fastest (smallest) time should be ranked 1st. Which formula in C2 can be copied down?
questions.explain: Key: B. Order 1 ranks ascending, and the list is locked. A ranks the slowest first; B's range slides when copied; D always ranks the first swimmer.

questions.stem: A librarian's sheet has a due date in C2 and today's date in D2. Which formula shows how many days the book is overdue?
questions.explain: Key: C. Today minus the due date gives days late. A gives a negative number for overdue books; C is meaningless; B lacks brackets and a calculation.

questions.stem: Kayla is calculating the average rainfall for a Barbados weather project and types =AVERGE(B2:B12) into cell B13. What will the cell display?
questions.explain: Key: A. A misspelt function name gives #NAME?. The other errors have different causes.

questions.stem: In an English Harbour car-rental sheet, cell E2 contains =C2*D2 (days × daily rate). The clerk copies it to E7. What does E7 contain?
questions.explain: Key: D. Relative references move five rows down with the formula. B would need absolute references; C and D miscount.

questions.stem: A duty-free shop stores the exchange rate in B1. Prices are in A4:A30. Which formula in B4 converts a price and can be copied down?
questions.explain: Key: A. The price moves; the rate is locked. A's rate slides to empty cells; B and D lock the price.

questions.stem: Ravi is building a two-way ticket-price table for a Carnival fete and needs a reference in which only the COLUMN is locked. Which reference should he use?
questions.explain: Key: A. The $ sits before the letter D. A locks the row; C locks both; D locks neither.

questions.stem: A sales sheet's total in B12 is =SUM(B2:B11). A new row is inserted above row 6. What is the total now?
questions.explain: Key: B. The total moves down a row and the range grows to include the new row.

questions.stem: A roster of 400 volunteers has headings in row 1 and names in column A. Which cell should be selected before View ▸ Freeze Panes to keep both visible?
questions.explain: Key: A. Freeze Panes freezes rows above and columns to the left of the active cell.

questions.stem: A commission rate of 15% must be stored so formulas work. A cell holds the number 15 and the % button is clicked. What is displayed?
questions.explain: Key: D. Percentage format multiplies the display by 100: 15 becomes 1500%. Type 15% or 0.15 instead.

questions.stem: A Trinidad bakery's spreadsheet has 2.456 stored in A1, formatted to show 2 decimal places. The baker enters =A1*100 in B1. What does B1 return?
questions.explain: Key: A. Formulas use the stored value 2.456, not the displayed 2.46.

questions.stem: The Basseterre cruise port tour list is sorted by Tour (A to Z) and then by Price (largest to smallest). What is Price in this sort?
questions.explain: Key: B. The second sort field orders records within each tour.

questions.stem: Leon selects only the Scores column of a class list and sorts it, ignoring Excel's warning. What is the result?
options: Scores no longer match the students' names
questions.explain: Key: C. Only one column moves, splitting the records apart.

questions.stem: A stock list has an AutoFilter showing Warehouse = Montego Bay and Qty less than 20. Which records are displayed?
options: Montego Bay items that also have fewer than 20
Only the first 20 Montego Bay items
Montego Bay items OR items with fewer than 20
questions.explain: Key: A. Filters on different fields are combined with AND.

questions.stem: In an Advanced Filter criteria range, 'Paint' is typed under Category on one row and '<10' under Qty on the NEXT row. Which records are extracted?
options: Paint items OR any item with fewer than 10
questions.explain: Key: C. Criteria on different rows are joined with OR.

questions.stem: A supermarket chain wants total sales for each store and each month from 40,000 sales records, and to rearrange the summary easily. Which tool is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. A pivot table groups and summarises large lists and can be rearranged by dragging fields.

questions.stem: The Meteorological Department wants to show how rainfall changed each month from June to November. Which chart is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: D. Change over time is best shown by a line chart.

questions.stem: A family wants a chart showing what share of their income goes to rent, food, transport and savings. Which chart is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: D. Parts of one whole: a pie chart.

questions.stem: A summary sheet must show cell B5 from a sheet named Feb. Which formula is correct?
questions.explain: Key: A. The sheet name, an exclamation mark, then the cell.

questions.stem: A workbook has sheets Jan, Feb, Mar and Apr in that order, each with total sales in D10. Which formula on a Summary sheet adds all four?
questions.explain: Key: C. A 3-D reference: first sheet:last sheet!cell.

questions.stem: St. Lucian Ferry Line keeps passenger names, sailings and seat bookings in organised, related tables that staff can search and update. What is this collection of data called?
questions.explain: Key: D. An organised collection of related data is a database; a DBMS is the software that manages it.

questions.stem: A clinic in Grand Anse installs Microsoft Access to build tables, run queries and print reports. Microsoft Access is BEST described as:
questions.explain: Key: A. Access is DBMS software; the clinic's records are the database.

questions.stem: Before computers, the Island Reads Library kept a drawer of cards, one per book, sorted by title. This drawer is an example of:
questions.explain: Key: C. Paper-based organised records are a manual database.

questions.stem: A Carnival troupe stores each member's phone number on every costume row of one spreadsheet. When a member changes her number, some rows are updated and others are not. This problem is called:
questions.explain: Key: A. Redundant copies that now disagree show data inconsistency.

questions.stem: In the tblGuest at a Montego Bay hotel there are 7 columns and 40 rows of guest data. Each row is called a:
questions.explain: Key: D. A row holding all the data about one guest is a record (tuple).

questions.stem: A school database table has columns StudentID, FirstName, LastName and Form. The column LastName is BEST described as a:
questions.explain: Key: B. A column is a field (attribute).

questions.stem: Island Power, an electricity company, stores customer telephone numbers such as 542-1187. Which data type should the Phone field have?
questions.explain: Key: C. Phone numbers contain dashes and are never calculated, so Text.

questions.stem: Wallblake Road Pharmacy records whether each prescription has been collected. Which data type is MOST suitable for the Collected field?
questions.explain: Key: D. Only two possible values: logical Yes/No.

questions.stem: Anguilla Ferry Line's PASSENGER table includes Name, DateOfBirth, Nationality and PassportNo. Which field is the MOST suitable primary key?
questions.explain: Key: A. Passport numbers are unique to each traveller; the others repeat.

questions.stem: In a CXC results table, StudentNo and SubjectCode together uniquely identify each record. This primary key is called a:
questions.explain: Key: C. Two or more fields forming the primary key together make a composite key.

questions.stem: In Castries Youth League, PLAYER (PlayerID, Name, TeamID) and TEAM (TeamID, TeamName, Coach). In PLAYER, TeamID is a:
questions.explain: Key: B. TeamID is TEAM's primary key placed in PLAYER to link the tables.

questions.stem: In the PLAYER and TEAM tables of a youth league, each team has many players and each player plays for one team. The relationship from TEAM to PLAYER is:
questions.explain: Key: A. One team, many players: one-to-many with TEAM on the one side.

questions.stem: Students at Seagrape Bay Secondary School can join many clubs and each club has many students. How should this be represented in a relational database?
options: Put ClubID in the STUDENT table
Create a linking table with StudentID and ClubID
Put StudentID in the CLUB table
Store everything in one flat file
questions.explain: Key: B. Many-to-many relationships are resolved with a linking (junction) table.

questions.stem: A Grenada swim club's validation rule for Age must allow members from 8 to 17 years old inclusive. Which rule is correct?
questions.explain: Key: D. Between includes both ends; the Or version accepts every number.

questions.stem: A school's tblStudent has a House field that must contain Red, Blue or Gold only. Which validation rule is correct?
questions.explain: Key: C. In checks against a list of allowed values.

questions.stem: Gros Islet Car Rentals uses the input mask 000\-0000 on its Phone field. What does the 0 mean in this mask?
questions.explain: Key: A. 0 = digit required; 9 = digit optional; L = letter required.

questions.stem: Referential integrity is enforced between tblMember and tblLoan at a library with no cascade options. Which action will Access REFUSE?
options: Adding a loan for a MemberID that does not exist
Deleting a member who has no loans
Adding a new member with no loans
questions.explain: Key: A. A foreign key value must match an existing primary key: no orphan records.

questions.stem: Cascade Delete Related Records is ticked between tblCustomer and tblRental. A clerk deletes a customer who has six rentals. What happens?
options: The rentals are moved to another customer
The customer and the six rentals are deleted
questions.explain: Key: B. Cascade Delete removes the related child records too.

questions.stem: A volunteer reduces the Field Size of a Short Text field District from 20 to 5. The field holds Georgetown. After accepting the warning, what is stored?
questions.explain: Key: A. Longer values are truncated to the new field size.

questions.stem: Using the Island Reads tblBook, a query has Genre: "Fiction" and Price: >20 on the same Criteria row. Which books are returned?
questions.explain: Key: B. Criteria on the same row are joined with AND.

questions.stem: A Trinidad bookshop query has "Poetry" in the Criteria row under Genre and "Drama" in the or row under Genre. Which records are returned?
options: Books that are both Poetry and Drama
questions.explain: Key: A. Separate rows are joined with OR.

questions.stem: Island Reads books cost $24.50, $45.00, $18.75, $32.00, $15.00, $28.00, $21.00, $39.99, $19.50, $26.00, $35.50 and $12.00. How many does the criterion Between 20 And 30 return?
questions.explain: Key: C. $24.50, $28.00, $21.00 and $26.00: four prices from 20 to 30.

questions.stem: A music shop in Barbados wants every song title containing the word Island anywhere. Which criterion should be entered under Title?
questions.explain: Key: C. Stars on both sides match the word anywhere in the title.

questions.stem: A Jamaican tuck shop query has the fields Quantity and UnitPrice. Which entry in the Field row correctly calculates each line's total?
questions.explain: Key: A. Name, colon, then the expression with field names in square brackets.

questions.stem: The librarian wants a query that asks "Which genre?" each time it runs. What should be typed in the Criteria row under Genre?
questions.explain: Key: C. A prompt in square brackets creates a parameter query.

questions.stem: A teacher shows the class this statement: SELECT Title FROM tblBook WHERE Price < 20 ORDER BY Title; Which part sets the condition the records must meet?
questions.explain: Key: C. WHERE holds the criteria; ORDER BY sorts.

questions.stem: A dive shop receptionist enters new customers one at a time on a screen with labels, drop-down lists and a Save button. This Access object is a:
questions.explain: Key: D. Forms are designed for entering and viewing data.

questions.stem: A school secretary wants one screen showing a form class at the top and a list of all its students underneath, changing as she moves between classes. She needs:
questions.explain: Key: B. A main form (one side) with a subform (many side) shows related records.

questions.stem: In a Carnival committee report grouped by Section, where should =Sum([Fee]) be placed to show the total fees for EACH section?
questions.explain: Key: B. Per-group totals go in the group footer; a grand total goes in the Report Footer.

questions.stem: Kayla's SBA report about the Frigate Bay Hotel is titled "Report1". According to the SBA mark scheme, what should she do to earn full marks for the title?
options: Leave it, since any title earns full marks
Use the query name as the title
Replace it with a specific title such as Frigate Bay Hotel: Bookings by Room Type, October 2026
questions.explain: Key: D. A correct, specific title earns 2 marks; a generic title earns at most 1.

questions.stem: Before building a lunch ordering app for Hummingbird Ridge High School, Kayla interviews the tuck shop manager to find out exactly what is needed. Which problem-solving step is she carrying out?
questions.explain: Key: A. Understanding what is needed is defining the problem. B and C come later; D is the final step.

questions.stem: A Form 4 class breaks the problem 'clean the dirty classroom' into Input (broom, mop), Processing (sweep, mop) and Output (clean classroom). Which step is this?
questions.explain: Key: C. Breaking a problem into IPO is analysis. A suggests alternatives; C checks the final solution; D codes it.

questions.stem: A Nevis ferry company compares a paper list, an offline app and a cloud website, then picks the offline app because the terminal often has no Internet. This choice is called:
questions.explain: Key: D. Choosing the best solution with a justification. B is the first step; C tests algorithms; D adds detail.

questions.stem: A team designing a Carnival band app draws a diagram with 'Band Registration System' in the top box and 'Register member', 'Take deposit' and 'Print list' underneath. What is this diagram?
questions.explain: Key: A. Modules in a hierarchy. A uses symbols and arrows; B records variable values; D has three columns.

questions.stem: Your teacher asks for an IPO table to accept the price of an item and display a 17% VAT. Which entry belongs in the PROCESSING column?
questions.explain: Key: A. Calculations are processing. A is input; B is output; D is irrelevant.

questions.stem: A program for a Gros Islet marina uses RATE ← 3.25 throughout, and the value never changes while the program runs. RATE is best described as a:
questions.explain: Key: A. A fixed value during the run is a constant. A can change; C ends input; D counts.

questions.stem: A Barbados dive shop stores each customer's phone number, such as +1 246 555 0187. Which data type is most suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. It contains + and spaces and is never used in arithmetic. A and B would lose symbols; D holds only TRUE/FALSE.

questions.stem: In an algorithm for a Montego Bay shop, the value '335' is written in single quotation marks. What data type is it?
questions.explain: Key: C. Several characters in quotes form a string. A and B would be unquoted numbers; C is one character.

questions.stem: Jaheim is choosing variable names for a cricket scoring program in Pascal. Which identifier is INVALID?
questions.explain: Key: A. Identifiers cannot start with a digit. A, B and D follow the rules.

questions.stem: A student lists these as characteristics of a good algorithm for a SKELEC bill program. Which is NOT a characteristic?
options: It can be interpreted in many different ways
It has a finite number of steps
questions.explain: Key: B. Steps must have exactly one meaning. A, B and D are all characteristics.

questions.stem: In the pseudocode, which statement is a PROMPTING statement for a library fines program?
options: Write "Enter the number of days late"
questions.explain: Key: C. A prompt uses Write to ask for data. A is input; C is assignment; D is selection.

questions.stem: Which symbol is used for assignment in Pascal, as in the SBA programs written at Frangipani Hill Academy?
questions.explain: Key: C. Pascal uses :=. A is pseudocode; C is Python comparison; D means not equal.

questions.stem: During a desk check of a calculation for a Jamaican hardware store, what is stored in Total by the line Total ← 6 + 4 * 2 ^ 2?
questions.explain: Key: C. Powers first: 2 ^ 2 = 4; then 4 * 4 = 16; then 6 + 16 = 22. B ignores BODMAS; C and D apply the operations in the wrong order.

questions.stem: A Weather Club program tests IF rainfall > 20 AND wind > 50 THEN. On a day with 25 mm of rain and wind of 40 km/h, the condition is:
options: TRUE, because one part is enough
FALSE, because both parts must be TRUE for AND
questions.explain: Key: C. 40 > 50 is FALSE, so the AND is FALSE. A and C describe OR; D: both values are given.

questions.stem: Using Boolean logic, a student evaluates NOT (TRUE OR FALSE) for a Paper 01 revision question. What is the result?
questions.explain: Key: B. TRUE OR FALSE = TRUE; NOT TRUE = FALSE. A and C are the value before NOT; D: it can be evaluated.

questions.stem: A raffle program at Breadfruit Valley Secondary uses FOR NUM = 10 TO 100 STEP 10 DO. How many times does the loop body run?
questions.explain: Key: D. 10, 20, …, 100 is ten values. A misses one end; C adds one; D ignores STEP.
