questions.stem: A cruise passenger program reads counts until the operator types 0, and some days there are no ships. Which loop is most suitable?
questions.explain: Key: A. Unknown number of repetitions, possibly zero: a pre-test WHILE loop. A needs a known count; C always runs once; D is not a loop.

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of times the body of a REPEAT … UNTIL loop runs in a PIN-checking program for an ATM on Fort Street?
options: It depends on a FOR counter
questions.explain: Key: D. The condition is tested after the body. A describes WHILE; C and B are wrong.

questions.stem: Trace this algorithm from a Sea-Almond Secondary School worksheet: x ← 4; y ← x * 3; x ← y − x; Write x, y. What is output?
questions.explain: Key: D. y = 12; x = 12 − 4 = 8. A uses the old x; C swaps them; D uses the wrong y.

questions.stem: Trace: t ← 0; FOR i = 2 TO 6 STEP 2 DO t ← t + i ENDFOR; Write t. This is from a fundraiser tally for a Trinidad school. What is output?
questions.explain: Key: C. i = 2, 4, 6; t = 12. A stops early; C adds all numbers 2–6; A is wrong.

questions.stem: Trace: n ← 20; c ← 0; WHILE n > 3 DO n ← n DIV 2; c ← c + 1 ENDWHILE; Write c, n. What is output?
questions.explain: Key: C. n: 20 → 10 → 5 → 2 (three passes); 2 > 3 is FALSE. A stops one pass early; C goes one too far; D mixes values.

questions.stem: A Grand Anse swim club accepts members aged 8 to 16 inclusive. Which pair of values are BOTH boundary test data?
questions.explain: Key: D. 8 is the lower edge and 17 is just above the upper edge. A is normal; C is erroneous; D mixes normal and erroneous.

questions.stem: A commission algorithm should pay 5% on sales MORE THAN $50,000 but uses IF sales >= 50000 THEN. The program runs without crashing. What type of error is this?
questions.explain: Key: B. It runs but gives a wrong result for exactly $50,000. A stops translation; B crashes; D: it is wrong.

questions.stem: Which flowchart symbol should contain 'Read Gallons' in a flowchart for a water company?
questions.explain: Key: D. Input uses the parallelogram. A is Start/Stop; C is processing; D is a decision.

questions.stem: In a flowchart for a Providenciales Airport baggage robot, a diamond 'Is weight <> 0?' sits above the loop body, and an arrow from the end of the body returns to it. Which pseudocode structure does this show?
questions.explain: Key: D. A decision before the body with a loop-back is a pre-test WHILE loop. A has no loop-back; C tests after the body; D needs a counter.

questions.stem: Kaya the Robo Lab rover faces East at (0, 0) and runs [drive forward (3)] [turn left (90)] [drive forward (2)]. Where does she finish?
questions.explain: Key: D. East 3 to (3, 0); left turn faces North; up 2 to (3, 2). B swaps coordinates; C turns the wrong way; D forgets the turn.

questions.stem: A beach clean-up robot program uses the block [repeat (10)]. Which CXC pseudocode structure matches it?
questions.explain: Key: A. A fixed number of repeats is a bounded FOR loop. A is selection; C and D never stop.

questions.stem: A Scratch-style program for a baggage robot at John A. Osborne Airport uses [repeat until <belt empty?>]. Because Scratch tests this condition BEFORE each pass, the matching pseudocode is:
questions.explain: Key: A. A pre-test loop that continues while the condition is FALSE. A always runs once; C and D are not suitable.

questions.stem: A relief robot team defines a custom block [define deliver supplies (packs)] and uses it at three shelters in Moengo. Which is the main benefit?
options: The routine is written once and reused, so fixes are made in one place
It removes the need for testing
questions.explain: Key: A. Modules give reuse and easier maintenance. A is unrelated; C is false; D describes files.

questions.stem: Trace: p ← 3; q ← 5; p ← p + q; q ← p − q; p ← p − q; Write p, q. This swaps values without a temporary variable. What is output?
questions.explain: Key: D. p = 8; q = 8 − 5 = 3; p = 8 − 3 = 5. C is the original; C and D stop part-way.

questions.stem: A technician at the Bay Volt Engineering writes instructions such as LDA 10 and ADD 11 for a meter chip. Which type of language is he using?
questions.explain: Key: C. LDA and ADD are mnemonics, used in assembly language (2GL). Machine code is binary; 4GLs and natural languages are high-level.

questions.stem: Kenya says her Python program will run on both her Windows laptop and her friend's Mac after translation. Which feature of high-level languages does this describe?
questions.explain: Key: C. High-level source code is portable: it can be translated for different machines. The other options describe low-level languages.

questions.stem: The Sauteurs Credit Union needs a list of all members whose loans are overdue, produced by stating WHAT data is wanted. Which generation of language is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: B. A 4GL such as SQL states the result wanted; 3GLs need step-by-step instructions; 1GL and 2GL are low-level.

questions.stem: Island Byte Studios sells a game as a single .exe file so that customers never see its source code. Which translator produced the file?
questions.explain: Key: A. A compiler translates the whole program into object code, which is linked into an executable. An interpreter produces no executable; an assembler handles assembly language.

questions.stem: When Jaden runs his Python program, lines 1 to 6 print their results and then the program stops on line 7 with an error. Which translator behaviour explains this?
options: An interpreter translates and runs one statement at a time
The program was compiled into an executable first
questions.explain: Key: A. Interpreters execute statements as they translate them, so earlier lines run before the faulty one is reached.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the CORRECT order of the stages in implementing a program?
options: Testing and executing, create source code, linking, interpreting and compiling, maintaining
Interpreting and compiling, create source code, linking, maintaining, testing and executing
Create source code, interpreting and compiling, linking, testing and executing, maintaining
Create source code, linking, interpreting and compiling, testing and executing, maintaining
questions.explain: Key: C. Source code is created, translated, linked into an executable, run and tested, then maintained.

questions.stem: Shanice's Pascal program compiles, but every exam mark of exactly 50 is shown as Fail. The code says If mark > 50 Then WriteLn('Pass'). What type of error is this?
questions.explain: Key: D. The program runs and finishes but gives a wrong result: a logic error caused by > instead of >=.

questions.stem: A program for the Frigate Bay Grill divides the night's tips by the number of staff. On a night when 0 staff are entered, it crashes. This is BEST described as a:
options: logic error that the compiler detected
questions.explain: Key: D. Division by zero happens while the program is running: a run-time error.

questions.stem: A program accepts the number of tickets for a ferry booking, from 1 to 20. Which set contains ONLY boundary test data?
questions.explain: Key: A. 1 and 20 are the edges of the valid range. 7 and 12 are normal; the others are erroneous.

questions.stem: Before typing his program, Rohan works through his algorithm by hand, recording the value of each variable after every step. Which manual test is he performing?
options: A dry run using a trace table
questions.explain: Key: D. Working through an algorithm by hand with a trace table is a dry run (desk check).

questions.stem: A school's program must store whether each student has returned a permission slip. The MOST suitable data type is:
questions.explain: Key: D. Returned or not returned: only two values, so Boolean.

questions.stem: Malik is naming the variables in his Pascal program for the Grand Anse library's book-loan system. Which of these is a VALID Pascal identifier?
questions.explain: Key: D. Identifiers start with a letter or underscore, contain no spaces and are not reserved words; begin is reserved.

questions.stem: Sunrise Bakery sells each coconut tart for $3.50. Which Pascal statement correctly assigns 3.50 to the variable Unit_Price?
questions.explain: Key: C. Pascal's assignment operator is := and the statement ends with a semicolon.

questions.stem: Devon's Python program reads two scores with input() and adds them. Entering 5 and 3 prints 53. What is the cause?
options: The inputs are strings and + joins them; int() is needed
questions.explain: Key: C. input() returns text; + concatenates strings. Converting with int() fixes the logic error.

questions.stem: What is displayed by the Pascal statement WriteLn(17 Mod 5, ' ', 17 Div 5); ?
questions.explain: Key: B. 17 Mod 5 is the remainder 2; 17 Div 5 is the whole-number quotient 3.

questions.stem: Kenya's Pascal program will not compile: If mark >= 50 Then WriteLn('Pass'); Else WriteLn('Fail'); What must she change?
questions.explain: Key: A. In Pascal a semicolon ends the If statement, so an Else after it is a syntax error.

questions.stem: The hurricane program tests wind >= 74 FIRST, then wind >= 96, wind >= 111 and so on. What category does it report for a 140 mph storm?
questions.explain: Key: C. The first true condition wins; 140 >= 74 is true, so it reports Category 1. The tests must start with the highest threshold.

questions.stem: At the Young Street Phones shop, a customer's record holds age = 15 and member = 'Y'. Which condition is TRUE for this customer?
questions.explain: Key: B. OR needs only one true part; member = 'Y' is true. The others are all false.

questions.stem: A program for the English Harbour Market must repeat a set of instructions exactly 25 times, once for each stall. Which loop construct is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Key: C. A known number of repetitions is bounded iteration: the FOR loop.

questions.stem: A menu at the Bridgetown ferry office must be displayed at least once and repeated until the user chooses Exit. Which construct is BEST?
options: REPEAT … UNTIL, tested at the bottom
questions.explain: Key: A. REPEAT … UNTIL always runs its body at least once.

questions.stem: count ← 0; FOR i ← 1 TO 10 DO IF i MOD 3 = 0 THEN count ← count + 1 ENDIF ENDFOR; Write count. What is written?
questions.explain: Key: C. i = 3, 6 and 9 are multiples of 3, so count is 3.

questions.stem: Tamara's program should total five prices but prints only the last one. Inside her FOR loop she has total ← 0 followed by total ← total + price. What is wrong?
options: The loop runs too few times
total is re-initialised on every pass; it should be set to 0 before the loop
The output is inside the loop
questions.explain: Key: C. Initialising inside the loop resets the accumulator each time.

questions.stem: A WHILE loop adds ages until 0 is entered. The inputs are 15, 16, 14 and 0. How many times is the loop body executed?
questions.explain: Key: A. 15, 16 and 14 are processed; 0 fails the test at the top, so the body runs 3 times.

questions.stem: Mr. Hodge stores the test scores of his Form 5 class at Bayleaf Hill Secondary using the Pascal declaration scores : Array[1..30] Of Integer; This declaration creates:
questions.explain: Key: D. The index range 1..30 gives thirty elements, all of type Integer.

questions.stem: A program searches an UNSORTED list of 200 employee numbers for one number. Which search method can be used?
options: Binary search after deleting half the list
questions.explain: Key: C. Binary search requires sorted data; linear search works on any order.

questions.stem: In Excel VBA, a teacher writes Do While Cells(r, 2) <> "" … r = r + 1 … Loop, starting at r = 2. What does the loop do?
options: Reads row 2 from column B across
Reads column B from row 2 down until an empty cell
Deletes every cell in column B
questions.explain: Key: C. Cells(r, 2) is column B; r increases each pass until an empty cell is reached.

questions.stem: Shanice is preparing the documentation for her SBA program, the Troupe Registration system for a Carnival band. Which item is an example of EXTERNAL documentation?
options: A user guide explaining how to register a member
A comment beside the fee calculation
questions.explain: Key: B. External documentation is for users; the others are internal documentation for programmers.

questions.stem: A procedure-head comment in Mr. Hodge's SBA example lists the purpose, author, date created and date modified. Which category of internal documentation is this?
questions.explain: Key: D. Author, dates and purpose belong in the procedure (program) head.

questions.stem: The beach clean-up algorithm is rewritten from Pascal into JavaScript. Which of the following changes?
questions.explain: Key: C. Logic stays the same; syntax such as keywords and punctuation changes.

questions.stem: Rohan is converting the beach clean-up pseudocode into a flowchart for his SBA. For the statement Read weight, which flowchart symbol must he use?
questions.explain: Key: C. Input and output are shown with parallelograms; rectangles are processes, diamonds decisions, terminators Start/Stop.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: A careers officer visiting Flamboyant Heights College asks students to define IT. Which answer is MOST complete?
options: Using computers to play games and watch videos
Using computers and telecommunications to capture, store, process, retrieve and transmit information
The repair of computers and printers
questions.explain: IT combines the technology (computers and telecommunications) with what it does to data and information. The other answers are either one small use or far too broad.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: Your teacher writes ICT on the board instead of IT. What does the extra C emphasise?
questions.explain: ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology. It stresses networks, phones, the Internet and messaging.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: At a King George V Street jewellery shop, which item is SOFTWARE in its IT system?
questions.explain: A program is software. The printer is hardware, the assistant is people and the prices are data.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: The rule "Back up the sales file to the cloud every evening before closing" is an example of which level of the ICT Components Hierarchy?
questions.explain: A rule or step that people follow is a procedure.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: A teacher's spreadsheet shows a student averaging 245% because one test score was typed as 950 instead of 95. Which term describes this?
questions.explain: Garbage In, Garbage Out: the computer processed incorrect input correctly and produced incorrect output.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: The CXC multiple-choice answer sheets for thousands of candidates are marked by machine in a fraction of the time humans would take. Which strength of computers does this MOST show?
questions.explain: Processing large volumes quickly is speed. Computers do not have human judgement or creativity.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: During a power cut in Portsmouth, a supermarket cannot use its tills even though the software is working. Which limitation of computers does this show?
questions.explain: Computers cannot work without power. A UPS or generator reduces this risk.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: A regional weather service wants to model the path and strength of a hurricane over the next five days. Which type of computer is BEST suited?
questions.explain: Weather modelling needs enormous numbers of calculations: a supercomputer.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: A bank with branches on six Caribbean islands must process millions of card transactions daily with near-zero downtime. Which type of computer is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Huge volumes of transactions and many simultaneous users, with high reliability, is the job of a mainframe.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: A science article says a new supercomputer can perform over a billion billion floating-point operations each second. Which unit measures this?
questions.explain: Supercomputer speed is measured in FLOPS (floating-point operations per second). An exaflop is 10<sup>18</sup> FLOPS.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: Which device in a hotel room in Canefield is MOST likely to contain an embedded system?
options: The digital safe with a keypad
questions.explain: A digital safe has a small dedicated computer that checks the code and controls the lock.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: Which statement about an embedded system is TRUE?
options: It is always larger than a desktop
It can run any program the user installs
It is a dedicated computer that controls one device or task
It must be connected to a monitor and keyboard
questions.explain: Embedded systems do a dedicated job inside another device and usually have no general user interface.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: A coach at a Caribbean football academy wants to track each player's heart rate and distance run during training. Which device is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Wearables use sensors on the body to track heart rate and movement.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: Which is a disadvantage of a laptop compared with a desktop of the same price?
options: It is usually less powerful and harder to upgrade
It cannot run on a battery
questions.explain: To stay thin and cool, laptops use lower-power parts that are harder to upgrade.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: Which computer type has the GREATEST portability?
questions.explain: A smartphone fits in a pocket and runs on a battery. Of these, it is the most portable.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: Which component in a game console is MOST responsible for producing detailed 3D graphics?
questions.explain: The GPU is a specialised processor for rendering graphics.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: A Carnival committee used to add up thousands of ticket sales by hand. Which is the MAIN advantage of switching to automated information processing?
options: It is faster and more accurate for large volumes of data
It can use human judgement for unusual cases
It costs nothing to set up
questions.explain: Automated processing handles large volumes quickly and consistently. It needs power, costs money to set up and cannot use human judgement.

questions.topic: What is IT? Types of computers
questions.stem: A juice factory in Trinidad keeps its pasteuriser at exactly 72 °C with no operator present. Which feature is ESSENTIAL for this process control system?
questions.explain: Process control needs sensor input, real-time processing and output to control devices.

questions.stem: A spreadsheet at the Sunrise Bakery checks whether each day's sales are greater than US$500. Which part of the CPU carries out this comparison?
questions.explain: Comparisons and calculations are done by the ALU.

questions.stem: Which part of the CPU fetches instructions from memory, decodes them and coordinates the other components?
questions.explain: The Control Unit is the CPU's manager.

questions.stem: Where does the CPU hold the data it is working on at this very instant?
questions.explain: Registers are tiny, very fast storage locations inside the CPU.

questions.stem: Tiana is typing her SBA in Word when a Barbados Light and Power power cut switches off her desktop. She had not saved for 20 minutes. Why is that work lost?
options: It was in RAM, which is volatile
It was in ROM, which is read-only
questions.explain: Unsaved work is held in RAM, which loses its contents when power is lost.

questions.stem: Which of these is MOST likely to be stored in ROM?
options: The instructions that start up the computer
questions.explain: ROM holds firmware such as the boot instructions.

questions.stem: A laptop advert says the processor has '24 MB cache'. What is the purpose of cache memory?
options: To hold frequently used instructions and data close to the CPU so it works faster
To store files permanently when the power is off
questions.explain: Cache reduces the time the CPU waits for data from slower RAM.

questions.stem: How many bits are in one byte?
questions.explain: 1 byte = 8 bits.

questions.stem: Jamal's game download is 3 GB. How many megabytes is that? (Use 1 GB = 1,024 MB.)
A tour company's promo photos are 5 MB each. How many fit on a 1 GB memory card? (1 GB = 1,024 MB; give the whole number.)
questions.explain: 1,024 ÷ 5 = 204.8, so 204 complete photos fit.

questions.stem: Which of these is the LARGEST unit of storage?
questions.explain: KB < MB < GB < TB < PB.

questions.stem: A regional bank keeps a copy of all its records for 10 years in a vault in another country. Which medium is MOST suitable for this archive?
questions.explain: Tape has very high capacity, low cost per GB and long shelf life, ideal for archives.

questions.stem: Why do most new laptops use an SSD rather than an HDD?
options: SSDs are faster and have no moving parts
SSDs need a laser to read them
questions.explain: Speed, low power and robustness are the main advantages; SSDs cost more per GB.

questions.stem: Roughly how much can a single-layer DVD hold?
questions.explain: CD ≈ 700 MB, DVD ≈ 4.7 GB, single-layer Blu-ray ≈ 25 GB.

questions.stem: At a GAIA self check-in kiosk, a passenger's boarding pass is printed. Which stage of the IPOS cycle is this?
questions.explain: Printing presents information to the user: output.

questions.stem: In the IPOS cycle, why is the arrow between processing and storage drawn in BOTH directions?
options: Because the CPU is inside the hard drive
Because storage is part of the output
Because storage devices are also input devices
Because data is saved to storage and also retrieved from it for processing
questions.explain: Data is saved to storage and later retrieved to be processed again.

questions.stem: After a storm, Holetown has electricity but no Internet for three days. Which business is MOST affected?
options: One that stores files on its office PC's SSD
One that stores all its files only in the cloud
One that uses an external HDD for backups
questions.explain: Cloud-only storage cannot be reached without an Internet connection.

questions.stem: A technician says the firmware chip in an old machine can be wiped by shining ultraviolet light on it and then reprogrammed. What type of memory is this?
questions.explain: EPROM is Erasable Programmable ROM, wiped with ultraviolet light. PROM can be programmed only once.

questions.stem: Keisha sends a 40-page document to print and immediately carries on typing while the printer works. What makes this possible?
options: A buffer that temporarily holds the print data
questions.explain: The buffer holds data waiting to be printed, so the CPU is free to continue.

questions.stem: The Holetown Youth Centre wants to connect a laptop to a projector to show a video with sound. Which port is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: HDMI carries both video and sound to displays and projectors.

questions.stem: A backup tape holds records with track numbers 16, 25, 34, 45, 59, 60 and 78 in that order. What must happen to read the record on track 34?
options: The tape must be formatted first
Track 34 cannot be read from tape
The drive jumps straight to track 34
The drive must wind past the records on tracks 16 and 25 first
questions.explain: Tape uses sequential access: data is retrieved in the order it was stored, so earlier records must be passed first.

questions.stem: Which term describes a set of matched tracks, for example track 3, on all the platters of a hard disk?
questions.explain: A cylinder is the same track on every platter; storing a file on one cylinder avoids moving the heads.

questions.stem: A factory receives blank memory chips and programs its machine instructions onto them once, using a special burner. The contents can never be changed. Which type of memory is this?
questions.explain: PROM is manufactured blank and written once using a PROM programmer (burner).

questions.stem: Your CXC Paper 01 answer sheet is marked by a machine that detects which bubble you shaded. Which technology is this?
questions.explain: OMR detects marks in fixed positions.

questions.stem: A bank in Georgetown processes cheques. The numbers at the bottom are printed in special ink so they can be read even if stamped over. Which technology reads them?
questions.explain: Magnetic Ink Character Recognition reads magnetic ink characters on cheques.

questions.stem: A newspaper archive wants to turn scanned pages of 1990s editions into searchable text. Which technology is needed?
questions.explain: OCR converts images of printed characters into editable text.

questions.stem: A restaurant in Hopkins puts a square black-and-white code on each table. Diners point their phone camera at it to open the menu. What is this?
questions.explain: A QR code is a 2-D code read by a camera; it often holds a web address.

questions.stem: A Carnival troupe designer wants to draw costume designs naturally on the computer, with lines that get thicker when she presses harder. What should she use?
questions.explain: Graphics tablets detect stylus pressure for natural drawing.

questions.stem: A weather station at Hato Airport must record air pressure every minute, day and night. What kind of input device is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Sensors measure physical quantities automatically and continuously.

questions.stem: Why does a temperature sensor connected to a computer often need an analogue-to-digital converter?
options: Because the sensor's signal is analogue but the computer processes digital data
To store the readings in the cloud
questions.explain: Computers process digital values, so the continuous analogue signal must be converted.

questions.stem: Why is chip-and-PIN more secure than a magnetic stripe card?
options: The chip creates unique transaction codes and the PIN confirms the cardholder
Chip cards never need a network
questions.explain: Unique codes make cloning hard and the PIN proves identity.

questions.stem: A clinic wants only its pharmacist to open the medicine cabinet. Staff keep lending key cards. Which device is BEST?
questions.explain: A fingerprint cannot be lent to another person.

questions.stem: A courier company prints delivery notes with two carbon copies underneath. Which printer must it use?
questions.explain: Only an impact printer can press through carbon copies.

questions.stem: Which printer is used in most supermarket tills and ATMs to print receipts?
questions.explain: Thermal printers are fast, quiet and need no ink.

questions.stem: A school office prints about 4,000 black-and-white pages each month. Which printer is MOST cost-effective?
questions.explain: Lasers are fast with a low cost per page for high-volume text.

questions.stem: An architect in St. John’s must print large, accurate building plans on A0 paper. Which device should she use?
questions.explain: Plotters produce large, precise drawings.

questions.stem: A hospital in Barbados wants to make a custom-fitted plastic hand brace for a patient. Which output device can do this?
questions.explain: 3D printers build solid objects layer by layer.

questions.stem: In an automatic gate at a Sandy Point villa, which device physically opens the gate after the processor receives the correct code?
questions.explain: Actuators turn signals into movement.

questions.stem: Which pair of devices would BEST help a student who is deaf follow an online lesson?
options: Live captions on the screen and visual alerts
questions.explain: Information must be visual for a deaf user.

questions.stem: A courier company's computer prints a barcode label that is later scanned at every depot. What kind of output is the barcode label?
questions.explain: A barcode is printed so that another machine can read it: machine-readable output.

questions.stem: Which group of keys includes F1 to F12?
questions.explain: The twelve function keys run along the top of the keyboard.

questions.stem: Which statement about a mouse is TRUE?
options: It is used to enter text
It controls the pointer but cannot enter text
It always has three scroll wheels
questions.explain: A mouse moves the pointer and selects; it cannot type text.

questions.stem: Which early impact printer struck characters on a rotating wheel against an ink ribbon?
questions.explain: The daisy-wheel printer used a wheel of characters struck by a hammer.

questions.stem: A government archive wants a compact, low-cost way to keep 50 years of printed gazettes for the long term. Which output medium is traditionally used?
questions.explain: Microfilm is compact, cheap to store and a good archival form.

questions.stem: A call-centre agent in West Bay needs both hands free to type while talking to customers. Which device is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: A headset gives hands-free listening and speaking.

questions.stem: Which of these is system software?
questions.explain: Android is an operating system, so it is system software.

questions.stem: Shanice uses a program to edit her Carnival TikTok videos. What type of software is this?
questions.explain: Video editing is a task for the user: application software.

questions.stem: While Kyle types his essay, Spotify plays music and a game updates in the background. Which OS function makes this possible?
questions.explain: The OS shares the processor between programs.

questions.stem: Which OS function lets you create a folder called 'IT SBA' and move files into it?
questions.explain: Creating, naming, moving and deleting files and folders is file management.

questions.stem: Malia plugs in a new printer but it will not print. A message says software is missing. What is MOST likely needed?
questions.explain: A driver lets the OS communicate with a specific device.

questions.stem: Which utility program would help after a computer is infected by a worm?
questions.explain: Anti-malware detects and removes malware such as worms.

questions.stem: A student needs to e-mail 40 photos, but the attachment limit is 25 MB. Which utility helps MOST?
questions.explain: Compression reduces file size.

questions.stem: Which of these is general-purpose application software?
questions.explain: A spreadsheet can be used for many unrelated tasks.

questions.stem: The government of Aruba commissions programmers to build a system for its unique work-permit rules. This is:
questions.explain: Written specially for one organisation's needs.

questions.stem: Which is an advantage of off-the-shelf software over custom software?
options: The buyer owns the source code
It always meets every need exactly
It is cheaper and available immediately
questions.explain: Development costs are shared among many buyers, and it is ready now.

questions.stem: What makes software open source?
options: Its source code is available to view and modify
It has no licence at all
It is sold in a shop
questions.explain: Open source means the code is published under a licence that allows modification.

questions.stem: Devon downloads a game editor that works free for 30 days and then asks him to pay. This is:
questions.explain: Shareware is 'try before you buy'.

questions.stem: A network technician types ipconfig to check a computer's address. Which interface is she using?
questions.explain: Typed commands at a prompt: command line interface.

questions.stem: Which is an advantage of a command line interface?
options: Uses little memory and is fast for experts
questions.explain: CLIs are efficient for experts and need few resources.

questions.stem: An ATM on Wallblake Road offers 'Withdraw / Balance / Deposit / Exit'. Which interface is this?
questions.explain: Choosing from a list of options is menu-driven.

questions.stem: In GUI terms, what does WIMP stand for?
questions.explain: WIMP describes the parts of a GUI.

questions.stem: A school cannot afford new software, so it pays a technician to add templates, formulas and simplified menus to Excel to create its grade book. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Adapting a general-purpose package is customisation. Custom-written software is created from scratch for one client.

questions.stem: Malware spreads across a company network overnight, copying itself from computer to computer with nobody opening any file. What is it MOST likely to be?
questions.explain: A worm replicates without human interaction and does not need to attach to a program.

questions.stem: Shanice downloads a free 'Carnival filter' app that secretly steals her passwords. This is an example of a:
questions.explain: A Trojan horse is disguised as something useful or fun.

questions.stem: Which utility gathers the scattered pieces of each file on a hard disk into one place and puts the free space together?
questions.explain: Defragmenting rearranges file fragments without changing their contents.

questions.stem: Which translator converts a whole high-level program into machine code at once, producing a file that can run on its own?
questions.explain: A compiler translates the entire program; an interpreter works line by line.

questions.stem: Virgin Power & Water collects meter readings all month and then produces every customer's bill in one run. Which processing mode is this?
questions.explain: Data accumulated over a period and processed together is batch processing.

questions.stem: Which task MOST needs real-time processing?
questions.explain: Life-critical control systems need instant, continuous processing.

questions.stem: A university mainframe lets 300 students log on at once, each receiving slots of CPU time and memory. This is called:
questions.explain: Time-sharing allocates computer resources in time slots to many users simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which component of an operating system provides basic-level control over all the hardware, reading and writing memory and handling devices?
questions.explain: The kernel is the OS core.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A laptop advert says its processor runs at 3.2 GHz. What does GHz measure?
options: The number of clock cycles per second
questions.explain: GHz (gigahertz) = billions of clock cycles per second.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Why does a quad-core processor help when Rhea streams music, video-calls and edits a document at the same time?
options: Four cores can work on several tasks at once
questions.explain: Multiple cores share the work of several programs.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Which upgrade would MOST improve performance in 3-D games and video rendering?
questions.explain: A graphics card has its own processor and memory for graphics.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Darnell's laptop slows down badly whenever he has many browser tabs and a game open. Task Manager shows memory at 97%. What would help MOST?
questions.explain: Memory is the bottleneck; more RAM (or closing programs) helps.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Which is the MAIN advantage of an SSD over an HDD in a laptop?
options: Faster start-up and loading, and no moving parts
Larger capacity at the same price
questions.explain: SSDs are faster and more robust, though dearer per GB.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A program lists '8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB recommended'. What does 'recommended' mean?
options: The program will run well with this amount
The program will not install with less
The program needs exactly this amount
questions.explain: Minimum = it runs; recommended = it runs well.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Which spec matters MOST to a sales rep travelling around the islands all day?
options: Long battery life and light weight
questions.explain: Portability depends on battery and weight.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A bakery's accounting program only runs on Windows. Which computer should NOT be bought?
questions.explain: The software cannot run on ChromeOS.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Before unplugging a desktop's power cable, what should you do FIRST?
options: Spray it with water to cool it
Switch off at the wall socket
questions.explain: Always switch off at the wall before handling mains cables.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A desktop shows no lights after a storm. The cable is firmly connected. What is the NEXT sensible check?
options: Test the wall socket with a lamp that is known to work
questions.explain: Test the socket before suspecting the computer.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: The computer and monitor both have power lights on, but the screen is black. Which is the MOST likely fix?
options: Reconnect the video cable and check the input source
questions.explain: The signal path between computer and monitor is the next thing to check.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Excel has stopped responding. Which keyboard shortcut opens Task Manager directly so you can end it?
questions.explain: Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: How should you remove jammed paper from a printer?
options: Use a knife to cut it out
Pull it quickly backwards while printing
Switch off, then pull it gently in the direction the paper normally travels
questions.explain: Gentle pulling in the feed direction avoids tearing and damage.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A laptop used on a bed keeps shutting down. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explain: Soft surfaces block vents, trapping heat.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A phone and a tablet are online, but one laptop cannot connect to the same Wi-Fi. Where is the fault MOST likely?
options: The laptop itself (e.g. airplane mode or Wi-Fi off)
questions.explain: Other devices work, so the problem is on the laptop.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A shop in Providenciales loses unsaved sales data whenever the power flickers. Which device would BEST prevent this?
questions.explain: A UPS keeps the computer running long enough to save and shut down.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A processor runs at 200 MHz. How many cycles does it complete each second?
questions.explain: 1 MHz = one million cycles per second.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Kayla's motherboard supports a maximum of 16 GB of DDR4 RAM and has two slots. Which upgrade is correct?
questions.explain: Match the type (DDR4), respect the maximum (16 GB) and the number of slots (two).

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A desktop has no sound output. Which component could be added to an expansion slot to fix this?
questions.explain: Sound, network and video cards are expansion cards.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: A monitor's power light is orange and flashing, and the screen is black. What does this usually mean?
options: The monitor is in suspend (sleep) mode
The printer is out of ink
questions.explain: Wake the computer by moving the mouse or pressing a key.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Laser prints show a faint copy of the image repeated down the page. What is the BEST fix?
options: Replace the ageing drum or maintenance kit
questions.explain: Ghosting on laser output points to the drum.

questions.topic: Choosing and troubleshooting a computer system
questions.stem: Which is the BEST modern advice for a lithium-ion laptop battery?
options: Fully drain it to 0% every day
Keep it cool and avoid regularly running it completely flat
Keep charging it after it swells
Store it in a hot car
questions.explain: Lithium-ion batteries have no memory effect; heat and deep discharges shorten their life.

questions.stem: Which of these is DATA rather than information?
options: The average mark of Form 5B is 68%
questions.explain: A list of raw numbers with no context is data.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST defines information?
options: Any number stored on a computer
Data that has been processed so that it is meaningful and useful
questions.explain: Information is processed, meaningful data.

questions.stem: A shop owner organises a week's receipts to find which items to reorder. This activity is called:
questions.explain: Turning disorganised data into useful information is data processing.

questions.stem: A student fills in a printed application form, and a clerk later types the data into the school's database. The application form is a:
questions.explain: It contains data that will be input into the system.

questions.stem: Why should source documents be filed away after the data has been entered?
options: The data may need to be checked again
questions.explain: Keeping them allows the entered data to be verified later.

questions.stem: Which is an example of a turnaround document?
options: A blank piece of lined paper
An Internet bill with a payment slip pre-printed with your account number, returned with payment
questions.explain: Printed by the system, completed and returned to the same system.

questions.stem: Which document is MACHINE-readable?
options: A multiple-choice answer sheet marked by OMR
questions.explain: OMR reads the marks directly.

questions.stem: Why do many forms ask you to write one CAPITAL letter in each box?
options: Because computers cannot store lowercase letters
To make handwriting easier to read and reduce errors
To make the form look nice
questions.explain: Separated capital letters are much easier to read accurately.

questions.stem: A weather station at Hewanorra Airport records wind speed automatically every minute. This method of data capture is:
questions.explain: Sensors recording at set intervals is data logging.

questions.stem: Which is NOT one of the qualities stored data needs for good information management?
questions.explain: Data should be accurate, up to date, structured and on a suitable medium.

questions.stem: When an insurance company searches its stored data to find a customer's policy, this is called:
questions.explain: Searching stored data to find relevant information is retrieval.

questions.stem: Why must users evaluate online information more carefully than a TV news broadcast?
options: Internet information is not regulated for quality or accuracy, and anyone can publish
questions.explain: Almost anyone can publish anything online.

questions.stem: Kezia is researching smartphone features and finds an article from 2012. Which criterion is the MAIN concern?
questions.explain: Currency is about how up to date the information is.

questions.stem: A website selling solar panels says solar panels are the best investment anyone can make. Which criterion is MOST in question?
questions.explain: A seller has an interest in promoting its product: bias.

questions.stem: Which source has the strongest AUTHORITY for information about a hurricane warning?
questions.explain: Official weather agencies are the authority on warnings.

questions.stem: A website shows a padlock and uses HTTPS. What does this tell you?
questions.explain: HTTPS is about a secure connection, not accuracy.

questions.stem: A website asks Jaden to type his new password twice. What is this an example of?
questions.explain: Entering data twice and comparing is double-entry verification.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes validation?
options: Software automatically checks that data is reasonable
A human compares data with the source document
Data is backed up to tape
questions.explain: Validation is automatic and checks reasonableness.

questions.stem: A clerk types the phone number 5428130 as 5421830. What type of error is this?
questions.explain: Two digits have been swapped.

questions.stem: A program accepts exam marks only from 0 to 100. Which check is this?
questions.explain: Lower and upper boundaries: range check.

questions.stem: An online form will not submit until the 'Emergency contact' field is filled. Which check is this?
questions.explain: A presence check ensures a field is not left blank.

questions.stem: A Quantity field rejects 'six' but accepts 6. Which check is this?
questions.explain: It checks the data is a number.

questions.stem: A student ID must be two letters followed by four digits, e.g. SM1234. Which check enforces this pattern?
questions.explain: A format check enforces a pattern.

questions.stem: A system rejects an order where the delivery date is before the order date. Which check is this?
questions.explain: Comparing two related fields is a consistency check.

questions.stem: Why do barcodes include a check digit?
options: To detect errors when the code is read or typed
questions.explain: The check digit is recalculated and compared to detect errors.

questions.stem: Using weights 5, 4, 3, 2 and modulus 11 (check digit = 11 − remainder), what is the check digit for 3142?
A clerk types a valid but wrong date of birth (15/03/2009 instead of 15/03/2008). Which technique would catch it?
questions.explain: The value is reasonable, so only comparing with the source catches it.

questions.stem: In a club membership file, all the data about ONE member is called a:
questions.explain: A record is all the data about one item.

questions.stem: In a table of students, the column 'Surname' is a:
questions.explain: Each column is a field.

questions.stem: Records in a file are stored in the order they were added, with no sorting. This is:
questions.explain: Serial = unsorted, in the order added.

questions.stem: Why can an index-sequential file NOT be stored on magnetic tape?
options: Index files are always on CDs
Tape only allows sequential access, but the index requires jumping to a position
questions.explain: Index-sequential needs direct access to jump to positions.

questions.stem: In random file organisation, how is a record's location found?
options: By a formula calculated from data in the record, such as the key
By reading every record from the start
questions.explain: A hashing formula calculates the address.

questions.stem: Which file organisation suits a monthly payroll that processes every employee in turn?
questions.explain: Every record in order: sequential.

questions.stem: A supermarket records each day's sales in a file used overnight to update stock levels. This is a:
questions.explain: Transaction files hold temporary data used to update the master.

questions.stem: A Form 4 student writes: 'A network is when computers are near each other.' Which definition should she use instead in her exam answer?
options: A group of computers in the same room
Two or more computers or devices linked together so they can communicate and share resources
Software that lets you browse the Internet
Any computer that is connected to a printer
questions.explain: A network needs devices LINKED (cable or wireless) for communicating and sharing resources. Being near each other is not enough.

questions.stem: The principal of a school in Puerto Plata asks why the 25 lab computers should be networked. Which is a valid advantage?
options: All computers can share one printer and the Internet connection
Each computer will run twice as fast
Viruses can no longer infect the computers
Students will no longer need passwords
questions.explain: Sharing hardware and the Internet connection is a main reason to network. Networking does not speed up each PC or stop viruses (it can actually spread them).

questions.stem: After the lab computers at a school are networked, a virus on one student's USB stick spreads to every PC. This illustrates which disadvantage of networks?
options: Malware can spread easily between connected computers
questions.explain: Connected computers give malware a path to spread. This is a classic network disadvantage.

questions.stem: A hotel group links the reservation systems of its hotels in Haiti, St. Kitts and Antigua. What type of network is this?
questions.explain: Several islands apart means a wide area: WAN.

questions.stem: Jaylen connects his phone to a Bluetooth speaker and his smartwatch while liming at Negril Beach. These devices form a
questions.explain: Devices around one person within a few metres, usually via Bluetooth, form a PAN.

questions.stem: A government links its offices, libraries and fire stations across one capital city such as Port of Spain. This is BEST described as a
questions.explain: A network covering a town or city is a MAN.

questions.stem: A café on Young Street lets customers connect laptops and phones by Wi-Fi inside the café. Which network type is this?
questions.explain: Wi-Fi inside one building is a Wireless LAN. WAN would mean a wide area.

questions.stem: In the client–server network at a secondary school, which computer checks students' usernames and passwords when they log in?
questions.explain: Authentication is a service provided centrally by a server.

questions.stem: A family business in Warrens has three laptops that share files and a printer with no central server. Which statement about this network is TRUE?
options: Each computer has equal status and can share its own resources
One laptop must control all log-ins
questions.explain: In peer-to-peer every computer is a peer with equal status.

questions.stem: A medical clinic must keep 5,000 patient records confidential and back them up every night. Which network model is MOST suitable?
options: A PAN, because it is personal
No network, because networks are unsafe
Client–server, because security and backup are central
questions.explain: Sensitive data and central backup point to client–server.

questions.stem: Employees of a cruise line log in to a private website to see rosters and company policies. The public cannot access it. This is an
questions.explain: Private, staff-only access = intranet.

questions.stem: A supermarket in Little Bay lets its wholesaler log in to view stock levels so it can deliver automatically. The wholesaler is using the supermarket's
questions.explain: Selected outsiders with controlled access = extranet.

questions.stem: A bank manager uses a VPN from home to reach the bank's private staff portal. The portal is still an intranet because
options: access is restricted to members of the organisation
questions.explain: Access, not location, defines an intranet. A VPN only provides secure remote access.

questions.stem: In a school lab using a star topology, the central switch fails. What happens?
options: The whole lab loses network access
questions.explain: Everything connects through the central switch, so its failure stops the whole star.

questions.stem: An emergency operations centre wants its network to keep working even if one link is cut during a hurricane. Which topology offers this?
questions.explain: Mesh offers multiple routes, so data can avoid a broken link.

questions.stem: Ms Thielman is on a video call while riding from Kralendijk to Antriol. Her call stays connected as her phone switches from one tower's area to the next. This is called
questions.explain: Moving between cells without dropping the call is a handover. Roaming means using another operator's network.

questions.stem: The IT manager of a hotel group warns that its intranet needs regular upgrades and some old staff software no longer works with it. Which disadvantage of an intranet is this?
options: It is open to the public
Upgrade costs and software incompatibility problems
questions.explain: Upgrades and software incompatibility are listed disadvantages of intranets.

questions.stem: A shipping company joins its LANs in Kingston and Port of Spain into a WAN. Which of these is a typical way WAN links are provided?
options: Leased lines, the public telephone network or satellite links
questions.explain: WANs use public networks, leased lines, radio, fibre or satellites; the others are very short-range.

questions.stem: Mr Hodge buys an old desktop for his shop in Port of Spain but it has no way to connect to the office network. Which component must he add?
questions.explain: A NIC lets the device connect to a network.

questions.stem: A technician at a school in All Saints checks the physical address 3C:52:82:1A:9F:04 on a laptop. This is the laptop's
questions.explain: A MAC address is a unique hardware address written in hexadecimal, belonging to the NIC.

questions.stem: A secondary school wants tablets in every classroom to connect to the school's cabled LAN. Which device should be installed in each block?
questions.explain: A WAP connects wireless devices to a wired LAN.

questions.stem: A lab of 30 PCs connected through a hub slows down badly when everyone saves work at once. Why?
options: The hub only works with fibre
The hub sends data to every port, causing collisions
The hub has too much bandwidth
questions.explain: Hubs broadcast to all ports, so traffic collides as devices increase.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST explains why switches replaced hubs in school labs?
options: Switches send data only to the intended device using MAC addresses
questions.explain: Targeted forwarding reduces traffic and collisions.

questions.stem: Which device connects a home LAN in Sandy Point to the ISP's network and forwards data packets between them?
questions.explain: Routers connect different networks.

questions.stem: A family still uses a DSL connection over the telephone line. The device that changes the computer's digital signals into analogue signals for the line is the
questions.explain: MOdulator–DEModulator.

questions.stem: The Wi-Fi is very weak in the back rooms of a large concrete villa in Bartica. Which device would MOST likely fix this?
questions.explain: A repeater regenerates the signal to extend coverage.

questions.stem: A hotel at Starfish Point needs a link between two buildings 600 m apart. The area suffers frequent lightning. Which medium is BEST?
questions.explain: Fibre carries light, not electricity, so lightning and interference do not affect it, and it covers long distances.

questions.stem: The cable that brings cable TV and cable Internet into many homes, with a copper core and a braided metal shield, is
questions.explain: That description is coaxial cable.

questions.stem: A TV remote control stops working when a bag is placed between it and the TV. Which medium does it use?
questions.explain: Infrared needs a clear line of sight.

questions.stem: A cruise ship sailing between Dominica and St. Lucia needs Internet access for passengers far from land. Which medium is used?
questions.explain: Only satellite covers ships in the open sea.

questions.stem: Shanice downloads a 400 MB file on a 40 Mbps connection. Ideally, how long will it take?
An ISP advertises a 100 Mbps plan. The 100 Mbps describes the connection's
questions.explain: Bandwidth is data per second.

questions.stem: Carnival marshals use radios where only one person can speak at a time, saying 'Over' to hand over. This transmission mode is
questions.explain: Both directions, one at a time = half-duplex.

questions.stem: A radio station in Nassau broadcasts to thousands of car radios that cannot reply. The mode is
questions.explain: One direction only = simplex.

questions.stem: In a Paper 02 answer, Shanice must define a network protocol. Which definition is correct?
options: An agreed set of rules that controls how data is sent and received
A device that connects two networks
questions.explain: A protocol is a set of rules; routers are devices, fibre is a medium, antivirus is software.

questions.stem: A technician lists items in a school network: a router, a wireless access point, a web server and Ethernet. Which one is a protocol?
questions.explain: Ethernet is a set of rules for wired LANs; the others are hardware or servers.

questions.stem: The network administrator at a college uses software to add new student accounts, monitor network use and push an update to all 200 PCs at once. This is
questions.explain: Network management software sets up users, monitors use, fixes problems and distributes software.

questions.stem: A radio station in Kingstown sends its signal so that anyone with a radio can listen, while two friends on a phone call hear only each other. These are examples of
questions.explain: The radio station is broadcast; the private call is point-to-point.

questions.stem: An old dial-up connection over an ordinary telephone line transmits at about 100 to 9,600 bps. This bandwidth category is
questions.explain: Telephone-line speeds of 100–9,600 bps are voice band; narrowband is 40–300 bps; broadband is millions of bps.

questions.stem: Your teacher asks the class for another name for a transmission medium, the pathway that carries information from sender to receiver. The answer is
questions.explain: A transmission medium is also called a communication channel.

questions.stem: In the notes, the three communication modes are simplex, half-duplex and duplex. A video call where both people talk and hear at once is
questions.explain: Duplex (full-duplex) means both directions at the same time.

questions.stem: An events company sets up a network at a different beach venue every weekend. Which advantage of wireless networks matters MOST?
options: Easy to set up and dismantle, mobile and versatile
questions.explain: Wireless networks are quick to set up and take down, ideal for temporary sites.

questions.stem: Mrs Usher's first mobile phone in the 1980s could only make voice calls, with no texts or Internet. Which generation was it?
questions.explain: 1G was analogue and voice-only; 2G added digital voice and SMS.

questions.stem: Kerry-Ann orders sneakers on a shopping app while waiting in line at a supermarket in Spanish Town. This is an example of
questions.explain: Buying and selling using mobile devices is mobile commerce.

questions.stem: A reporter covering a press briefing films, edits and sends a news story using only her smartphone. This is called
questions.explain: Professional reporting done entirely on a phone is mobile journalism (mojo).

questions.stem: During a storm, a resident posts a dramatic flooding video on social media that turns out to be from another country, years earlier. Which drawback of citizen journalism does this show?
options: Content may be unverified or false
questions.explain: Citizen reports can be unverified, out of date or false.

questions.stem: A café owner on the Brades main road wants to create a Wi-Fi hotspot for customers. According to your notes, which two devices create a hotspot?
options: A GPS receiver and NFC tag
A modem and a wireless router
questions.explain: A hotspot network mainly includes a modem and a wireless router.

questions.stem: Bluetooth was introduced in 1994 as a wireless replacement for which type of connection?
questions.explain: Bluetooth was designed to replace RS-232 serial cables between nearby devices.

questions.stem: Grandpa remembers when mobile phones first became digital and he could send SMS text messages. Which generation introduced this?
questions.explain: 2G brought digital voice and SMS.

questions.stem: A content creator live-streams HD video of a beach clean-up from her phone. The generation that first made mobile HD streaming common was
questions.explain: 4G (LTE) delivered mobile broadband for HD streaming.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to control a crane remotely in real time with almost no delay. Which feature of 5G matters MOST?
questions.explain: Low latency allows real-time control.

questions.stem: Dante's laptop has no Internet, so he shares his phone's 4G data with it over Wi-Fi. This is called
questions.explain: Sharing phone data with other devices is tethering / personal hotspot.

questions.stem: A Curaçaoan resident visiting Aruba sees a message that her phone is now on an Aruban network and charges may apply. This is
questions.explain: Using another operator's network outside your home network is roaming.

questions.stem: Before using new wireless earbuds, Leah must confirm a 'Pair' request on her phone. Which technology needs this step?
questions.explain: Bluetooth devices must be paired.

questions.stem: Why is NFC suitable for contactless payment?
options: Its very short range (about 4 cm) means payments need a deliberate tap
It needs no electricity at all
questions.explain: The very short range prevents accidental or remote payments.

questions.stem: Kemar has no mobile signal on a hike but his phone still shows his position on a map he downloaded earlier. Why?
options: GPS receives satellite signals and does not need mobile data
questions.explain: GPS is receive-only from satellites; offline maps provide the background.

questions.stem: How many GPS satellites does a receiver normally need to calculate a 3D position and correct its clock?
questions.explain: At least four satellites are needed.

questions.stem: At an airport, Rhea sees 'Free_Airport_WiFi' with no password. What is the main risk of online banking on it?
options: Others may intercept data or it may be a fake (evil twin) hotspot
Banking apps never work on Wi-Fi
It uses too much mobile data
questions.explain: Open and fake hotspots allow eavesdropping.

questions.stem: A patient in The Valley has a video consultation with a specialist in another country. This is an example of
questions.explain: Health care at a distance is telemedicine.

questions.stem: All local cell towers are down after a hurricane. Which device can a rescue coordinator still use to call overseas?
questions.explain: Satellite phones do not depend on local towers.

questions.stem: Jason receives a text: 'Your bank card is blocked. Click this link to unblock it now.' This is MOST likely
questions.explain: Phishing by SMS is smishing.

questions.stem: A sales rep's phone holding customer data is stolen. Which measure lets the company erase the data from a distance?
questions.explain: Remote wipe erases data on a lost device.

questions.stem: A house in a valley behind San Nicolaas has no mobile signal, while the hilltop does. This coverage problem is mainly caused by
questions.explain: Hills block radio signals, creating dead spots.

questions.stem: For a Paper 02 answer, Kemar must define the Internet. Which statement BEST describes the Internet?
options: A collection of linked web pages
A global network of interconnected computer networks
A web browser made by Microsoft
questions.explain: The Internet is the network infrastructure; linked pages are the Web.

questions.stem: Jamal makes a WhatsApp call to his uncle in Barbados. Which statement is correct?
options: He is using the Web, not the Internet
He is using the Internet, but not the World Wide Web
questions.explain: VoIP is an Internet service that is not part of the Web.

questions.stem: Ms Campbell tells her Form 4 class to open the program they use to view web pages. Which of these is a web browser?
questions.explain: Edge is a browser. Google Search is a search engine.

questions.stem: A café's website files are stored on a computer at a hosting company that sends pages to visitors on request. That computer is a
questions.explain: Web servers store and serve pages.

questions.stem: In the URL https://www.tobagotours.co.tt/trips.html, what is the top-level domain?
questions.explain: The TLD is the last part of the domain: .tt.

questions.stem: In the URL https://www.gndschools.gd/forms/registration.pdf, the file name is
questions.explain: The last item after the final slash is the file.

questions.stem: In https://www.islandnews.bb/sports/cricket/scores.html, which part is the path?
questions.explain: Folders between the domain and the file form the path.

questions.stem: When Kerry-Ann types www.coralreefcafe.tt, which system finds the matching IP address?
questions.explain: DNS translates names into IP addresses.

questions.stem: A technician at a Roseau office is typing a printer's IPv4 address into its settings. Which of these is a valid IPv4 address?
questions.explain: IPv4 uses four numbers 0–255 separated by dots; 300 is out of range.

questions.stem: Tyrese opens a web page's source code and sees tags such as <h1> and <p> marking headings and paragraphs. The language he is looking at is
questions.explain: HyperText Markup Language.

questions.stem: A banking site's address starts with https:// and shows a padlock. This means
options: data sent between the browser and the site is encrypted
questions.explain: HTTPS encrypts data in transit.

questions.stem: The company that the Richardson family pays each month to connect their home to the Internet is their
questions.explain: An ISP provides Internet access.

questions.stem: Nadia sends her completed SBA from her laptop to Microsoft Teams. She is
questions.explain: Sending data from your device to a server is uploading.

questions.stem: A web designer needs to move the finished website files from her laptop onto the hosting server. Which protocol is designed for this?
questions.explain: FTP/SFTP transfers files to servers.

questions.stem: Students in a Form 5 class create revision pages that every class member can edit. This website is a
questions.explain: A wiki is collaboratively editable.

questions.stem: During a class debate, Jaden claims that one American company owns and controls the whole Internet. Which response is correct?
options: No single person, company or government owns or controls the Internet; it works through agreed protocols
The Internet is owned by the United Nations
Each ISP owns the whole Internet
He is right: one company controls it
questions.explain: The Internet is a network of networks owned by many parties, held together by shared protocols such as TCP/IP.

questions.stem: The Hummingbird Ridge High School media club records a series of audio episodes interviewing local musicians, which listeners download to their phones. This is a
questions.explain: Audio (or video) episodes for streaming or download are podcasts.

questions.stem: Grandpa remembers his modem dialling the ISP's number and screeching before he typed his username and password to get online. This connection method is
questions.explain: Dial-up is the oldest method: the modem dials the ISP over the phone line.

questions.stem: For a Carnival-week quiz night at school, Team Soca must answer: which statement about the origin of the World Wide Web is correct?
options: It is owned by one government
It was designed in 1991 by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN
It was invented in 2010 by a social media company
questions.explain: Tim Berners-Lee designed the Web at CERN around 1991, and CERN gave it away free; the Internet came first.

questions.stem: When Andre downloads a photo, it is split into packets that travel separately and are put back together in order at his device. Which protocol makes this transfer reliable?
questions.explain: TCP controls reliable transfer by checking and reassembling packets.

questions.stem: A web designer is told to use XHTML instead of older HTML. What is the main difference?
options: XHTML is used to send e-mail
XHTML is stricter, with more rules, so browsers handle the code consistently
questions.explain: XHTML (2000) is a stricter version of HTML.

questions.stem: A Paramaribo chef posts recipes regularly; the newest post appears at the top and readers comment. This is a
questions.explain: Reverse-date posts with comments = blog.

questions.stem: A manager at a Guyana firm authorises a large payment, then claims he never did. The system keeps no record of who approved it. Which kind of system security is missing?
questions.explain: Undeniableness means people cannot deny their actions; a record (audit trail or digital signature) provides it.

questions.stem: An IT auditor at a Nevis hotel writes: 'The procedure for issuing staff keycards has no check on whether the person still works here.' In security terms this is a
options: vulnerability in a set of procedures
questions.explain: A vulnerability can be a weakness in procedures, not just software.

questions.stem: Shania visits a hacked recipe website and, without clicking any download button, malware is installed on her laptop. This distribution channel is called
questions.explain: Unintended download just by visiting a site = drive-by download.

questions.stem: A Barbados school's timetable program sometimes shows the wrong room because of a coding mistake made by its developer. This program is BEST described as
options: defective software with a bug, not malware
questions.explain: Malware is deliberately harmful; a legitimate program with accidental errors is defective software.

questions.stem: When the Regent Street Accounting buys a software package, it receives a document stating that the program may be installed on three computers only. This document is the
questions.explain: The EULA sets out how the software may be used; breaking it is piracy.

questions.stem: The two journalists in the Prestel case could not be convicted of fraud. Why?
options: They had permission to use the system
Fraud required a person to be deceived, and a computer cannot be deceived
questions.explain: This gap led to the Computer Misuse Act 1990, which created specific offences such as unauthorised access.

questions.stem: A fitness app collects users' location 'to map their runs' but later sells the location history to advertisers without telling them. This is MAINLY
options: a violation of privacy (data used for a different purpose)
questions.explain: Collecting for one purpose and using for another without consent violates privacy.

questions.stem: Investigators hide a small microphone in an office that transmits conversations to a nearby receiver. This type of electronic surveillance is
questions.explain: A hidden transmitting microphone = bugging; wiretapping physically taps phone lines.

questions.stem: A carer has her elderly client's online-banking password. The client's bills go unpaid and there are unexplained withdrawals. This MOST likely indicates
questions.explain: Unauthorised use of someone's money, shown by unpaid bills and unexplained withdrawals, is financial abuse.

questions.stem: Which feature of cyberbullying means a student can be targeted even at midnight in her own bedroom?
options: It is persistent: devices allow 24-hour contact
questions.explain: Persistence (24/7 contact) is one of the special concerns, with permanence and being hard to notice.

questions.stem: A hacker gets into a Barbados school's grading system and changes several students' final marks. No data is deleted and the system stays online. Which security goal has been MOST directly broken?
questions.explain: The data is now inaccurate: integrity. The system is still available, and portability is not a security goal.

questions.stem: On the morning of the tax deadline, a government e-services portal cannot be reached because its servers are overwhelmed by fake requests. Which goal is broken?
questions.explain: Legitimate users cannot use the service: availability.

questions.stem: An IT audit of a Nassau law office finds that all computers still use the factory-default password 'admin'. In security terms, the default password is BEST described as a
questions.explain: It is a weakness that could be exploited: a vulnerability.

questions.stem: The manager of a Grenada credit union says: 'Criminals in the region have started targeting small banks with ransomware.' Nothing has happened at his credit union yet. What he describes is a
questions.explain: Something that could cause harm but has not happened yet is a threat.

questions.stem: Within one hour of a single infected laptop joining the network at a hotel in Ocho Rios, Jamaica, every unpatched PC on the network is infected, though no one opened any file. This malware is MOST likely a
questions.explain: Spreading by itself across a network without user action is the defining feature of a worm.

questions.stem: A Word document on the shared drive at a St. Lucia school infects each computer that opens it, and each infected computer then infects other documents. This is a
questions.explain: Malware that attaches to host files and spreads when they are opened is a virus.

questions.stem: Staff at a Georgetown, Guyana, accounting firm arrive to find every file renamed with the extension .locked and a note demanding payment in Bitcoin for the decryption key. This is
questions.explain: Encrypting files and demanding payment is ransomware.

questions.stem: A student's online banking password is stolen, even though she never shared it. Investigators find a small program on her laptop that recorded every key she pressed. This program is a type of
questions.explain: A keylogger secretly records keystrokes: spyware.

questions.stem: A resident of Nevis receives an SMS saying she has won a Carnival cruise and must text back her ID number and card details to claim it. This is an example of
questions.explain: Phishing via SMS text message is smishing.

questions.stem: Customers of a Trinidad bank type the bank's correct web address into their browsers but are taken to a convincing fake site, where their logins are stolen. This attack is called
questions.explain: Redirecting users who typed the correct address (e.g. by poisoned DNS) is pharming.

questions.stem: Mr. Hodge in Anguilla receives a phone call from someone claiming to be from his internet provider, who asks for his account password to 'fix a fault'. This is
questions.explain: Phishing by voice call is vishing.

questions.stem: An employee of a Barbados rum distillery is secretly paid by a foreign competitor to copy the company's new blending formula onto a flash drive. This is BEST described as
questions.explain: Stealing a competitor's trade secrets = industrial espionage.

questions.stem: At a busy café in Layou with free open Wi-Fi, a person uses software to capture unencrypted messages and logins sent by other customers. This misuse is
questions.explain: Intercepting communications in transit = electronic eavesdropping.

questions.stem: A small business in Antigua buys one licence for a design program and installs it on all six office computers. This is
questions.explain: Using software beyond the terms of its licence is software piracy.

questions.stem: A news report says a Jamaican government website was taken offline by traffic from over 20,000 infected devices around the world. The word that BEST describes this attack is
questions.explain: Many infected devices acting together = distributed denial of service via a botnet.

questions.stem: Kerry copies a poem from 1850, which is out of copyright, and enters it in a school poetry competition as her own work. This is
questions.explain: No copyright exists any more, but she still claimed someone else's work as her own: plagiarism.

questions.stem: A government ministry in an island state deliberately posts only flattering statistics and edited photos about a new road project to persuade citizens to support it before an election. This is BEST described as
questions.explain: A deliberate, one-sided message designed to persuade = propaganda. Bias can be unintentional; this was planned.

questions.stem: A Barbados cricket fan writes a blog about a Test match. Without meaning to, he praises every decision by his own team and criticises every decision by the visitors. His blog shows
questions.explain: His point of view affects what he writes, though not deliberately: bias.

questions.stem: Mrs. Hodge in St. John’s notices purchases on her card statement from an online electronics store she has never used. Her card is still in her purse. What has MOST likely happened?
options: Credit card fraud using her stolen card details
questions.explain: Criminals used her card details without the physical card: credit card fraud, a form of identity theft.

questions.stem: A government installs cameras on main roads and software that reads car number plates, and stores the records for years. Critics say this could be misused. This debate is about
questions.explain: Electronic monitoring of people's activities = surveillance, which raises privacy concerns.

questions.stem: Which of these is the BEST example of cybercrime?
options: A criminal hacks into a Trinidad shop's system and transfers money to his own account
A teacher deletes an old file by mistake
A printer runs out of ink
questions.explain: Cybercrime is crime carried out using computers and the Internet, such as hacking to steal money.

questions.stem: During a tropical storm, a resident of Charlestown forwards a voice note claiming Liamuiga Power & Water will cut all power for a week. She genuinely believes it is true, but it is false. Her forwarding is BEST described as spreading
questions.explain: False information shared by someone who believes it = misinformation. Disinformation is deliberate.

questions.stem: After her e-mail is hacked, a nurse in Dominica finds that someone has opened two credit cards in her name and run up debts. Which impact on the individual does this BEST show?
questions.explain: Debts in her name are a financial impact of identity theft.

questions.stem: A school counsellor in Barbados notices that a student targeted by months of online harassment is sleeping badly, avoiding friends and missing school. This is MAINLY a
questions.explain: Effects on sleep, mood and social life are psychological.

questions.stem: After news reports that a Caribbean airline 'lost passenger data to hackers', bookings drop sharply even though the system is working again. This is an example of
questions.explain: Customers avoid the airline because they no longer trust it.

questions.stem: A clinic in Jamaica is investigated and fined after patient records were left unprotected and leaked. The fine is MAINLY
questions.explain: Investigation and fines by a regulator are legal impacts (and tangible).

questions.stem: Hackers disrupt the computer systems that control water pumping for an entire island. Why is this especially serious for the government?
options: It is a form of plagiarism
Water companies do not use computers
Water supply is critical national infrastructure that affects public health and safety
questions.explain: Critical infrastructure attacks endanger the whole population.

questions.stem: Days before an election, thousands of WhatsApp messages falsely tell voters in one district that their polling station has moved. What is the MAIN impact on democracy?
options: Voters' phones are infected with worms
Voters may be misled into not voting, reducing fairness and trust in the result
questions.explain: False voting information can suppress votes and damage trust.
