questions.stem: A small Antigua hotel paid no ransom but still lost money after a ransomware attack. Which was MOST likely its largest hidden cost?
options: The price of the antivirus it already had
Lost bookings while systems were down
The cost of the ransom note paper
questions.explain: Downtime and lost revenue are usually the biggest hidden cost.

questions.stem: Which of these impacts on a Trinidad firm after a cyberattack is TANGIBLE?
options: A US$8,000 invoice for IT recovery
questions.explain: A specific invoice can be measured: tangible.

questions.stem: Why is the leak of citizens' fingerprints from a national ID database MORE serious in the long term than the theft of their bank cards?
options: Fingerprints cannot be changed, so the risk lasts for life
questions.explain: Biometric data is permanent; bank cards can be cancelled and reissued.

questions.stem: Ransomware shuts down the computer system of the company that manages container unloading at the Willemstad cruise terminal for a week. Which is the MOST likely knock-on impact?
options: Students cannot log into Google Classroom
Supermarkets and hardware stores run short of stock
questions.explain: If containers cannot be processed, businesses that depend on imports run short.

questions.stem: Why are small businesses, such as a family garage in West Bay, often hit HARDER by a cyberattack than large banks?
options: Small businesses do not use computers
They usually have fewer resources, backups and IT staff to recover
Hackers are not interested in banks
questions.explain: Fewer resources make recovery harder; some small firms never reopen.

questions.stem: A Guyanese engineering firm loses a major contract after a competitor obtained its tender price through hacking. This impact is BEST described as
questions.explain: Stolen trade secrets let a rival win: lost competitive advantage.

questions.stem: A young soca producer in Trinidad finds her new album shared free on download sites the day it is released. The MOST direct impact on her is
options: loss of income from sales and streams
questions.explain: Piracy reduces the creator's legitimate income.

questions.stem: A question asks: 'Explain ONE impact of a DDoS attack on an online store. (2 marks)'. Which answer earns BOTH marks?
options: Customers cannot access the site to buy, so the store loses sales during the attack.
DDoS stands for distributed denial of service.
questions.explain: It states the impact and explains how the attack causes it.

questions.stem: The owner of an Orange Walk dive shop asks whether to pay a ransom after an attack. Which is the STRONGEST reason against paying?
options: There is no guarantee of recovery, and paying funds crime and may lead to repeat attacks
It is illegal to have backups
Paying guarantees the data is returned
questions.explain: Criminals may not deliver, and payers become targets.

questions.stem: Which sentence shows EVALUATION rather than description in an answer about a data breach at a school?
options: The privacy impact on students is the most serious because their data can be misused for years, whereas the school's costs are one-off.
questions.explain: It makes a judgement and justifies it with a comparison.

questions.stem: A Barbados company wants ONE firewall that protects all 60 computers on its network before traffic reaches any of them. It should choose
options: a software firewall on one PC
questions.explain: A hardware firewall sits between the network and the Internet and protects every device.

questions.stem: A system monitors the important operating-system files on one server and alerts the administrator if they change. This is a
questions.explain: Monitoring a single host's files = HIDS.

questions.stem: A hacker's program tries every word in an English dictionary, with common number endings, as a student's password. This is a
questions.explain: Trying dictionary words and variations = dictionary attack.

questions.stem: Kayla logs into the school system with her username and password (step 1). The system then lets her see her own grades but not her classmates' (step 2). Step 2 is
questions.explain: Authentication proves who you are; authorisation decides what you may access.

questions.stem: A Trinidad firm does a full backup on Sunday. Each night it copies everything that has changed since Sunday's full backup. These nightly copies are
questions.explain: Changes since the last FULL backup = differential.

questions.stem: A café in Albina still uses WEP encryption on its Wi-Fi. What should the IT technician advise?
options: Keep WEP, it is the strongest
Upgrade to WPA2 or WPA3, because WEP is easily cracked
questions.explain: WEP is the weakest; WPA2 is a minimum and WPA3 is best.

questions.stem: An e-mail 'from your principal' asks you to buy gift cards urgently. What is the BEST way to verify it?
options: Reply to the e-mail and ask if it is real
Forward it to all your friends
Phone or speak to the principal using contact details you already have
questions.explain: Verify through a channel you already trust, never through the suspicious message.

questions.stem: An e-mail comes from support@rnicrosoft.com. What trick is being used?
options: Substitution: 'rn' replaces 'm' to look like microsoft
questions.explain: Attackers swap characters that look alike.

questions.stem: A bank's app recognises its customers partly by the rhythm in which they type their PIN. This is an example of
questions.explain: Typing rhythm, gait and voice are behavioural biometrics.

questions.stem: The power in The Valley goes off for a few minutes several times a week. Wallblake Road Travel office wants staff to be able to save work and shut down safely when this happens. Which device should they buy?
questions.explain: A UPS provides battery power for a short time so users can save and shut down.

questions.stem: After the power returns following an outage in Spanish Town, a spike in voltage damages a shop's computer. Which device would have BEST prevented this?
questions.explain: Surge protectors absorb voltage spikes.

questions.stem: A Barbados accounting firm keeps its only backup drive in the same room as its server. Why is this a poor arrangement?
options: A fire, flood or theft could destroy both the server and the backup
The backup will run too slowly
Backups must always be on paper
questions.explain: Backups must be kept separately, ideally off-site or in the cloud.

questions.stem: A laptop containing a St. Kitts clinic's patient records is stolen from a car. Which countermeasure would mean the thief CANNOT read the records?
questions.explain: Encrypted data is unreadable without the key.

questions.stem: Which of these combinations is a TRUE example of two-factor authentication?
options: Password and a code from an authenticator app on your phone
questions.explain: Two different factor types: something you know + something you have.

questions.stem: A school in Guyana wants to block unknown computers on the Internet from connecting to its network, and stop students reaching certain websites. Which countermeasure does BOTH?
questions.explain: A firewall filters traffic in and out according to rules.

questions.stem: Why must antivirus software at a Trinidad bank be updated regularly?
options: So it can recognise newly discovered malware
So it can replace the firewall
questions.explain: Signature databases must be updated to detect new malware.

questions.stem: At a Jamaican hospital, porters can view patients' full medical histories on the system. Which countermeasure would BEST fix this?
options: Set access privileges so porters see only what their job needs
questions.explain: Least privilege limits access to what each role needs.

questions.stem: A teacher's grade in the Oranjestad school system was changed overnight. Which countermeasure would show WHO made the change and WHEN?
questions.explain: An audit trail logs who did what and when.

questions.stem: Ransomware spreads through a network in Antigua by exploiting a flaw for which the software maker released a fix two months ago. Which countermeasure would have prevented this?
questions.explain: Patches fix known vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: A Turks and Caicos bank wants only specific managers to enter the vault room, and wants entry that cannot be lent to someone else like a key. Which is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Biometrics are tied to the person and cannot be lent.

questions.stem: Which is the MOST suitable way to put out a fire in a server room?
questions.explain: CO₂ and clean-agent gases extinguish fire without damaging electronics; water conducts electricity and damages equipment.

questions.stem: New students at a Grenada secondary school must agree to rules about using school computers before receiving a login. This document is a(n)
questions.explain: An AUP is an organisation's rules for using its systems.

questions.stem: Which password for a Form 5 student's school e-mail account is the STRONGEST?
questions.explain: A long passphrase of random words with numbers and symbols is strongest.

questions.stem: Tia sees a cruel meme about a classmate being shared in her year-group chat. Which response BEST shows digital citizenship?
options: Reply with an insult to whoever posted it
Don't share it, support the classmate, report it and tell a trusted adult
Share it to her own story
questions.explain: Being an upstander: support, report and tell.

questions.stem: A bank in Kingston wants a system that watches its network and immediately warns the security team when someone appears to be accessing systems without authorisation. It needs a(n)
questions.explain: An IDS monitors for unauthorised access and raises alerts.

questions.stem: At the end of each school year, the Calabash Point Secondary moves the records of students who have left onto separate storage, in case they are needed in future, and removes them from the everyday system. This is
questions.explain: Storing data no longer in daily use for future reference = archiving (not the same as a backup).

questions.stem: A clerk at a Barbados clinic accidentally overwrites a patient's blood group with the wrong value. Which aspect of data has been damaged?
questions.explain: Integrity means data is accurate and not wrongly changed.

questions.stem: Why do many organisations, such as a St. Lucia insurance company, discourage staff from moving files on memory sticks?
options: Memory sticks can carry viruses and are easily lost along with sensitive data
questions.explain: They can introduce malware and, if lost, expose the data stored on them.

questions.stem: A small Antigua business syncs its files to a cloud folder instantly. Ransomware encrypts the office PC and the encrypted files sync to the cloud. What should the business use instead?
options: Backups that keep previous versions or an offline copy
questions.explain: Versioned or offline backups let you restore files from before the attack.

questions.stem: A Jamaican factory installs robots that apply paint in a sealed booth, so workers no longer breathe fumes. Which advantage of automation does this show?
questions.explain: Removing workers from hazards = improved safety.

questions.stem: After its packing line is automated, a Barbados company finds it takes weeks to switch the line to a new product. This shows that automated systems
options: are less flexible than manual systems
questions.explain: Lower flexibility is a known disadvantage.

questions.stem: A Chaguanas resort hires someone to grow its Instagram presence, respond to online reviews and analyse engagement figures. The job title is
questions.explain: Strategy, content, reviews and metrics = social media specialist.

questions.stem: Which BEST describes the difference between a network engineer and a network administrator?
options: The engineer plans and designs networks; the administrator keeps an existing network running
questions.explain: Engineers design and implement; administrators maintain and operate.

questions.stem: Which is a duty of a computer systems analyst?
options: Defining the problem by conferring with clients and evaluating procedures
questions.explain: Analysts define problems and design solutions.

questions.stem: Before a Jamaican bank releases its new mobile app, a team runs it with planned test data to find bugs and report them to the programmers. These professionals are
questions.explain: Finding bugs using test data = software tester.

questions.stem: A programmer writes device drivers and parts of an operating system so that new hardware works correctly. This person is a
questions.explain: Writing system software = systems programmer.

questions.stem: Dominica tourism office employs someone to keep its website running, update events, fix broken links, answer visitor e-mails and check traffic statistics. This person is the
questions.explain: Maintaining a live website = webmaster.

questions.stem: In a large government office in Trinidad, one person is responsible for keeping track of all the organisation's files and storage media, organising backups and restoring lost files. This role is the
questions.explain: Tracking files and managing backups/restores = file librarian.

questions.stem: A Grenada law firm scans its old files, stores all new documents electronically and shares them by e-mail and the cloud. It is moving towards a
questions.explain: Storing and sharing documents electronically = paperless office.

questions.stem: A supermarket in Montego Bay installs machines that let customers scan and pay for their own shopping without a cashier. This is an example of
questions.explain: Machines doing tasks people did = automation.

questions.stem: Which job at a Barbados utility company is MOST likely to disappear when smart meters are installed in every home?
questions.explain: Smart meters send readings automatically, replacing manual reading.

questions.stem: A Trinidad bank introduces mobile banking. Which new job is MOST likely to be created?
questions.explain: Building and maintaining the app creates developer jobs.

questions.stem: The Caribbean Coastal Bank sends tellers on a course so they can work as digital-services advisers after its branches automate. This is an example of
questions.explain: Learning skills for a new role = retraining (reskilling).

questions.stem: Ms. Toussaint, an insurance clerk, works from her home in Saint-Marc using a laptop, video calls and cloud storage. This is called
questions.explain: Working remotely using ICT = telecommuting.

questions.stem: Which is a DISADVANTAGE of telecommuting for the employee?
questions.explain: Isolation is a common disadvantage; the others are advantages.

questions.stem: Tevin earns money in Jamaica by accepting delivery jobs through an app whenever he chooses, with no fixed employer. He is part of the
questions.explain: Short-term, app-based, flexible work = gig economy.

questions.stem: Which is the MAIN disadvantage of gig work for someone like Tevin?
options: He usually has no sick pay, paid holidays or guaranteed income
He can work for several apps
questions.explain: Insecure income and lack of benefits are the key disadvantages.

questions.stem: A Jamaican hospital hires someone to interview staff, study the current paper-based process and design a new computerised system. This person is a
questions.explain: Investigating needs and designing systems = systems analyst.

questions.stem: Who in a Guyanese bank would be responsible for backing up the customer database and controlling which staff can access it?
questions.explain: Backups and access control for databases = DBA.

questions.stem: At Frangipani Hill Academy, who would set up user accounts for new students and keep the school's Wi-Fi and switches working?
questions.explain: Network and user account management = network administrator.

questions.stem: An airline in the Caribbean hires someone to monitor its systems for attacks, investigate suspicious logins and test for vulnerabilities. The job title is
questions.explain: Monitoring and investigating threats = cybersecurity analyst.

questions.stem: A company in Barbados needs someone to design the circuit board for a new hurricane weather-sensor device. It should hire a
questions.explain: Designing hardware = computer engineer.

questions.stem: The Barbadian tourism office wants someone to study visitor statistics and produce charts showing trends by month and country. Who should it hire?
questions.explain: Analysing data and reporting trends = data analyst.

questions.stem: After a factory in Trinidad installs robots, the remaining workers only press start and stop buttons and watch the machines. Their job has become less skilled. This is called
questions.explain: Jobs that need less skill after automation = deskilling.

questions.stem: Which BEST explains why remote work can be an opportunity for small Caribbean islands?
options: It removes the need for Internet access
Islanders can work for clients and employers anywhere in the world without emigrating
It guarantees higher pay for everyone
questions.explain: Remote work opens global job markets to island residents.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: At a Grenada secondary school, students watch a short lesson video at home and use class time for group problem-solving with the teacher's help. This approach is called
questions.explain: Lesson at home, practice in class = flipped classroom.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: A Form 4 student can search for information, judge whether a website is reliable and produce a well-referenced presentation. She is showing
questions.explain: Finding, evaluating and producing information = digital literacy.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: A teacher in Trinidad notices several essays contain identical paragraphs copied from the same website. Which drawback of ICT in education does this show?
questions.explain: Easy copying has increased plagiarism.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: When an unconscious tourist is brought into a Guyanese hospital, doctors can see his allergy list from his home clinic. This benefit comes from
questions.explain: EHRs can be accessed across facilities.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: Which medical imaging technology uses strong magnets and radio waves to show soft tissue?
questions.explain: MRI = magnetic resonance imaging.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: A small hospital in Dominica sends a CT scan to a radiologist in Jamaica at night, who returns a report within the hour. This is
questions.explain: Sending images to a remote radiologist = teleradiology.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: A man uses an online symptom checker, which suggests a mild virus, so he stays home; he actually has a serious infection. This illustrates which risk of self-diagnosis tools?
options: False reassurance leading to delayed treatment
questions.explain: False results can delay proper care.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: A Barbados hotel orders bulk linen through a supplier's online trade portal. This is
questions.explain: Business buying from business = B2B.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: Which is a key BUSINESS benefit of an EPOS system in a George Town supermarket?
options: It replaces the need for electricity
Stock levels update automatically with each sale
questions.explain: Automatic stock control and accurate reporting.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: Why are fingerprints useful to police as long-term markers of identity?
options: They can only be taken by doctors
They are detailed, nearly unique, hard to alter and last a lifetime
questions.explain: These properties make fingerprints reliable identifiers.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: Investigators place a tiny microphone in a suspect's car that transmits conversations to a nearby receiver. This type of electronic surveillance is
questions.explain: A hidden transmitting microphone = bugging.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: During flooding in Nassau, residents post videos of the rising water before any reporter arrives. This is
questions.explain: Ordinary people reporting events with their phones.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: Which development made music piracy grow rapidly?
options: Digital formats such as MP3 that are easy to copy and share
questions.explain: Digitisation made copying easy.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: A game lets players in Antigua swing their arms to play virtual cricket without a controller. Which gaming technology is used?
questions.explain: Motion sensors detect body movement.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: A Jamaican factory's cold store has sensors that send temperature readings to a computer, which switches the cooling on or off to keep it at 4 °C. This is a
questions.explain: Sensor feedback controlling a process = process control.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: An engineer designs a part on screen and sends the design directly to a machine that cuts it from metal. The design and making stages are
questions.explain: Computer-aided design, then computer-aided manufacturing.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: Which combination of technologies is MOST important for predicting a hurricane's track?
options: Satellites, hurricane hunter aircraft data and supercomputer models
questions.explain: Observation data plus forecast models.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: A garage in Georgetown enters a car's symptoms into software that compares them with stored rules and suggests the most likely fault. This software is
questions.explain: Diagnosis from stored knowledge and rules = expert system.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: Tourists point their phones at Fort James and see historical information and images appear over the live camera view. This is
questions.explain: AR adds digital content to the real world.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: Smart water meters across an island send readings automatically over the network and alert the utility to leaks. They are part of
questions.explain: Connected everyday objects with sensors = IoT.

questions.topic: ICT in different fields and emerging technologies
questions.stem: The government moves all business registrations online. Older shop owners in rural areas without Internet struggle to register. This problem is an example of
questions.explain: Unequal access to ICT and skills = digital divide.

questions.stem: Jalen has typed his SBA introduction and wants to combine his partner's three-page Word file into it without opening it and copying. Which command should he use?
questions.explain: Text from File inserts the whole content of another document at the cursor, combining documents in one step.

questions.stem: A Form 5 chemistry teacher at Breadfruit Valley Secondary is typing a worksheet that includes the formula for carbon dioxide. Which feature formats the 2 in CO2 correctly?
questions.explain: The 2 in CO₂ sits below the line, which is subscript (Ctrl+=).

questions.stem: The Oranjestad Realty advertises an apartment of 85 m2. Which formatting should be applied to the 2?
questions.explain: Square metres are written m² with the 2 raised: superscript (Ctrl+Shift+=).

questions.stem: The Turks and Caicos Islands Schools Athletics Association needs to print an A4 certificate that is wider than it is tall. Which page setting should be changed?
questions.explain: Landscape orientation makes the page wider than it is tall.

questions.stem: Every page of the Kaya Grandi Traders Association report must show the association's name at the top. Which feature is BEST?
questions.explain: A header appears in the top margin of every page automatically.

questions.stem: Rhea typed “Page 1”, “Page 2” and so on at the bottom of each page of her 12-page report. Then she inserted a table on page 3. What is the MOST likely result?
options: The table is moved to the end
Word converts them to page number fields
The typed numbers are now in the wrong places
questions.explain: Typed numbers are ordinary text and move with the content. Use Insert ▸ Page Number instead.

questions.stem: In the bibliography of her SBA, Tamika wants the first line of each reference to start at the margin and the following lines to be indented. Which feature does she need?
questions.explain: A hanging indent keeps line 1 at the margin and indents the rest.

questions.stem: The Liberta Marina must show boat names, lengths and berth numbers so that each boat's details line up across the page. Which feature is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Data that must line up in rows and columns belongs in a table.

questions.stem: A teacher at Sea-Almond Secondary School asks for essays with a gap the height of a full line between every line, so she can write corrections. Which setting meets this request?
questions.explain: Double spacing (2.0) leaves a full line's gap between lines.

questions.stem: Marcus copies a table of ferry times from a web page and wants it to look exactly as it does on the website, including its colours. Which paste option should he choose?
questions.explain: Keep Source Formatting keeps the original fonts, colours and layout.

questions.stem: The Caribbean History Society wants all its notes and sources listed together at the very end of its booklet rather than on each page. Which feature should it use?
questions.explain: Endnotes collect all notes at the end of the document or section.

questions.stem: Andre formatted 10 headings by hand in 16 pt blue. His teacher asks for green headings. Which feature would have let him change all 10 in one step?
questions.explain: Modify the style once and every heading using it updates.

questions.stem: Kemar wants Chapter 2 of his report to always start at the top of a new page, even if he edits Chapter 1. What should he insert before the Chapter 2 heading?
questions.explain: A page break forces a new page however the text above changes.

questions.stem: Dangriga Church wants to include its typed 1970 history in a new booklet AND edit the wording. After scanning the pages, what technology turns them into editable text?
questions.explain: Optical Character Recognition converts images of text into editable characters.

questions.stem: St. Kitts–Nevis Ferry timetable table needs the title “Weekend Sailings” across the full width of its top row of four cells. What should be done?
questions.explain: Merging the four top cells makes one wide cell for the title.

questions.stem: The Wallblake Road Café menu lists prices such as $4.50, $12.75 and $105.00 down the right of the page. Which tab stop lines the prices up on the decimal point?
questions.explain: A decimal tab stop aligns numbers on their decimal point.

questions.stem: Kayla presses Enter at the end of every line while typing a paragraph. When she later changes the margins, her lines break in strange places. What should she have done?
options: Used a page break after each line
Let word wrap move text to the next line and pressed Enter only at the end of the paragraph
Pressed Tab at the end of each line
questions.explain: Word wrap adjusts automatically; hard returns at the end of every line do not.

questions.stem: A newsletter column for the Barbados Youth Choir has straight left AND right edges. This alignment is called
questions.explain: Fully justified text adjusts word spacing so both margins are straight.

questions.stem: Which formatting choice is MOST appropriate for a formal letter from Coralstone College's principal to parents?
options: Three decorative fonts and clip art
Yellow text on a white background
One clear font at 11–12 pt with the school letterhead in the header
questions.explain: Formal letters need clear, consistent, professional formatting.

questions.stem: Sasha selects a paragraph in her report on Corozal Market and presses the Delete key, intending to paste it on page 4. What happens when she presses Ctrl+V on page 4?
options: Word asks where the paragraph should go
Nothing from that paragraph is pasted, because Delete does not place text on the clipboard
The paragraph is restored to its original place
questions.explain: Delete removes text without copying it to the clipboard. She should have used Cut (Ctrl+X).

questions.stem: Tyrese wants a COPY of a table of ferry prices further down the same page, using the mouse only. What should he do?
options: Hold Shift while clicking the table
Hold Ctrl while dragging the selected table
Drag the selected table to the new place
questions.explain: Dragging moves; holding Ctrl while dragging copies.

questions.stem: The Anguilla Ferry Co. timetable has one destination formatted perfectly. Nia wants to apply the same formatting to nine other destinations scattered around the page without clicking the button nine times. What should she do?
options: Copy and paste the formatted destination nine times
Double-click Format Painter, paint all nine, then press Esc
questions.explain: Double-clicking locks the Format Painter on until you press Esc.

questions.stem: A teacher replaces every “art” with “visual arts” in a timetable. Now the timetable says “visual artsists” and “stvisual arts”. Which option would have prevented this?
questions.explain: Whole words only stops matches inside longer words such as “artists” and “start”.

questions.stem: Devon accidentally applies bold to his entire 10-page SBA report. What is the quickest fix?
options: Close without saving and lose today's work
questions.explain: Undo (Ctrl+Z) reverses the last action.

questions.stem: An essay competition run by the Caribbean Youth Writers' Network has a 750-word limit. Where can Keisha find the exact number of words in her essay?
options: Review ▸ Word Count or the status bar
questions.explain: Word count is on the status bar and in Review ▸ Word Count.

questions.stem: Which error would a spelling checker MOST likely fail to detect?
options: Teh ferry leaves at 7 a.m. from Marigot.
The ferry leaves at 7 a.m. frm Marigot.
The ferry leavs at 7 a.m. from Marigot.
The ferry leaves at 7 a.m. form Marigot.
questions.explain: “form” is a real word used wrongly, so it passes the dictionary check.

questions.stem: In a speech for Curaçao Youth Parliament, Jaden used “important” seven times. Which tool helps him find alternatives?
questions.explain: The thesaurus suggests synonyms such as vital, essential or significant.

questions.stem: Ms. Hodge wants to ask a student whether a statistic in his report is from a reliable source, without changing his text. What should she use?
questions.explain: A comment adds a note in the margin without altering the text.

questions.stem: With Track Changes on, Kerry-Ann deletes the word “Friday” and types “Saturday”. In All Markup view, how do these changes usually appear?
options: Friday is struck through; Saturday is underlined
Friday is underlined; Saturday is struck through
questions.explain: Deletions are struck through (or in a balloon); insertions are underlined.

questions.stem: A reviewer changed “Brades” to “Braddes” in a tracked document. What should the author do with this change?
questions.explain: The change introduces a spelling error, so reject it to restore the original.

questions.stem: The Lelydorp Construction keeps a document of staff salaries. Only the director should be able to open it. Which feature is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Encryption with a password prevents anyone without it from opening the file.

questions.stem: The Mahoe Grove High School PTA sends a Word form where parents tick boxes and type names but must not alter the questions. Which protection should be used?
questions.explain: Filling in forms allows input only in form fields/controls.

questions.stem: Which statement about Mark as Final is TRUE?
options: It stops anyone from opening the document
It discourages editing, but users can choose Edit Anyway
questions.explain: Mark as Final is a weak, advisory protection.

questions.stem: While correcting “Paramaribo” in a letter, Ana notices that every letter she types replaces the letter to the right of the cursor. Which mode is on?
questions.explain: In Overtype mode new characters replace existing ones; Insert mode pushes text along.

questions.stem: A power cut hits the Santiago de los Caballeros Library while Dario is typing. When he restarts Word, it offers a recovered version of his document. Which feature made this possible?
questions.explain: AutoRecover saves recovery information at intervals (10 minutes by default).

questions.stem: The cursor is between the letters “Ma” and “rigot”. Which key removes the letter “a”?
questions.explain: Backspace deletes to the left of the cursor; Delete removes to the right.

questions.stem: A student is about to e-mail her finished SBA report. Which should she do LAST?
options: Accept or reject all tracked changes
questions.explain: Protection comes last; you cannot easily review or edit a protected document.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: Simone wants Word to generate a TOC for her 18-page report on the English Harbour Fish Fry. What must she do to her headings first?
options: Apply heading styles such as Heading 1 and Heading 2
questions.explain: Word builds a TOC from heading styles, not from appearance.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: After generating a TOC, Marlon added a new section called “Interviews”. Which TOC update option should he choose?
questions.explain: Adding or renaming headings requires the entire table to be updated.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: Where is the Table of Contents command found in Microsoft Word?
questions.explain: References ▸ Table of Contents.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: In a mail merge for the Jolly Harbour Yacht Club's annual dinner invitations, what is the primary document?
options: The invitation containing standard text and merge fields
questions.explain: The primary (main) document holds the standard text and the merge fields.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: The Falmouth Dental Clinic keeps patient names and addresses in an Access table that it uses for appointment reminder letters. In the mail merge, the Access table is the
questions.explain: The table of variable details is the data source.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: In a data source of 500 APUA-style utility customers, one row containing a single customer's details is called a
questions.explain: One row = one record.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: A data source stores full names in one field (“Ms. Shanice Hodge”). Why is this a problem for the greeting “Dear Ms. Hodge,”?
options: The letter will be too long
Mail merge only works with numbers
The title and surname cannot be inserted separately
questions.explain: Separate Title, FirstName and LastName fields give flexible greetings and sorting.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: A filter is set to District Equal to English Harbour AND Balance Greater than 0. Which customer is included?
questions.explain: With AND, both conditions must be true.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: The Dickenson Bay Ferry Co. wants letters for passengers from Barbuda or Montserrat. Which filter is correct?
questions.explain: A passenger can only have one home island, so OR is needed.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: Kezia set up the first mailing label with Address Block. The other labels are still empty apart from «Next Record». What should she click?
questions.explain: Update Labels copies the first label's layout to all other labels.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: Before printing 400 letters, why should the PTA secretary use Preview Results?
options: It sends the letters by e-mail
It shows actual data in the letter so errors can be fixed before merging
questions.explain: Preview shows real records so problems such as missing spaces are caught.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: Andre cannot find the Check Box and Drop-Down List controls to build a club sign-up form. What should he do?
options: File ▸ Options ▸ Customize Ribbon ▸ tick Developer
questions.explain: Form controls are on the Developer tab, which is hidden by default.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: A sign-up form for Antiguan Science Fair asks students to choose their school from five options. Which control is BEST?
questions.explain: A drop-down limits answers to valid choices and prevents spelling variations.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: Which setting allows users to complete form controls but not change any other part of the document?
questions.explain: Filling in forms locks everything except the controls.

questions.topic: Table of contents, mail merge and fillable forms
questions.stem: The St. John’s Library wants every member to start with a fresh, blank copy of its protected form. How should it save the form?
questions.explain: Opening a template creates a new document based on it, leaving the original blank.

questions.stem: Before building a website for St. Kitts Heritage Trust, which TWO things should be decided first?
options: The domain name and hosting company
questions.explain: Purpose and audience drive every other design decision.

questions.stem: Which planning tool shows all the pages of a website and how they are linked?
questions.explain: A site map shows pages and links; a wireframe shows one page's layout.

questions.stem: Jamal sketches boxes labelled Logo, Menu, Main text, Photo and Footer for the Contact page of the Barbados Surf School site. What has he produced?
questions.explain: A wireframe sketches one page's layout.

questions.stem: Which file name should be used for the home page of a website so the server opens it automatically?
questions.explain: Servers look for index.html by default; lowercase, no spaces.

questions.stem: The Antigua Sailing Week site has a home page linking to Races, Results, Parties and Contact, and Results links to one page per day. Which navigation structure is this?
questions.explain: A tree from the home page down is hierarchical.

questions.stem: An online tutorial for the Guyana Coding Club moves from Lesson 1 to Lesson 2 to Lesson 3 using Next and Back buttons only. Which structure is this?
questions.explain: Sequential pages with Next/Back are linear.

questions.stem: Why should the navigation bar appear in the same place on every page of the Trinidad Steelband Festival site?
options: It makes the site load faster
Visitors always know where to find links and do not get lost
questions.explain: Consistent navigation improves usability.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN purpose of alt text on an image?
options: To link the image to another page
To describe the image for screen readers and when it fails to load
questions.explain: Alt text is the text alternative to the image.

questions.stem: Which is the BEST alt text for a photo on the Jamaica Coffee Farm site?
options: Image of an image of coffee
Farm workers picking ripe red coffee cherries on a hillside
questions.explain: Good alt text briefly describes what matters in the image.

questions.stem: The text “Hellshire Beach Eco Club” appears on the browser tab. Which HTML element sets this?
questions.explain: The title element in the head sets the tab text.

questions.stem: Which image format is MOST suitable for a photograph of a Carnival parade on a web page?
questions.explain: JPEG compresses photographs efficiently.

questions.stem: The Les Cayes Bakery logo has a transparent background and sharp edges. Which format suits it best?
questions.explain: PNG supports transparency and keeps edges sharp (SVG also suits logos).

questions.stem: A page for the Liberta Marina loads slowly on phones because of its photos. What is the BEST fix?
options: Resize and compress the photos before uploading
questions.explain: Smaller image files download faster.

questions.stem: The Palmetto Point Secondary PTA has no budget and no one who can code, and needs a site this week. Which approach is MOST suitable?
options: Save a spreadsheet as a web page
A free online website builder with a template
questions.explain: A builder needs no coding and includes hosting and templates.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST distinguishes a website from a web page, using Antigua Carnival Committee as an example?
options: A web page is one document shown in a browser; the website is the collection of linked pages under the committee's domain
A website is one document; a web page is a collection of documents
A website is stored on your computer; a web page is stored on a server
They mean exactly the same thing
questions.explain: One page versus a collection of related pages owned by one organisation under one domain.

questions.stem: Keon copies his finished pages from his laptop to the hosting company's server so the public can see them. This is called
questions.explain: Sending files from your computer to a server is uploading.

questions.stem: Which organisation oversees the system of domain names and top-level domains such as .gd and .com worldwide?
questions.explain: ICANN coordinates domain names and delegates top-level domains to registries.

questions.stem: On the Nevis Heritage Trust site, the browser first downloads index.html, which immediately redirects to welcome.html, the main page with the introduction and links. Which statement is correct?
options: index.html is the index page (first page downloaded); welcome.html is the home page (main page)
index.html is the home page and welcome.html is the index page
questions.explain: The index page is the first page downloaded; the home page is the main page. Usually they are the same, but not here.

questions.stem: Which BEST defines a web host?
options: A person or company that provides space on a web server for your website
The first page of a website
questions.explain: The host is the provider; the server is the computer.

questions.stem: Consider the URL http://www.nevispages.com/news.htm. What is the domain name?
questions.explain: The domain name is nevispages.com; www names the server and is not part of the domain name; news.htm is the page file; .com is the extension.

questions.stem: When publishing and viewing the Montserrat Volcano Tours site, which protocols are normally used?
options: FTP to upload pages to the server, HTTP/HTTPS to download pages into a browser
HTTP to upload pages, FTP to view them
questions.explain: FTP transfers files up to the server; HTTP fetches pages for viewing.

questions.stem:
Which line of HTML creates the MOST important heading on a page about Montserrat Volcano Tours?

A) h1 element B) h6 element C) head element D) title element
questions.explain: h1 is the top-level heading; head and title are not visible headings.

questions.stem: Which HTML element is used to create every type of hyperlink on the Guyana Rainforest Tours website?
questions.explain: Links use the anchor element with an href attribute.

questions.stem: In the anchor element, what does the href attribute specify?
questions.explain: href is the hypertext reference: the link's destination.

questions.stem: The Antigua Sailing Club wants a link that opens a new e-mail to its secretary. The href must start with
questions.explain: mailto: opens the visitor's e-mail program.

questions.stem: A long FAQ page for the St. Lucia Jazz Festival has a heading with id="tickets". Which href jumps to it from the top of the same page?
questions.explain: A hash followed by the id targets a bookmark on the same page.

questions.stem: A bookmark link uses href="#Contact" but the target has id="contact". What is the MOST likely result?
options: The link does not jump to the section
questions.explain: Fragment identifiers must match exactly, including case.

questions.stem: In Microsoft Word, which shortcut opens the Insert Link dialog?
questions.explain: Ctrl+K opens Insert ▸ Link.

questions.stem: In Word's Insert Link dialog, which option links to a bookmark or heading in the same document?
questions.explain: Place in This Document lists bookmarks and headings.

questions.stem: Grenada Spice Co-op links its price list, which it made in Excel, from its website. This is a link to
questions.explain: A file the organisation created is a user-created file.

questions.stem: On the Dominica Hiking Club gallery page, each small picture opens a large version when tapped. The small pictures are called
questions.explain: Thumbnails are small images that act as links.

questions.stem: A link to files/menu.pdf worked on Tia's laptop but gives “404 Not Found” on the published site. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The browser does not support PDF links
The PDF was not uploaded to the files folder on the server
The link text is too long
questions.explain: The file must be uploaded to the location the link points to.

questions.stem: Which link text is BEST for accessibility on the Belize Reef Trust site?
questions.explain: Link text should describe the destination even when read on its own.

questions.stem: While evaluating the Bahamas Weather Watch site, a student notes that the page shows when it was last updated and names the meteorological office as its source. Which criterion does this support?
questions.explain: Date and source help judge whether information is accurate and current.

questions.stem: The Curaçao Dive Centre site needs sideways scrolling on a phone and its text is tiny. Which criterion is weak?
questions.explain: The layout does not adapt to small screens.

questions.stem: Which change would MOST improve the load time of a home page containing eight 5 MB photos?
questions.explain: Smaller image files download faster.

questions.stem: When should a website be tested?
options: Never, if a builder is used
During building, before publishing and again after publishing
questions.explain: Some problems only appear after upload, so test at every stage.

questions.stem: On the Tobago Turtle Trust page, the words “Adopt a turtle” are underlined and link to adopt.html. What are these clickable words called?
questions.explain: The text that is linked from is the anchor text.

questions.stem: Which is the BEST reason to view a new page in a web browser on your own computer before uploading it?
options: It makes the page load faster online
Some features only become apparent when the page is viewed in a browser
questions.explain: Previewing in a browser reveals problems before visitors see them.

questions.stem: Traditionally, which two colours did browsers use for unvisited and visited hyperlinks?
questions.explain: Blue for links and magenta/purple for visited links, usually underlined.

questions.stem: How can the Barbados Senior Citizens' Club check that its new website suits its intended audience?
options: Invite some club members to try the site and observe their reactions
Ask the web designer's teenage friends
questions.explain: Test with people who fit the intended audience and watch how they use it.

questions.stem: Kemar tells his classmate that a spreadsheet is 'just a table in Word'. Which statement BEST explains how a spreadsheet differs?
options: A spreadsheet recalculates formulas automatically when data changes
A spreadsheet can only hold numbers
questions.explain: Automatic calculation and recalculation is what makes a spreadsheet different from a word-processed table.

questions.stem: The active cell in a grade-book sheet is where column F meets row 12. What does the Name Box show?
questions.explain: Column letter first, then row number: F12.

questions.stem: A teacher at Sandbox Tree College selects the range B3:E10 to format test scores. How many cells are selected?
questions.explain: B–E is 4 columns; rows 3–10 is 8 rows; 4 × 8 = 32.

questions.stem: Cell H7 in a hotel's booking sheet displays 1,575. When the receptionist clicks H7, the formula bar shows =F7*G7. Which statement is TRUE?
options: The formula bar is showing the wrong cell
H7 contains a formula and displays its result
questions.explain: The formula bar shows the true contents (a formula); the cell displays the result.

questions.stem: The St. John’s cruise port tour operator keeps January, February and March sales on three tabs in one file called Tours2026.xlsx. What is Tours2026.xlsx?
questions.explain: The file is the workbook; each tab is a worksheet.

questions.stem: In a school canteen sheet, which entry is a LABEL?
questions.explain: Chicken roti is text describing data.

questions.stem: A Grenada farmer changes the price of nutmeg in cell B2 to see how her income in B10 would change. This is an example of…
questions.explain: Changing inputs to see the effect on results is what-if analysis (modelling).

questions.stem: After typing 1250000 into a narrow column, Shaquille sees ####### in the cell. What is the BEST action?
questions.explain: ##### means the column is too narrow to show the number. Widen it.

questions.stem: Daniella types 'Mon' in A2 and drags the fill handle down to A8. What appears in A8?
questions.explain: AutoFill continues the days: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun (A2–A8).

questions.stem: Which entry will a spreadsheet treat as a formula?
questions.explain: A formula must begin with =. An apostrophe forces text.

questions.stem: Which task is BEST suited to a spreadsheet rather than a word processor?
options: Calculating monthly loan repayments for different interest rates
Writing a cover letter for a job at Douglas-Charles Airport
questions.explain: Calculating and comparing repayments for different rates is numeric what-if modelling.

questions.stem: A Barbados school's student IDs start with zeros, e.g. 00321. When typed into a cell they show as 321. How should the IDs be entered?
options: Format the cells as Text or type an apostrophe first
questions.explain: Text format or a leading apostrophe stores the ID as a label and keeps the zeros.

questions.stem: Without typing a formula, Andre wants a quick total of the selected cells D2:D40. Where can he look?
questions.explain: The status bar shows Sum, Average and Count for the selection.

questions.stem: A bakery in Trinidad typed 2000 instead of 200 for flour costs and the sheet showed a huge loss. This illustrates…
questions.explain: Wrong input gives wrong output, however accurately calculated.

questions.stem: Which correctly refers to the cells from A2 down to A20?
questions.explain: A colon separates the first and last cells of a range.

questions.stem: In a sheet, B4 contains =B2*B3 and B7 contains =B4-B5. B2 is changed. Which cells recalculate?
questions.explain: B4 depends on B2, and B7 depends on B4.

questions.stem: In which column and which row does the cell P64 lie?
questions.explain: A cell address is the column letter followed by the row number.

questions.stem: Mrs. Hodge gives her Form 4 class a spreadsheet that already has the formulas, formatting and layout for a weekly budget; students only add their own figures. What is this called?
questions.explain: A template is pre-prepared with formulas, formatting and layout.

questions.stem: Jamal wants 2026 in A1 to be treated as a label so it is never used in a calculation. What should he type?
questions.explain: An apostrophe in front makes the entry a label.

questions.stem: A teacher's grade book has 900 rows and she needs cell K850 quickly. Which key opens the Go To box?
questions.explain: F5 (or Ctrl + G) opens Go To.

questions.stem: How many cells are in the range D4:G9?
questions.explain: D–G is 4 columns; 4–9 is 6 rows; 4 × 6 = 24.

questions.stem: Javon wants C2 to show the cost of 6 tickets at the price in B2. Which formula is correct?
questions.explain: The asterisk * is the multiplication operator, and formulas start with =.

questions.stem: A cell contains =10+6/2. What does it display?
questions.explain: Division first: 6/2 = 3, then 10 + 3 = 13.

questions.stem: Test scores for a Montserrat student are in B5, C5 and D5. Which formula correctly calculates her average?
questions.explain: Brackets force the addition first. =AVERAGE(B5,D5) would ignore C5.

questions.stem: A tuck-shop sheet has prices in B2:B20. Three cells say 'TBA' and two are empty; the rest are numbers. What does =COUNT(B2:B20) return?
questions.explain: 19 cells − 3 text − 2 empty = 14 numbers.

questions.stem: Which formula counts how many runners in C2:C40 finished in under 60 seconds?
questions.explain: Range first, then the criteria in quotation marks.

questions.stem: D4 contains 49.5. What does =IF(D4>=50,"Merit","Keep going") display?
questions.explain: 49.5 is not ≥ 50, so the value-if-false is shown.

questions.stem: Which operator means 'not equal to' in a spreadsheet?
questions.explain: <> means not equal to.

questions.stem: A tour operator's table in A2:D30 has Tour code, Tour name, Duration, Price. Which formula returns the PRICE of the code in G2?
questions.explain: Price is the 4th column of the table; FALSE for an exact code match.

questions.stem: A cashier types code X999 into a VLOOKUP order form and sees #N/A. Why?
options: X999 is not in the first column of the lookup table
questions.explain: #N/A means the lookup value was not found.

questions.stem: Golf scores are in B2:B12; the LOWEST score wins. Which formula ranks the player in row 2 correctly?
questions.explain: Order 1 ranks ascending, so the smallest score is 1st.

questions.stem: Which formula always shows the current date?
questions.explain: TODAY needs empty brackets and an equals sign.

questions.stem: B2 holds 01/12/2026 and C2 holds 25/12/2026. What does =C2-B2 display when formatted as a number?
questions.explain: 25 − 1 = 24 days between the dates.

questions.stem: Kayla typed =AVERGE(B2:B9). What will the cell show?
questions.explain: A misspelt function name gives #NAME?.

questions.stem: The formula =B2/C2 shows #DIV/0!. Which is the most likely cause?
questions.explain: Dividing by zero or an empty cell causes #DIV/0!.
64 fails ≥80 and ≥65 but passes ≥50: C.

questions.stem: What does =2^3+1 display?
A youth cricket camp in Antigua accepts players aged 13 to 16 inclusive. Age is in C2. Which formula returns TRUE only for eligible players?
questions.explain: Both conditions must hold, so AND; >= and <= include 13 and 16. OR would be true for every age, and the last option is not valid Excel syntax.

questions.stem: Which of these is a LOGICAL TEST that could be used inside an IF function?
questions.explain: A logical test has a TRUE or FALSE answer. B2<>"Paid" asks whether B2 is not equal to Paid.

questions.stem: D2 holds a citizen's age, 17. What does =IF(D2<=17,"Non-voting age","Voting age") display?
questions.explain: 17 <= 17 is TRUE, so the value-if-true is shown.

questions.stem: A student is given PASS if the mark is OVER 60, else FAIL. Mark is in B4 and equals 60. Which formula is correct, and what does it show?
questions.explain: 'Over 60' means > 60, so exactly 60 fails.

questions.stem: Which function displays the current date AND time?
questions.explain: NOW returns date and time; TODAY returns only the date.

questions.stem: In a Guyana rice farm sheet, yields are in C2:C25. Which formula finds the smallest yield?
questions.explain: MIN returns the smallest number in a range.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: Cell D3 contains =B3+C3. It is copied to D9. What does D9 contain?
questions.explain: Six rows down: 3 → 9 in both references.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: In the formula =C4*$F$1, what does $F$1 mean?
options: F1 will change when the formula is copied
F1 will not change when the formula is copied
questions.explain: $ locks both column and row; it has nothing to do with currency.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: Tariq has typed =B4*D1 and his cursor is just after D1. He presses F4 once. What does the formula become?
questions.explain: The first press of F4 makes the reference fully absolute.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: A Curaçao travel agent stores the exchange rate in H2 and prices in B5:B40. Which formula in C5 converts the price and can be copied down?
questions.explain: The price moves; the rate is locked.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: In which reference is only the ROW locked?
questions.explain: The $ is in front of 7, the row number.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: G2 contains =SUM(B2:F2). It is copied to G3. What is in G3?
questions.explain: One row down: 2 → 3.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: Cell B2 is named VAT. Which formula is equivalent to =C5*$B$2?
questions.explain: A name can replace the absolute reference directly.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a valid range name?
questions.explain: Names cannot contain spaces.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: To keep row 1 and column A visible while scrolling, which cell should be selected before Freeze Panes?
questions.explain: Freeze Panes freezes rows above and columns left of the active cell.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: A total in B10 is =SUM(B2:B9). A row is inserted above row 5. What and where is the total now?
questions.explain: The total moves down one row and the range expands.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: A Jamaican shop's formulas all use the rate in $C$1. Someone deletes column C. What do the formulas show?
questions.explain: The referenced cell no longer exists.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: Rhea wants to send a supplier her price list without the formulas. What should she use?
questions.explain: Paste Values keeps only the results.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: Cell E2 contains =C2*D2. It is CUT and pasted into E8. What is in E8?
questions.explain: Moving a formula does not change its references.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: Sales are in B2:B11 and the total in B12. Which formula in C2 gives each item's share and can be copied down?
questions.explain: The part moves; the total is locked.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: Columns D and E are hidden. Which selection lets you unhide them?
questions.explain: Select the columns on both sides of the hidden ones, then Unhide.

questions.topic: Replicating formulae, absolute addressing and named ranges
questions.stem: C2 contains =SUM($B$2:B2). What does C6 contain after copying down?
questions.explain: The locked start stays; the relative end moves.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: Cell B4 in a Barbados credit union's sheet holds 0.065. It is formatted as Percentage with 1 decimal place. What does it show?

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: Which number format lines up the $ signs at the left edge of the cell and shows zeros as a dash?
questions.explain: That is the Accounting format.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: A cell shows 4.57 because it is formatted to 2 decimal places, but the formula bar shows 4.5678. What value does =A1*100 use?
questions.explain: Formulas use the stored 4.5678, giving 456.78.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: A heading 'Number of passengers (adults)' is too long for its column. Which feature keeps it inside the cell on several lines?
questions.explain: Wrap Text breaks the text onto multiple lines within the cell.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: A teacher wants every mark below 50 to turn red automatically. Which feature should she use?
questions.explain: Conditional formatting applies formatting when a condition is met.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet list of Piarco Airport flight arrivals, each row holds one flight's number, airline, time and gate. What is one row called?
questions.explain: A row of data about one item is a record.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: A list of Guyana rice-farm yields is sorted in descending order of Yield. Which farm appears first?
options: The farm name starting with A
questions.explain: Descending means largest to smallest.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: A list is sorted by Parish, then by Surname. What is Surname?
questions.explain: The second sort field is the secondary key; it orders records within each parish.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: Leon selects only column C (Scores) and sorts it, ignoring Excel's warning. What is the result?
options: Scores no longer match the students' names
questions.explain: Only the scores move, so records are split apart.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: An AutoFilter is set on a list of 200 Carnival troupe members to show only 'Section = Blue Waves'. What happens to the other records?
options: They are sorted to the bottom
They move to a new sheet
questions.explain: Filtered-out records are hidden, not deleted.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: In an Advanced Filter criteria range, two conditions are typed on the SAME row. How are they combined?
questions.explain: Same row = AND; different rows = OR.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: A Jamaican supermarket chain has 50,000 sales records and wants total sales by store and month. Which tool is MOST efficient?
questions.explain: A pivot table summarises large lists by categories quickly.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: Source data for a pivot table is corrected. What must be done for the pivot to show the new figures?
questions.explain: Pivot tables update only when refreshed.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: A 6-page printout of a hotel's guest list has headings only on page 1. Which feature puts them on every page?
questions.explain: Print Titles repeats rows at the top of each printed page.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: Which keyboard shortcut switches the sheet between showing values and showing formulas?
questions.explain: Ctrl + ` (the grave accent) toggles Show Formulas.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: The VICTORY COLLEGE results sheet has two title rows at the top and a totals row at the bottom. Before a Custom Sort on Average Marks, what should be highlighted?
options: The whole sheet including titles and totals
The headings and data only, excluding the title rows and the totals row
questions.explain: Titles and totals must stay where they are; only the records (with their headings) are sorted.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: A sales sheet lists products and their Quarter 3 sales. To extract the products whose Quarter 3 sales were more than 5000, which filter option should be used on the Quarter 3 column?
questions.explain: Number Filters ▸ Greater Than, then type 5000.

questions.topic: Formatting, sorting, filtering and pivot tables
questions.stem: A Montserrat school records an exam date stored as 46142. Which format shows it as 30-Apr-26?
questions.explain: dd-mmm-yy gives day, short month name and 2-digit year.

questions.stem: The Meteorological Department of Trinidad and Tobago wants to show how rainfall changed each month from June to November. Which chart is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Change over time is best shown with a line chart.

questions.stem: A family wants to show what share of their monthly income goes to rent, food, transport and savings. Which chart?
questions.explain: Shares of one total: pie chart.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to display the total score of each of 25 students. Which chart is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Individual scores are categories to compare, not parts of a whole or a time series.

questions.stem: A chart shows two data series: 2025 sales and 2026 sales. Which element tells the reader which colour is which year?
questions.explain: The legend is the key to the series colours.

questions.stem: On a column chart of money raised per class, which axis title is BEST for the vertical axis?
questions.explain: The value axis title names the measure and units.

questions.stem: To chart country names in column A and figures in column C (skipping B), what should you do while selecting?
questions.explain: Ctrl lets you select non-adjacent ranges.

questions.stem: Ms. Daniel wants the chart to fill its own sheet named PIE. Which command?
questions.explain: Move Chart places the chart on a new chart sheet.

questions.stem: Which formula refers to cell D4 on a sheet named Feb?
questions.explain: SheetName!Cell.

questions.stem: Which formula correctly uses B3 on a sheet named Exchange Rates?
questions.explain: Names with spaces go in single quotes.

questions.stem: A workbook has sheets Week1 to Week4 in order, each with total sales in E10. Which formula adds all four?
questions.explain: First sheet:last sheet!cell.

questions.stem: Summary!C5 contains =Jan!C5. Jan!C5 changes from 80 to 95. What does Summary!C5 show?
questions.explain: Linked cells update automatically.

questions.stem: What is the quickest way to rename a sheet tab?
questions.explain: Double-click (or right-click ▸ Rename).

questions.stem: Shanelle copies a table of prices from a Word document and pastes it into Excel. What is this called?
questions.explain: Bringing data in from outside the spreadsheet program is importing.

questions.stem: Which BEST describes a spreadsheet template?
options: A pre-prepared spreadsheet with formulas, formatting and layout already set up
questions.explain: Templates are ready-made designs: you add data.

questions.stem: A clerk at a Trinidad shipping agency formats a new sheet the same way every week. Which feature can do all the steps in one action?
questions.explain: Macros record and replay a sequence of steps.

questions.stem: A chart legend shows 'Series1' and the axis shows 1, 2, 3 instead of quarter names. What is the BEST fix?
options: Change the chart to a pie
Use Select Data to edit the series name and axis labels
questions.explain: Select Data ▸ Edit lets you choose the label cells.

questions.stem: A Form 4 student at Bayleaf Hill Secondary writes four definitions of a database in the notes. Which one would earn full marks in Paper 02?
options: A large spreadsheet with many rows
Any file saved on a computer
An organised collection of related data that can be easily accessed, managed and updated
A program used to store data
questions.explain: A database is an organised collection of related data. A program is a DBMS, and a spreadsheet or any file is not necessarily organised related data.

questions.stem: The Grand Anse Market co-operative installs a program that lets staff create tables, run queries and print reports about vendors. What is this program?
questions.explain: Software that creates and manages databases is a DBMS. The vendor data it holds is the database.

questions.stem: Gouyave Guesthouse's tblGuest has a heading row and 18 rows of guest data, each with 7 columns. How many records and fields does it have?
questions.explain: Each guest row is a record (18; the heading row is not a record) and each column is a field (7).

questions.stem: In a textbook from Trinidad, a table is described as a relation, a row as a tuple and a column as an attribute. Which everyday database word means the same as attribute?
questions.explain: Attribute = field (column). Tuple = record (row).

questions.stem: The Grenville Clinic stores patient phone numbers such as 543-0912. A volunteer suggests the Number data type. Why is Text better?
options: Number fields cannot hold seven digits
Text fields are faster to sort
Phone numbers contain symbols like dashes and are never used in calculations
Text fields use less storage than numbers
questions.explain: Phone numbers contain non-numeric symbols and are never added or averaged, so Text is correct.

questions.stem: Island Power, an electricity company, records the amount due on each bill. Which data type is MOST suitable for AmountDue?
questions.explain: Money values should use Currency, which shows $ and two decimal places and avoids rounding errors.

questions.stem: The La Sagesse Community Centre records whether each child has a signed photo consent form. Which data type should the field PhotoConsent use?
questions.explain: Only two possible values: logical (Boolean) Yes/No.

questions.stem: The Carriacou Ferry Line's PASSENGER table has the fields PassengerName, DateOfBirth, Nationality and PassportNo. Which field is the BEST primary key?
questions.explain: A passport number is unique to each traveller. Names, birthdays and nationalities repeat.

questions.stem: In the Grenadian Carnival Committee database, SECTION (SectionID, SectionName, Leader) and MASQUERADER (MasqID, Name, Phone, SectionID). What is SectionID in MASQUERADER?
questions.explain: SectionID is SECTION's primary key copied into MASQUERADER to link the tables: a foreign key.

questions.stem: A CXC results table stores StudentNo, SubjectCode and Grade. A student sits many subjects and each subject is sat by many students. What should the primary key be?
options: StudentNo and SubjectCode together (a composite key)
questions.explain: Neither field is unique alone, but each student–subject pair occurs once, so they form a composite key.

questions.stem: The librarian at Island Reads often searches for members by LastName, even though several members share the same surname. LastName is an example of a:
questions.explain: A non-unique field used for searching or sorting is a secondary key.

questions.stem: A Jamaican youth club stores member addresses on every attendance row of one spreadsheet. The club's file is large and slow because the same addresses appear hundreds of times. This is called:
questions.explain: Storing the same data more than once is data redundancy.

questions.stem: At Young Street Bakery, one customer can place many orders, but each order is placed by one customer. What is the relationship between CUSTOMER and ORDER?
questions.explain: One customer, many orders; each order has one customer: one-to-many.

questions.stem: Students at Seagrape Bay Secondary School can join many clubs and each club has many students. How should a database designer store this relationship?
options: Create a linking table holding StudentID and ClubID
Put a ClubID field in the STUDENT table
Merge both tables into one flat file
Put a StudentID field in the CLUB table
questions.explain: A many-to-many relationship is resolved with a linking (junction) table, giving two one-to-many relationships.

questions.stem: A small Barbados craft shop is told a database will cost money for software and training. Which of these is ALSO a genuine limitation of using a database?
options: A single failure or security breach can affect all the data at once
questions.explain: The other three are advantages. Centralised data means one failure or breach affects everything, so backups and security are essential.

questions.stem: Your teacher asks her Form 4 class at Flamboyant Heights College for an example of a MANUAL database. Which answer is correct?
options: A MySQL server at a hotel
A telephone directory printed on paper
questions.explain: A manual database is kept on paper: telephone directories, library card catalogues, patient record cards and printed voter lists.

questions.stem: In the Hummingbird Ridge High School database, all the fields describing one student (ID, name, gender, date of birth) together form a:
questions.explain: A collection of related fields about one entity is a record (tuple).

questions.stem: Jaden is choosing data types in Microsoft Access for his SBA. Which of these is NOT a data type available in Access?
questions.explain: Access offers Short Text, Number, Yes/No, Currency, Date/Time and others, but no data type called Character.

questions.stem: In the Storms database from class, the column Category holds a value for every hurricane. Which formal term describes a column of data in a table?
questions.explain: A column is a field, formally an attribute. A tuple is a row (record).

questions.stem: In tblStudent, both StudentID and CXCCandidateNo are unique. What is any field that COULD be used as the primary key called?
questions.explain: Any field (or combination) able to act as the primary key is a candidate key.

questions.stem: Kezia is building her SBA database for an Antigua guesthouse. She needs to add a field and change another field's data type. Which view must she use?
questions.explain: Field names, data types and properties are all part of the structure, edited in Design View.

questions.stem: The Island Reads Library wants today's date to appear automatically in DateOut for each new loan. Which property and setting achieves this?
questions.explain: Default Value fills in a value for new records; Date() returns today's date. A rule of =Date() would reject any other date.

questions.stem: A Barbados swim club records each swimmer's age. Members must be from 8 to 17 years old inclusive. Which validation rule is correct?
questions.explain: Between includes both ends. >8 And <17 rejects 8 and 17; the Or version accepts every number.

questions.stem: A Trinidad school's tblStudent has a House field. Valid houses are Red, Blue and Gold. Which validation rule is correct?
questions.explain: In checks the value against a list. No value can equal all three at once, and Like "R*" only allows words starting with R.

questions.stem: The BZE Taxi Association uses the input mask >LL\-000 for permit codes. What would be stored if a dispatcher types tx482?
questions.explain: > converts letters to uppercase, LL requires two letters, \- shows a dash, 000 requires three digits.

questions.stem: A student sets the validation rule >=0 on a Price field but leaves Validation Text blank. A user types -5. What happens?
options: Access rejects it and shows its own general error message
questions.explain: The rule still works; without validation text the user sees a system message instead of a friendly one.

questions.stem: At Willemstad Dental Clinic, every patient record must include a LastName. Which field property setting enforces this?
questions.explain: Required = Yes means the field cannot be left blank: a presence check.

questions.stem: In tblCustomer, CustomerID is an AutoNumber primary key. In tblOrder, CustomerID will be the foreign key. Which data type should it be in tblOrder?
questions.explain: AutoNumber is stored as a Long Integer, so the foreign key must be Number (Long Integer).

questions.stem: In a Jamaican school's tblExamEntry, StudentID and SubjectCode together must form the primary key. How is this set in Design View?
options: Type both field names into one row
Set StudentID as the key, then set SubjectCode as the key
Set Indexed to Yes on both fields
Hold Ctrl, select both row selectors, then click Primary Key
questions.explain: Selecting both rows together and clicking Primary Key creates one composite key; doing them separately replaces the first key.

questions.stem: Rohan wants to link tblTeam and tblPlayer in his SBA about a St. Kitts football league. Where does he create a permanent relationship?
questions.explain: Relationships are created in the Relationships window on the Database Tools tab.

questions.stem: Referential integrity is enforced between tblPatient and tblVisit at an Old Road clinic. A receptionist tries to add a visit for PatientID 450, but there is no patient 450. What happens?
options: The visit is saved with a blank patient
The visit is saved and a warning is printed later
questions.explain: A foreign key value must match an existing primary key, so the orphan record is refused.

questions.stem: Cascade Delete Related Records is ticked between tblMember and tblLoan at a library. A librarian deletes a member who has five loans. What happens?
options: The member and all five related loans are deleted
The loans are moved to another member
Only the member is deleted; the loans remain
questions.explain: Cascade Delete automatically deletes the related records along with the parent record.

questions.stem: In the Relationships window of a hotel database, the line between tblGuest and tblBooking shows 1 at tblGuest and ∞ at tblBooking. What does this tell you?
options: One guest can have many bookings, and referential integrity is enforced
questions.explain: The ∞ (many) is on the booking side, and the symbols only appear when integrity is enforced.

questions.stem: A volunteer changes the Field Size of a Short Text field called Village from 30 to 4. The field contains 'Bartica'. After saving and accepting the warning, what is stored?
questions.explain: Values longer than the new size are truncated to the first four characters.

questions.stem: Shanice types a new member into the datasheet of tblMember, then clicks on the next row. She has not pressed Ctrl+S. Is the new record saved?
options: Only after the table is closed and reopened
Only if AutoSave is ticked in Excel
No, records are saved only with Ctrl+S
Yes, Access saves a record automatically when you move to another record
questions.explain: Access saves each record as soon as the focus leaves it.
