questions.stem: Ms. Croes, a graphic designer, now works from her home in Paradera for a company in Toronto, sending work over the Internet. What is this called?
questions.explain: Telecommuting means working from home or remotely using ICT. Benefits include no travel; drawbacks include isolation.

questions.stem: A guest house in Wheeland lets tourists book and pay for rooms online at any time of day. Which field of ICT use does this show?
questions.explain: Online booking systems let tourism businesses sell 24 hours a day to customers worldwide.

questions.stem: In the CIA triad, a hacker who secretly CHANGES students' marks in a school database is attacking which property?
questions.explain: Integrity means data is accurate and has not been altered without permission. Confidentiality is about who can see the data; availability is about being able to reach it.

questions.stem: At a hospital in Davy Hill, receptionists can view appointment times but cannot open medical histories, while doctors can see both. What security measure is this?
questions.explain: Access privileges limit what each user can see or change, protecting confidentiality.

questions.stem: Which is a DRAWBACK of using online learning platforms in Caribbean schools?
options: Students without reliable Internet or devices at home can fall behind (the digital divide).
Students can review lessons at any time.
Students can learn from experts in other countries.
questions.explain: The digital divide means unequal access to technology. The other options are benefits.

questions.stem: Ms. Carty's Form 4 chemistry handout shows the formula for water, H₂O, with the small 2 lowered below the line. Which formatting feature does this use?
questions.explain: Subscript places characters slightly below the line. Superscript raises them, as in 10² or 1st.

questions.stem: The name "Tera Kora" was spelt "Terra Kora" 14 times in a tourist brochure. Which feature fixes all of them fastest?
questions.explain: Find and Replace searches for text and replaces every instance in one step.

questions.stem: The Paramaribo Jubilee Library wants to send the same letter to 300 members, each with their own name and address. Which feature should it use?
questions.explain: Mail merge combines one main document with a data source to create personalised letters, labels or envelopes.

questions.stem: On a long FAQ page for the Roseau cruise terminal, clicking "Opening hours" jumps straight down to that part of the same page. What type of hyperlink is this?
options: A link to a downloadable file
A link to an e-mail address
A link to a bookmark (location) on the same page
questions.explain: Bookmark links jump to a named location in the same page or document.

questions.stem: Kezia is designing the home page for her school's Carnival troupe. Where is the navigation bar with links such as Home, Costumes and Contact usually placed so visitors can find it easily?
options: Hidden at the very bottom of only the home page
At the top of the page (or down the left side), in the same place on every page
In a different place on each page for variety
questions.explain: Consistent navigation, usually across the top or down the side, helps visitors move around the site easily.

questions.stem: Jamal's report on Hurricane Irma includes a wide table that does not fit across a normal page. What is the best page-layout change for that page?
options: Change that section to landscape orientation
questions.explain: Landscape orientation makes the page wider than it is tall, giving room for wide tables. A section break lets just that page change.

questions.stem: Three students are editing their group SBA document, and the teacher wants to see exactly what each person added or deleted. Which feature should they turn on?
questions.explain: Track Changes records insertions and deletions and shows who made them, so they can be accepted or rejected.

questions.stem: After adding two new sections to his report, Akeem notices the page numbers in his automatic table of contents are wrong. What should he do?
options: Delete the report and start again
Update the table of contents (update entire table)
Type the page numbers in by hand
questions.explain: An automatic table of contents can be updated to show new headings and correct page numbers.

questions.stem: The Jacmel Sailing Club runs a mail merge for its newsletter. What is the list of members' names and addresses (for example in a spreadsheet or table) called?
questions.explain: The data source holds the records. The primary document holds the standard text, and merge fields show where data is inserted.

questions.stem: Before designing a website for a Mandeville youth football league, why should the designer first identify the target audience?
options: Because the audience writes the HTML code
Because the audience decides the domain name
So that the content, language, colours and layout suit the people who will use it
So that the page loads without images
questions.explain: Purpose and audience guide every design choice, from reading level to colours and navigation.

questions.stem: On the contact page of a guest house website, clicking "Email us" opens a new message already addressed to bookings@seabreeze.bb. What kind of link is this?
questions.explain: A mailto link opens the visitor's e-mail program with the address filled in.

questions.stem: Kadeem copies a table from a website into his report, but it brings strange fonts and colours with it. Which paste option keeps only the words so the text matches his document?
options: Paste as text only (Keep Text Only)
questions.explain: Keep Text Only removes the source's formatting so the text takes on the formatting of the destination document.

questions.stem: A Form 5 student wants every main heading in his 20-page project to look the same AND to be able to create an automatic table of contents. What should he use?
options: Bold and size 16 typed by hand each time
Heading styles such as Heading 1 and Heading 2
questions.explain: Styles keep formatting consistent and allow the word processor to build and update a table of contents automatically.

questions.stem: A web page for a Carnival troupe uses bright yellow text on a white background. What is the main problem?
options: Search engines cannot index yellow text.
The page will not load on phones.
Poor contrast makes the text hard to read.
questions.explain: Good design needs strong contrast between text and background for readability and accessibility.

questions.stem: The Trinidad and Tobago Youth Council sends out an electronic sign-up form, but people keep typing over the questions. What should the designer do before sending it?
options: Protect (restrict editing of) the form so only the form fields can be filled in
Change the page to landscape orientation
questions.explain: Protecting a fillable form locks the fixed text so users can only complete the controls such as text boxes, check boxes and drop-down lists.

questions.stem: In a spreadsheet of Carnival troupe costume sales, what is the cell address of the cell in column C, row 7?
questions.explain: A cell address gives the column letter followed by the row number.

questions.stem: A teacher wants the highest mark in cells C2:C30. Which function should she use?
questions.explain: MAX returns the largest value in a range; MIN returns the smallest.

questions.stem: Which chart type best shows how St. Lucia’s monthly rainfall changes over a year?
questions.explain: Line graphs show trends over time.

questions.stem: Mr. Brooks's grade-book spreadsheet shows 74 in cell F3, but he wants to see the formula behind it. Where can he see it?
questions.explain: The formula bar displays the contents of the active cell, including the formula. The name box shows the cell address.

questions.stem: The treasurer of a youth cricket club wants to see what would happen to profit if the price of match tickets went up by $2. Which spreadsheet feature is she using?
questions.explain: Spreadsheets recalculate automatically, so changing one value shows the effect on all related formulae.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to show each student's position in class, with the highest average as 1st. Which function helps?
questions.explain: RANK returns the position of a number within a list of numbers.

questions.stem: In a sports-day spreadsheet, the "average points" cell for a house with no events entered yet shows #DIV/0!. What does this mean?
options: The function name is spelt wrongly.
A cell referred to has been deleted.
The column is too narrow to show the number.
The formula is trying to divide by zero or by an empty cell.
questions.explain: #DIV/0! means division by zero. #### means the column is too narrow; #NAME? means an unrecognised function name; #REF! means an invalid reference.

questions.topic: SO 5.5 · Replicating formulae and cell referencing
questions.stem: On a price list for a Young Street souvenir shop, the formula in C2 is =A2*B2. It is copied down to C3. What formula appears in C3?
questions.explain: Relative references change when copied: moving down one row adds 1 to each row number.

questions.stem: A spreadsheet of 500 cruise ship arrivals has headings in row 1. When scrolling down, the headings disappear. Which feature keeps row 1 visible?
questions.explain: Freeze Panes locks rows or columns so they stay on screen while scrolling.

questions.stem: A list of students is sorted by Form class, and within each form by surname alphabetically. What is the surname in this sort?
questions.explain: The primary key is sorted first (Form). The secondary key sorts records that have the same primary value.

questions.stem: On a column chart comparing sales of three snow cone flavours at Carnival Village, which element tells the reader which colour stands for which flavour?
questions.explain: The legend identifies each data series by colour or pattern.

questions.stem: In the budget workbook for Linden Youth Choir, a cell on the "Summary" sheet must show the total in cell D20 of the sheet named "January". Which formula is correct?
questions.explain: To refer to another sheet, type the sheet name, an exclamation mark, then the cell address.

questions.stem: In a maths club spreadsheet at Flamboyant Heights College, cells A1 = 10, A2 = 4 and A3 = 2. What does =(A1-A2)/A3+A3^2 give?
questions.explain: Brackets first: 10 - 4 = 6. Then the power: 2^2 = 4. Then division: 6 / 2 = 3. Finally 3 + 4 = 7.

questions.topic: SO 5.5 · Replicating formulae and cell referencing
questions.stem: A teacher names cell H1 "ExamWeight" and writes =C2*ExamWeight. What is the main benefit?
options: The formula is easier to read and the reference stays fixed when copied, like an absolute reference.
It makes the spreadsheet open faster.
It changes the number format to currency.
It prevents anyone from typing in H1.
questions.explain: Named ranges act as absolute references and make formulae more meaningful.

questions.stem: A Roseau bakery's workbook has identical sheets named Jan, Feb and Mar. Which formula adds cell B5 across all three sheets?
questions.explain: A 3-D reference (Jan:Mar!B5) refers to the same cell across a range of sheets.

questions.stem: In a table of students at Hummingbird Ridge High School, all the details about ONE student (ID, name, form, date of birth) make up what?
questions.explain: A record is one complete set of related data about one item or person. Each separate detail is a field.

questions.stem: Which data type is best for a field that stores whether a student has paid the school fee (Yes or No)?
questions.explain: Boolean fields store one of two values, such as Yes/No or True/False.

questions.stem: Which database object is used to search for and display records that meet certain criteria, such as all students in Form 5B?
questions.explain: A query selects records and fields that meet criteria.

questions.stem: The Anguilla Ferry Company stores passengers in one table, sailings in another and tickets in a third. In a database, what is a table?
options: A single piece of data such as a phone number
A collection of related records about one type of thing, arranged in rows and columns
questions.explain: Each table stores data about one entity, such as Students or Books.

questions.stem: The Antigua and Barbuda Turtle Watch group uses Microsoft Access to create, manage and query its nesting records. What is this kind of software called?
questions.explain: A DBMS lets users create tables, enter data, run queries and produce forms and reports.

questions.stem: Both StudentID and NationalIDNumber are unique for every student. StudentID is chosen as the primary key. What is NationalIDNumber?
questions.explain: Any field that could serve as the primary key is a candidate key; the one chosen becomes the primary key.

questions.stem: A validation rule for the field Age in a youth sports club table is "Between 10 And 18". What happens if a user types 25?
options: The entry is rejected and the validation text message is shown.
The value is changed to 18 automatically.
questions.explain: Validation rules reject data that breaks the rule; validation text explains the problem to the user.

questions.stem: A Basseterre insurance clerk needs all customers whose surname begins with "Ri", such as Richardson and Rivers. Which criterion should she use?
questions.explain: The wildcard * stands for any number of characters, so "Ri*" matches anything starting with Ri.

questions.stem: The receptionist at a dental clinic wants a query that asks "Enter the date" each time it runs and then shows appointments for that date. What type of query is this?
questions.explain: A parameter query prompts the user for the criterion each time it is run.

questions.stem: Which data type should be used for a field storing the price of a Carnival ticket, such as $45.00?
questions.explain: Currency stores money values accurately and allows calculations.

questions.stem: In Calabash Point Secondary's Exam Results table, neither StudentID nor SubjectCode is unique on its own, but together each pair appears once. What kind of key is StudentID + SubjectCode?
options: A candidate field with no use
questions.explain: A composite (compound) key uses two or more fields together to identify each record uniquely.

questions.stem: Students can join many clubs and each club has many students. How is this many-to-many relationship set up in a relational database?
options: By merging both tables into one big table
With a linking (junction) table such as Membership that holds StudentID and ClubID
By putting all club names in one field of the Students table
It cannot be stored in a database
questions.explain: A many-to-many relationship is split into two one-to-many relationships through a linking table.

questions.stem: A query must list Form 5 students who are EITHER in the Science club OR the Robotics club. How should the criteria be set?
options: Form = 5 And Club = "Science" And Club = "Robotics" on one row
Form = 5 on both criteria rows, with "Science" on one row and "Robotics" on the "Or" row for Club
questions.explain: Criteria on the same row are joined with AND; criteria on different rows are joined with OR. Form 5 must appear on both rows.

questions.stem: A small guest house keeps its bookings in one big spreadsheet. The guest's address is typed again for every stay, and some copies now have different spellings. What problem does this show?
questions.explain: Repeating the same data in many places (redundancy) means copies can disagree (inconsistency). A relational database stores each fact once.

questions.stem: The tourism office asks a team to "use computers to help cruise visitors". What is the FIRST step in solving this problem?
questions.explain: You must understand exactly what the problem is before proposing or coding a solution.

questions.stem: Shania writes an algorithm for booking seats on the Anguilla ferry. Which is a necessary property of any good algorithm?
options: It must have exactly ten steps.
It must be written in Python.
It has a finite number of steps and eventually stops.
questions.explain: A good algorithm is finite, precise, unambiguous, in logical order and terminates.

questions.stem: In a flowchart for a school canteen till, which symbol represents "Read price" or "Print total"?
questions.explain: Parallelograms show input and output.

questions.stem: The canteen at Frangipani Hill Academy wants a program to reduce long queues. After defining the problem, what should the team do next?
options: Propose and evaluate possible solutions, then choose the best one
Run trace tables on the final program
questions.explain: Problem-solving steps: define the problem, propose and evaluate solutions, choose the best, develop an algorithm, test and validate.

questions.topic: SO 7.4 · Variables, constants and data types
questions.stem: Which data type is best for a variable that stores a student's average mark, such as 72.5?
questions.explain: Real numbers have a decimal part. Integers are whole numbers only.

questions.stem: A guavaberry recipe algorithm says: "Add some sugar and stir for a while." Which property of a good algorithm is missing?
questions.explain: "Some" and "a while" are vague. Each step must be precise and unambiguous.

questions.stem: Which control structure should be used when the number of repetitions is KNOWN in advance, such as reading 30 students' marks?
questions.explain: A FOR loop is a counter-controlled loop used when the number of repetitions is fixed.

questions.topic: SO 7.7 · Testing algorithms and trace tables
questions.stem: Before typing her SBA program, Keisha completes a trace table by hand. What is a trace table used for?
options: Drawing the structure of a website
Tracking the values of variables step by step during a dry run to check an algorithm
questions.explain: A trace table records how each variable changes as you work through an algorithm by hand.

questions.topic: SO 7.7 · Testing algorithms and trace tables
questions.stem: A program to calculate the average age of students crashes when the user types "fifteen". Which kind of test data revealed this?
questions.explain: Erroneous data is the wrong type or outside the range; it checks that the program handles bad input.

questions.topic: SO 7.4 · Variables, constants and data types
questions.stem: Dante is naming variables for his SBA cricket-scores program. Which is a VALID variable name in most programming languages?
questions.explain: Identifiers usually cannot contain spaces or most symbols and cannot start with a digit.

questions.stem: In a loop that adds up The Valley bakery's sales for every day in a week, the statement total ← total + sales is used. What is "total"?
questions.explain: An accumulator collects a running total. A counter increases by a fixed amount, usually 1.

questions.topic: SO 7.7 · Testing algorithms and trace tables
questions.stem: A cricket scoring algorithm runs: total ← 0; FOR n ← 1 TO 3 DO total ← total + n ENDFOR; PRINT total. What is printed?
questions.explain: total becomes 0+1 = 1, then 1+2 = 3, then 3+3 = 6.

questions.stem: Your SBA asks for both an algorithm and a program for a cricket club's fees system. Which statement best describes the relationship between them?
options: An algorithm is the step-by-step plan; a program is that plan written in a programming language the computer can run.
An algorithm can only be written as a flowchart.
A program is written first; the algorithm is written afterwards.
questions.explain: The algorithm is the logic. A program implements that logic in a specific language. Algorithms can be shown as pseudocode, flowcharts or blocks.

questions.stem: The processor in a VirginTel router only understands binary 0s and 1s. Which type of language is written in this form and run directly?
questions.explain: Machine code is the lowest-level language (1GL). All other languages must be translated into it.

questions.topic: SO 8.5 · Sequence, selection and loops in code
questions.stem: In a Python check-in program for a Noord hotel, which line asks the guest for their name and stores it?
questions.explain: input() reads text from the keyboard; the = sign assigns it to the variable name.

questions.topic: SO 8.5 · Sequence, selection and loops in code
questions.stem: A countdown display for a cricket match must print the numbers 1 to 5. Which Python loop does this?
questions.explain: range(1, 6) gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The end value is not included.

questions.stem: An engineer programming a Lucayan Power & Water meter chip uses short codes such as ADD, MOV and JMP, translated into machine code one-to-one. What is this language?
questions.explain: Assembly uses mnemonics and is translated by an assembler.

questions.stem: A fuel-cost program for a Little Bay taxi firm crashes while running when it divides by a number of trips the user entered as 0. What kind of error is this?
questions.explain: Run-time errors occur while the program is executing, such as dividing by zero or opening a missing file.

questions.stem: A team in Cockburn Town is building an app for the Turks and Caicos Islands Ferry Service. Which shows the program implementation steps in the correct order?
options: Maintain → compile → execute → create source code
Create source code → translate/compile → link → execute → maintain
Link → create source code → maintain → execute
Execute → create source code → link → compile
questions.explain: Code is written, translated, linked with any library code, run and tested, and then maintained over time.

questions.topic: SO 8.5 · Sequence, selection and loops in code
questions.stem: A Barbados school teaches Pascal while Breadfruit Valley Secondary uses Python. Which Pascal statement matches the Python line total = price * qty ?
questions.explain: Pascal uses := for assignment and ends statements with a semicolon.

questions.topic: SO 8.5 · Sequence, selection and loops in code
questions.stem: A Python program counts passes in a Form 5 class: count = 0, then for m in [55, 40, 80, 49]: if m >= 50: count = count + 1, then print(count). What is printed?
questions.explain: Only 55 and 80 are 50 or more, so count increases twice.

questions.stem: The Santo Domingo software company RD Code gives customers a booklet explaining how to install the program and use each screen. What is this?
questions.explain: User documentation helps ordinary users. Technical documentation explains how the program works for programmers.

questions.stem: A grade-calculator algorithm for Caribbean schools is written in pseudocode, Python and Pascal. What stays the SAME across all three?
questions.explain: Syntax changes between languages, but the logic of the algorithm stays the same.

questions.stem: Before her SBA deadline, Aaliyah spends an hour debugging her program. What is the main purpose of debugging?
options: To find and fix errors in a program
To make the program run without a translator
questions.explain: Debugging means locating and correcting errors, using tools such as breakpoints, print statements and trace tables.

questions.topic: SO 8.5 · Sequence, selection and loops in code
questions.stem: The Belize Youth Carnival registration program accepts only ages from 13 to 19 inclusive. Which Python condition is correct?
questions.explain: Both conditions must be true, so use and, with >= and <= to include 13 and 19.

questions.topic: SO 8.5 · Sequence, selection and loops in code
questions.stem: A teacher in Antigua uses this Python code: biggest = marks[0], then for m in marks: if m > biggest: biggest = m. What does it do?
options: It finds the smallest value in the list marks.
It finds the largest value in the list marks.
It counts how many marks there are.
It sorts the list from highest to lowest.
questions.explain: biggest starts as the first item and is replaced whenever a larger value is found.

questions.stem: A weather station in Kingston uses the pseudocode "IF temp > 30 THEN PRINT 'Hot' ENDIF". Which Python version is correct?
questions.explain: Python uses lower-case if, a colon and an indented body. The Pascal version uses then/begin/end and writeln.
